# Compact adaptive degree-two scratch baseline

## Decision, 2026-10-06

The user requested the third representation arm and selected the **compact
adaptive** version previously used for IXI. The first two runs remain unchanged.
All three use the same 10,000 training, 1,952 validation and 13,071 test images,
original subject splits, seed, MRI preprocessing and 300-epoch scratch schedule.
No plants, pretrained weights, extra samples, or new exclusion filtering.

The third arm adds degree-two nodes to approximate each branch with straight
segments. It retains exactly the shared junction/termination/boundary endpoints
from the spline target caches. No skeleton re-extraction or node snapping is
performed. Original full generator guides remain uncertain references.

## Target construction

Reuse `optimal_keep_mask` and the prior adaptive physical-error profile:
`max(0.75 * local vessel radius, 0.1 mm)`, with a 95% mask-containment requirement
for shortcuts. Radius comes from the existing patch mask in physical units.
These SyntheticMRI guides are already smooth, so no additional smoothing is
applied. This derivation operates on the shared **cropped generator guides**;
it is not an exact rerun of IXI's full-volume skeleton extraction/smoothing.
That deliberate difference preserves the common endpoint topology and crop
boundary supervision of the current comparison.

A fixed 36-patch audit showed strict containment infeasible on three original
guides. Existing adjacent guide segments are therefore allowed even when mask
and guide disagree; all newly introduced shortcuts still require 95% containment.
These inherited violations are counted in the manifest. No guide is repaired,
branch deleted, or patch excluded because of mask disagreement. The revised
audit passed all 36 patches, added 240 degree-two nodes, found a maximum of 45
nodes and recorded five inherited segments below the containment threshold.

The optimal solver searches predecessor costs in ascending order, stopping at
the first feasible arc. This preserves its minimum-segment solution and historical
smallest-index tie break while reducing expensive chord checks. A targeted check
confirmed identical retained samples on straight/bending curves at two tolerances;
a separate check verified preservation of uncertain adjacent segments.
The new `preserve_adjacent` option defaults to false for all existing callers.

## Token budget and training

Keep 120 queries if **all training and validation targets fit**. If necessary,
raise the third arm to the smallest multiple of 32 covering their measured
maximum, with a safety guard at 512 queries. Test labels do not determine this
budget. Keep all test patches and report any test targets exceeding the budget.
Any increase is recorded explicitly and makes this an accuracy/capacity comparison,
not a comparison at equal token count. The two earlier 120-token arms are unchanged.
Same seed does not imply identical whole-model initialization if query dimensions
change. The immutable generated `adaptive/training-config.yaml` records the budget.

The architecture is the existing graph model with the edge existence head and
no spline head/loss. Other settings inherit the straight-edge scratch config:
batch 4; AdamW 7e-5, decay 1e-4; one warmup epoch; polynomial power 0.9;
no augmentation; validation every five epochs; shared five graph-loss weights
3/4/0.8/2/6. The inherited validation positive-edge cap is 40 per graph.
Best checkpoint selection uses the five graph losses, and final/latest is retained.
The same four validation examples show the degree-two graph predictions.

Native graph losses and node/edge metrics should not be compared directly with
junction-only targets, because there are different numbers of supervised nodes
and edges. Evaluate all arms against common endpoint/branch topology after
contracting degree-two chains, full-guide curve geometry, tortuosity and branch
coverage. Report compute and token budgets too.

## Execution and provenance

- `scripts/prepare_adaptive_comparison.py`: derive all targets on CPU, record
  node counts, inherited mask disagreements, shared manifest checksum and budget.
- `scripts/check_adaptive_comparison.py`: require exact split IDs, real batch,
  degree-two contraction agreement, capacity, model and loss construction.
- `cluster/jean_zay/prepare_adaptive_comparison.slurm`: full preparation and check.
- Training uses `COMPARISON_ARM=adaptive` and depends on successful preparation.
- Targets/config/provenance live in SCRATCH under
  `spline_learning/scratch_comparison_10k_300ep/adaptive`; MRI/masks are linked.
- Both jobs use the same verified package archive and protected interpreter.
  W&B compute logging is offline and must be synced from the login node.

Submission IDs will be recorded after submission. Full GT checks are still
pending until the preparation job completes; the GPU training cannot start first.

## Submissions

- CPU preparation and full preflight: **709919**.
- Compact adaptive scratch GPU training: **709924**, dependency `afterok:709919`.
- Stable implementation commit: `d0ccbef` (`representation`).
- Training parameters and split memberships match the first two arms; its actual
  query budget will be recorded after full preparation, before GPU training.
- Job provenance is saved alongside the original two IDs in
  `experiments/spline_learning/metadata/scratch-comparison-jobs.json`.

## Clarification about existing adaptive targets

The earlier IXI 300-epoch run (`ixi_q256_types_300ep_20260924`) already used
pre-extracted compact adaptive degree-two targets from
`IXI/vascular_patches/optimal_radius_0p75x_c095_vedo_original`. Those are IXI
images and cannot serve as targets for the current SyntheticMRI patch IDs.
The older SyntheticMRI 300-epoch run (`finetune_vessels_full_300ep`) used
`syntheticMRI/new_patches_boundary`, the native generator graphs with sparse
straight-edge targets; it did not use the radius-based adaptive representation.
An audit of the 91 available SyntheticMRI source graphs found 126 native
degree-two nodes, versus 181,034 terminal and 185,839 degree-three nodes.
Thus native degree-two nodes can exist, but these are not systematic adaptive
subdivision nodes used to capture branch geometry. The current CPU job reuses
existing SyntheticMRI guides and creates their compact adaptive targets.

## 2026-10-07: CPU preflight recovery

Target extraction completed successfully for all 25,023 patches in job 709919.
It produced 175,683 additional degree-two nodes; maximum nodes per patch is 67
(training/validation maximum 60). All targets fit the unchanged 120-query budget,
including test. There are 4,213 inherited guide segments below mask containment;
these were retained and counted under the documented uncertain-guide policy.

The job failed afterwards during `check_adaptive_comparison.py`: the cluster's
PyTorch CPU import attempted `cudaSetDevice` without a GPU. Its diagnostic
explicitly requires `IDR_DEBUG=WARN` for intended CPU-only execution. The
preparation script now sets that flag. Verification-only job **721618** reuses
the complete extracted targets; no graph regeneration is performed. Existing
training job **709924** now depends on `afterok:721618`. Verification outcome
and scheduler state will be recorded after the check completes.

Recovery verified: job **721618 COMPLETED (exit 0)**. Exact memberships, a real
validation batch, contraction back to shared endpoint topology, 120-query
capacity, model and criterion construction all passed on the CPU allocation.
The original adaptive training **709924 is RUNNING**, released automatically
by the corrected successful dependency. No targets were regenerated.

## Completed training and queued held-out evaluation

Training **709924 completed all 300 epochs**, exit 0, elapsed 13:51:03.
The validation-loss-selected checkpoint is epoch 25; the final checkpoint is
epoch 300. Test job **750145** evaluates both on the same 13,071 held-out IDs.
It saves native predictions/metrics and applies `shared-guides-v2` topology,
whole-vessel geometry and object-count scoring from saved predictions.
No test-set tuning or model/dataset changes are involved. Results will be
saved to `scratch_adaptive_degree2_10k_300ep/test/{best,final}` under the shared
SCRATCH run root, with W&B logging offline as for the other two arms.

# Eight-point Catmull–Rom training — 2026-10-09

## Question and protocol

Does supervising points that lie on the represented curve make learning easier
than supervising B-spline handles? The user requested a 300-epoch experiment
with the same control budget. This run starts **from scratch**, matching the
original 300-epoch B-spline comparison. It is separate from the pretrained,
image-informed connectivity pilots.

| Setting | Catmull–Rom run |
|---|---|
| Dataset | SyntheticMRI vessels only |
| Membership | Same 10,000 training, 1,952 validation, 13,071 test patches |
| Graph nodes | Existing junctions, terminations, boundary nodes; no added degree-2 nodes |
| Representation | Centripetal Catmull–Rom, alpha 0.5, physical millimetres |
| Budget | Eight points including graph endpoints; six internal points = 18 predicted scalars per 3D edge |
| Head | Same pair-token MLP and learned parameter count as the B-spline head |
| Initialization | Seed 364505; random weights; zero geometry residual gives a chord |
| Optimization | Whole network, 300 epochs, batch 4, 750,000 updates |
| AdamW | LR 7e-5, weight decay 1e-4, betas 0.9/0.999 |
| Schedule | 2,500 warmup updates; original polynomial schedule, power 0.9 |
| Loss | Original control-coordinate Smooth L1 in mm, beta 1; weight 1.4739989612791453 |
| Other weights | Boxes 3, class 4, cardinality 0.8, nodes 2, edges 6 |
| Validation | Every five epochs, same graph-loss checkpoint selection, four projections |
| Tracking | W&B offline, same comparison group; distinct Catmull–Rom run name/tags |
| Resources | One H100; 20-hour allocation; latest full-state checkpoint each epoch |

No image-evidence correction, loss ramp, pretraining, or new connectivity loss
is added to this experiment. Its purpose is to isolate the representation and
corresponding target construction under the original optimization settings.
The nominal geometry weight is preserved, not recalibrated to equalize
gradient magnitudes between representations.

## Implementation and targets

`models/catmull_rom.py` evaluates differentiable cubic Hermite segments with
centripetal knots computed from the predicted points. Reflected endpoint ghost
points and tangents are derived, not learned. A small distance floor handles
coincident points. The head copies predicted graph endpoints exactly into both
the controls and sampled curves. Model configuration selects `bspline` (the
backward-compatible default) or `catmull_rom`.

The existing full guide of each branch is resampled at eight equally spaced
physical arc-length positions. These are the supervised interpolation points;
64 curve samples are also cached for monitoring. This differs deliberately
from the B-spline target's endpoint-constrained least-squares handles. The
existing guide is an uncertain reference, not perfect anatomy. Interpolation
does not guarantee vessel-mask containment or correct connectivity.

Images, segmentations, graphs, splits, branch orientation, full guides, and
boundary-node rules are inherited. Only the new family-specific controls and
curves are generated. The dataset loader rejects mismatched curve families.
Original caches and checkpoints are not overwritten.

The unchanged control loss directly supervises internal point coordinates.
This tests easier target learning; it does not add a new image-containment or
topology objective. The earlier scratch-training collapse could still recur.

## Jobs and verification

- **805038**: CPU target preparation, with independent target cache.
- **805044**: after successful preparation, verify exact memberships,
  identical initial learned tensors/parameter counts and unchanged optimizer,
  then three real GPU updates, validation, projections, and inference.
- **805047**: 300-epoch training, starts only after **805044** succeeds.

All 13 focused local tests passed before submission. These cover agreement
with the existing NumPy viewer implementation, interpolation at knot positions,
direction reversal, finite gradients including coincident points, physical
metric handling, parameter counts, endpoint anchoring, target preservation,
and existing B-spline/inference behavior. Python compilation, shell syntax,
and `git diff --check` also passed. GPU verification is a queued prerequisite;
its submission is not evidence of success. The additional native/common metric
regression and inference tests also passed (eight tests in the second check).
Saved predictions now explicitly carry the curve family, and both metric paths
reconstruct the appropriate physical curve. Target preparation produced all
10,000 / 1,952 / 13,071 caches successfully; GPU verification remains pending.

## Files and next steps

Code repository: `Graph-Native-Betti-Matching-Representation`.

- Config: `configs/scratch_comparison_catmull_rom_300ep.yaml`.
- Preparation: `scripts/prepare_catmull_rom_targets.py` and
  `cluster/jean_zay/prepare_catmull_rom.slurm`.
- Training/check: `cluster/jean_zay/train_catmull_rom.slurm`.
- Compact provenance: `experiments/spline_learning/metadata/catmull-rom/`.
- Logs: `experiments/spline_learning/logs/catmull-*.{out,err}` and
  `scratch-catmull-rom-805047.{out,err}`.

Dataset cache:
`/lustre/fsn1/projects/rech/vnc/upz25mj/experiments/gnbm/spline_learning/scratch_comparison_10k_300ep/catmull_rom/`.

Run:
`/lustre/fsn1/projects/rech/vnc/upz25mj/experiments/gnbm/spline_learning/runs/scratch_catmull_rom_k8_10k_300ep/`.

After training, evaluate both the graph-loss-selected best checkpoint and the
fixed epoch-300 checkpoint with the same BN policy and representation-independent
full-guide geometry/topology protocol used for the three existing runs. Do not
rank representations by agreement with their own fitted curve targets alone.
No test evaluation is launched in this submission chain.

# Catmull–Rom versus B-spline: existing single cases

## Open the experiments

Download just these two HTML files and open them locally in a browser:

- [SyntheticMRI](../experiments/synthetic_mri_patch/results/synthetic_mri_patch.html)
- [IXI](../experiments/ixi_patch/results/ixi_patch.html)

They embed the plotting library, MRI volume, mask mesh, guides, fit data and
viewer code. No assets folder, server or network connection is required.

Select **Catmull–Rom: 8 interpolation points** or **10 interpolation points**.
The orange overlay shows the B-spline with the same point budget; switching
back to B-spline reverses the comparison. Pink points belong to the editable
family, orange points to the saved comparison. Click a pink point and edit its
X/Y/Z coordinates under **Edit edge parameters**. Catmull–Rom follows that
point exactly. **Restore fit** returns to the guide-point interpolation.
The ordinary branch/guide selectors, MRI slices, mask and graph nodes remain.

Static comparisons, on the original selected branch, are also available:
[SyntheticMRI image](../experiments/synthetic_mri_patch/results/catmull_rom_comparison.png)
and [IXI image](../experiments/ixi_patch/results/catmull_rom_comparison.png).

## Representation and parameter count

Catmull–Rom passes through its ordered interpolation points. An interior
B-spline control is a handle and usually does not lie on its curve.
These Catmull–Rom points are **edge geometry parameters**, not extra graph
junction/termination nodes or extra object tokens.

Use centripetal knots:

`t[i+1] = t[i] + ||P[i+1] - P[i]||^0.5`

Distances are measured in physical millimetres. Each interval is a cubic
Hermite curve; its tangents are computed from neighboring points and knot
intervals. Two reflected endpoint ghost points are derived, not learned.
Both graph endpoints stay fixed. There are no separately predicted tangents,
knots or alpha values in this simulation.

| Total points including endpoints | Free 2D geometry values | Free 3D geometry values |
|---|---:|---:|
| 8 | 12 | 18 |
| 10 | 16 | 24 |

This is the same coordinate budget as an 8/10-control B-spline with fixed
endpoints. The total coordinates including both endpoints are 16/20 in 2D
and 24/30 in 3D; endpoint coordinates are shared graph-node parameters.
The viewers also include 6, 12 and 16 interpolation points.

## Why it is worth testing

On-curve parameters are interpretable landmarks and may simplify geometric
supervision or editing. Catmull–Rom has continuous tangents but generally not
continuous curvature at its interpolation points. A cubic B-spline with simple
interior knots has continuous curvature. Interpolation can also reproduce
uncertain guide noise rather than smoothing it.

Centripetal Catmull–Rom avoids cusps and self-intersections **within an individual
segment** for distinct neighboring points. This does not guarantee global
non-intersection or vessel-mask containment. See
[Yuksel, Schaefer and Keyser, Parameterization and Applications of Catmull–Rom Curves](https://www.cemyuksel.com/research/catmullrom_param/).
Repeated neighboring points use a minimum knot increment of 1e-9 in this
double-precision prototype; the segment guarantee does not apply to that
degenerate case. A future learned implementation would need appropriate
spacing/order checks and numerical handling in its training precision.

## Construction and measured example results

The existing B-splines retain their endpoint-constrained least-squares fits.
Catmull–Rom interpolates equal arc-length samples from the selected uncertain
guide. Its positions are not optimized by least squares. The families share
endpoints and scalar budget but use different target-construction methods.
This is an illustrative capacity/editing comparison, not proof of the best
possible Catmull–Rom approximation and not a trained-model comparison.

Original-guide results: unweighted mean across all branches in each case.

| Case | Family / total points | Guide distance mm | Absolute tortuosity error | Mask support |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| IXI, 12 branches | B-spline / 8 | 0.03391 | 0.01058 | 99.214% |
| IXI, 12 branches | Catmull–Rom / 8 | 0.05460 | 0.01925 | 98.151% |
| IXI, 12 branches | B-spline / 10 | 0.02410 | 0.00896 | 99.735% |
| IXI, 12 branches | Catmull–Rom / 10 | 0.03065 | 0.01567 | 99.505% |
| SyntheticMRI, 19 branches | B-spline / 8 | 0.02295 | 0.00163 | 99.633% |
| SyntheticMRI, 19 branches | Catmull–Rom / 8 | 0.02459 | 0.00228 | 99.633% |
| SyntheticMRI, 19 branches | B-spline / 10 | 0.01529 | 0.00135 | 99.633% |
| SyntheticMRI, 19 branches | Catmull–Rom / 10 | 0.01449 | 0.00118 | 99.633% |

The existing alternate smoothed-guide fits are also available. Two cases do
not establish which representation learns better. This SyntheticMRI patch is
only mildly tortuous, so it is a weak stress test for severe bends. Neither
guide agreement nor image-derived mask support is independent anatomical
validation.

## Reproducibility and scope

The update reused the exact embedded cases: IXI `sample_000001_0007` and
SyntheticMRI `sample_000013_0002`. Volumes, masks, mesh, anchors, branch
guides and every non-Catmull numerical fit were verified unchanged. Existing
source paths in provenance describe the original extraction; they were not
re-read or newly verified during this update. No dataset, training target,
checkpoint or training configuration was changed.

- Shared Python evaluator: `DenseVesselGraph/scripts/catmull_rom.py`.
- Update command: `python scripts/update_single_patch_curve_viewers.py` from
  that repository, using the usual verified runtime.
- Existing shared experiment builder and viewer sources are in
  `experiments/ixi_patch/src/`; SyntheticMRI uses those same functions/templates.
- CSV measurements and construction notes are in each case's `results/`.
- Three interpolation/tangent/degeneracy regression checks passed.
- Python and browser-JavaScript evaluations agreed within 1.4e-15 mm on
  nonuniform and repeated-point fixtures. Simulated DOM interactions checked
  family switching, equal-budget overlay, point editing, restore and guide
  switching. These checks did not execute WebGL in a real browser on the cluster.
- Both static comparison figures were visually inspected.

If proceeding to learning, start with the existing eight-point budget and
training/validation split, and predefine shared topology/geometry evaluation.
Assess spacing, point order, guide noise sensitivity and supervision calibration
before interpreting any difference from B-spline learning.

Implementation committed as `f64280a` on the `representation` branch.

## Report 12

Source: `docs/research/spline_learning/controlled-unfreezing.md`

<!-- BEGIN SOURCE: docs/research/spline_learning/controlled-unfreezing.md -->

# Controlled unfreezing — 2026-10-09

## Decision and question

The user authorized controlled unfreezing and parallel diagnostics. Frozen
residual learning on 10k patches reached validation curve F1 0.68995 and
10.27% endpoint-neutral shape improvement over chords, with fixed graph
detection. [Previous results](residual-token-diagnostics.md) support proceeding
to the joint-optimization phase. Scratch training remains deferred.

Question: with a successful graph detector and geometry head, does geometry
supervision harm graph learning through shared tokens or predicted coordinates?
Three arms isolate these routes without altering forward geometry or matching:

| Task | Arm | Geometry gradients to tokens | Geometry gradients through predicted endpoints |
|---|---|---|---|
| 823645_0 | `graph_only` | Blocked | Blocked |
| 823645_1 | `tokens_only` | Allowed | Blocked |
| 823645_2 | `joint` | Allowed | Allowed |

In **every** arm the spline MLP trains. The graph-only arm detaches both its
inputs, so the detector receives exactly graph-only gradients while the head
can adapt to changing features. This avoids confounding the comparison with
a stale frozen geometry head. There is no geometry-to-edge classifier module
in this model, so head updates cannot change graph predictions directly.

## Fixed protocol

- Same full model weights from `frozen_followup_20261009/residual_continue/model.pt`
  (15k cumulative frozen-head updates), including identical learned geometry.
- Same 10,000 training patches, original 512 training monitoring cases, and
  ordered 128 validation cases. No test-set access. Single seed 364505.
- **5,000 new updates per arm**, batch four. Fresh AdamW in all arms; no
  source optimizer state reused because trainable parameter groups change.
- Unfreeze transformer encoder/decoder, image projection, query embeddings,
  and node/class/relation heads at constant **7e-6**. Train spline MLP at
  **7e-5**. Existing AdamW betas/epsilon and weight decay **1e-4** unchanged.
- CNN (`model.encoder`) stays frozen. `model.decoder.encoder` is the distinct
  transformer encoder and is trainable. All BN buffers remain fixed. Model
  stays in eval mode with autograd enabled, disabling dropout in every arm.
  Thus stochastic layers cannot explain arm differences.
- Existing graph losses/weights and residual-control objective retained;
  spline weight **1.4739989612791453**. No new loss, matcher, target, image
  feature module or architecture. Graph-loss training progress is held at
  epoch 1/progress 0 for these bounded paired runs (classification curricula
  are disabled in the source configuration). No LR warmup or decay.
- All forward loss values are identical for identical model states across
  arms. Only geometry backward routes differ. Detaching endpoint coordinates
  still allows token gradients to alter future node predictions indirectly.

The smaller detector LR and frozen CNN define a conservative first unfreezing
stage. These runs do not test full-network training or reproduce scratch
initialization. There is no automatic further unfreezing after completion.

## Measurements and verification

At 0/1k/5k updates, evaluate decoded node/edge/common geometry metrics,
same-endpoint chords, and GT-matched-positive spline geometry independently.
Retain raw guide, fitted-target, residual and endpoint-neutral errors, plus
the <=1 mm endpoint subset. Centerline guides remain imperfect references.
GT-matched assignment identities are saved per patch. Report the fraction of
GT nodes whose assigned query changed since initialization and the previous
geometry evaluation; this measures assignment changes on fixed cases, not
intrinsic random instability or necessarily a bad permutation.

Every 500 updates, record validation losses and fixed-probe CNN, transformer
memory, token and node-output image sensitivity. At training updates 1/1k/5k,
record graph versus weighted-spline gradient norms and cosine alignment for
transformer encoder/decoder, node-coordinate head, projection, queries and
relation head. These are sparse single-batch probes, not population estimates.
Zero geometry gradients to the detector/control and coordinate head/token-only
arm are asserted. Track frozen CNN parameters and all buffers by digest.

Initial decoded metrics must match the source checkpoint. Record initial model
hash, dataset/evaluation membership and actual batch-order hash for a final
cross-arm audit. Each task has an independent three-update GPU smoke followed
by a fresh full trial. CPU tests verified:

1. Equal spline forward values across all routes; intended token/endpoint
   gradients blocked or nonzero, while head gradients remain nonzero.
2. Graph-only control detector gradients exactly match graph-only total loss.
3. CNN parameters/BN buffers remain unchanged after an optimizer update.
4. Existing frozen-head and geometric checks still pass (seven tests total).

Offline W&B, validation projections, branch-level metrics, final model and
optimizer state are saved. No prior checkpoint or result is overwritten.

## Interpretation before results

- If joint harms graph F1/image sensitivity while graph-only remains healthy,
  geometry gradient coupling is implicated in this fine-tuning regime.
- If tokens-only preserves performance while joint degrades, the predicted-
  coordinate route is implicated. This includes the endpoint-conditioned MLP
  route; residual supervision already removes the direct chord error term.
- If both geometry-coupled arms degrade similarly, shared-token gradients are
  a stronger candidate. Encoder-memory sensitivity and gradient probes help
  localize the change; a small cosine alone is not proof of causation.
- If every arm degrades, examine graph continuation/LR/matching behavior
  before attributing the problem to splines.
- If joint improves geometry and connectivity without sensitivity loss, it
  supports staged pretrained joint training under this recipe. It still does
  not establish the initiating cause of the original 300-epoch collapse.

Stop for evidence review afterwards. Do not rank methods by total loss alone.

## Files and submission

Code repository: `Graph-Native-Betti-Matching-Representation`.

- `scripts/controlled_spline_unfreeze.py`: diagnostic-only gradient routing,
  unfreezing, optimizer groups, monitoring and assertions; reuses existing
  criterion, loaders, metrics and pilot visualization helpers.
- `scripts/frozen_spline_diagnostic.py`: optional assignment identity output;
  default behavior unchanged for previous experiments.
- `tests/test_controlled_spline_unfreeze.py`: two targeted gradient/state tests.
- `configs/spline_controlled_unfreeze.yaml`: common short protocol.
- `cluster/jean_zay/spline_controlled_unfreeze.slurm`: three independent tasks,
  one H100 each, one-hour ceiling; each is GPU-smoke gated.

Submitted **823645_0/1/2**, initially pending for priority. Actual concurrent
execution depends on scheduler availability. Syntax and seven CPU tests passed;
GPU checks and results are pending at submission.

Run root:
`/lustre/fsn1/projects/rech/vnc/upz25mj/experiments/gnbm/spline_learning/runs/controlled_unfreeze_20261009/`.
Logs: `experiments/spline_learning/logs/controlled-unfreeze-823645_<task>.{out,err}`.
Compact evidence: `experiments/spline_learning/metadata/controlled-unfreeze/`.

## Initial attempt stopped before trial updates

All tasks in 823645 exited 1 after roughly five minutes. All three separate
GPU smokes completed their three updates successfully. Each actual trial
stopped during initial evaluation on the same assertion: training common
curve F1 differed from the source run by **1.138147492e-6**, just above the
1e-6 diagnostic tolerance (0.7014372277 versus 0.7014383659). Validation curve
F1 was identical. This is not a trained unfreezing result or model collapse.

Saved-prediction comparison verified identical ordered sample IDs, query IDs
and edges on all 512/128 cases. Maximum normalized-coordinate/curve drift was
5.96e-7; maximum score drift was 5.61e-6. The three new arms produced identical
initial common metrics. These are tiny numerical differences in inference
that affect a thresholded curve metric; the particular kernel causing the
roundoff has not been isolated and is not necessary to resolve this failure.

Small fix: diagnostic aggregate-metric equality tolerance becomes 1e-5.
Metric distance thresholds, model weights, data, training and objectives are
unchanged. Replaying the saved initial common metrics reproduces three failures
under the old tolerance and passes under the new tolerance. Python/Slurm
syntax checks also passed. Runtime import warnings in the logs were not the
terminating error; the GPU smokes and full initial evaluations completed.

Resubmission uses the new output root `controlled_unfreeze_20261009_attempt2`
under the same runs directory. Original failed trials and successful smoke
artifacts are preserved. Each resubmitted task retains its GPU smoke gate.

Resubmitted as **824964_0/1/2** with the same arm ordering. Logs use `controlled-unfreeze-824964_<task>.{out,err}`. Results pending.

## Completed results: 824964_0/1/2

All completed 5,000 updates, exit 0:0, in **17m59s / 16m06s / 16m14s**.
Cross-arm audit verified identical initialized weights, initial metrics,
trainable parameters, optimizer settings, data/evaluation membership, and
actual batch-order hashes. CNN parameters and all buffers remained fixed.
The intended gradient blocking passed the sampled runtime assertions.

### Validation (128 cases; higher F1 is better)

| Arm | Node F1 | Edge F1 | Common branch F1 | Curve F1 | Own-chord curve F1 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Initial frozen residual model | 0.90753 | 0.85858 | 0.25497 | **0.68995** | 0.65540 |
| Graph-only detector + detached geometry head | **0.90753** | **0.87126** | **0.27387** | 0.68420 | 0.65214 |
| Joint tokens, endpoints detached | 0.90544 | 0.86380 | 0.27148 | 0.68857 | **0.65284** |
| Fully joint | 0.90536 | 0.86197 | 0.26897 | 0.68195 | 0.64801 |

Native node/edge F1 and the representation-independent common branch/curve
scores use different matching rules; do not interpret their numerical scales
interchangeably. All three improve edge/branch F1 over initialization, but none
improves validation curve F1 over the initial frozen residual model.

Training-subset curve F1 progresses from 0.70144 to 0.70945 / 0.71599 / 0.71129.
Thus there is some training improvement without a corresponding validation
curvature gain. There is no single model that wins all measured objectives.

### GT-matched validation geometry and representation diagnostics

| Arm | Raw guide error mm ↓ | Endpoint-neutral guide error mm ↓ | Neutral improvement over chord ↑ | GT-query assignments changed |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Initial | 0.89677 | **0.44987** | **10.27%** | — |
| Graph-only detector | 0.88313 | 0.45100 | 10.05% | 6.27% |
| Tokens, endpoints detached | **0.87929** | 0.45065 | 10.12% | 6.19% |
| Fully joint | 0.88406 | 0.45261 | 9.73% | 5.86% |

All 2,059 GT-positive validation branches remain evaluated. Raw geometry
improves slightly while endpoint-neutral shape is approximately unchanged or
slightly worse. Assignment changes are similar across arms and are lowest
for fully joint, so these data do not support a geometry-specific matching
instability explanation. A changed query assignment is not necessarily wrong.

Transformer-memory image sensitivity remains approximately **0.920** (initial
0.92030; finals 0.91775 / 0.91968 / 0.92019). No collapse is observed on the
fixed probes. The legacy `cnn_pair_mae` field measures **projected CNN features**
returned by the model, not raw frozen CNN activations; its small drift is
compatible with the trainable input projection and does not imply CNN updates.

Sparse gradient probes show weighted geometry/graph norm ratios around
0.11–0.20 in the transformer encoder and 0.14–0.21 in the decoder for coupled
arms. Encoder/decoder cosines are mostly near zero. In fully joint training,
the coordinate-head ratio is only about 0.027–0.071; its final cosine is
negative (~−0.48), but a single small-gradient probe cannot establish a cause.
These are three minibatch measurements, not population gradient estimates.

### Interpretation and decision

1. **Controlled pretrained unfreezing is stable here.** Neither geometry route
   reproduces the original catastrophic encoder collapse. This does not rule
   out a problem during scratch learning, with absolute targets, larger LR,
   train-mode stochastic layers or unfrozen CNN. Those conditions differ.
2. **There is no demonstrated benefit from geometry gradients into the detector
   in this short run.** The graph-only detector control has the best connectivity.
   Token-only coupling gives slightly better curve F1 than that control, but
   it does not beat the initial frozen model. Opening the endpoint route gives
   no measured advantage. Differences are single-seed validation observations,
   not established statistically significant rankings.
3. **Keep separate detector and geometry optimization as the conservative
   working route.** Train graph detection with its graph losses and adapt the
   residual head on detached detector features/endpoints. Keep the frozen
   residual checkpoint as the curvature reference; it still has the best
   validation curve F1. There is no basis yet for claiming a combined improvement
   in both connectivity and tortuosity or for restarting scratch training.

Next decision: verify this connectivity/geometry trade-off on a larger fixed
validation subset (and fixed-case visualizations) before committing to a
longer recipe; avoid selecting it from total loss alone. Do not use the test
set to keep choosing interventions. The initiating cause of the original
300-epoch failure remains unresolved. **No additional jobs were launched**
while reviewing these results.

Compact summaries, histories, gradient probes, comparison CSV and completion
audit are in `experiments/spline_learning/metadata/controlled-unfreeze/`.
Full artifacts remain under the `_attempt2` run root above. Original failed
attempts and all prior checkpoints are preserved.

## Report 13

Source: `docs/research/spline_learning/curve-informed-connectivity.md`

<!-- BEGIN SOURCE: docs/research/spline_learning/curve-informed-connectivity.md -->

# Connectivity informed by predicted vessel curves — 2026-10-08

## Objective and change

Recover connectivity and tortuous paths jointly. A frozen graph with curved
edges cannot repair missing or incorrect connections. The user authorized
implementing connectivity informed by image evidence along candidate curves.

The new optional path predicts a candidate eight-control spline **before edge
selection**, samples learned MRI features along that path, and adds a learned
correction to the original relation logits. Node positions, existence scores,
relation tokens, curve controls, and image features all remain trainable.
Both positive and negative candidate pairs receive edge classification loss.
Positive curves retain the existing fitted-target supervision.

### Implementation

- `models/curve_evidence.py`: a small full-resolution 3D MRI encoder (eight
  learned channels), raw MRI intensity, and an all-ones support channel.
  No target segmentation, centerline, or fitted controls enter this encoder.
- Differentiable trilinear sampling at 32 positions on each predicted spline.
  Coordinates follow voxel-index/axis-size DHW, with the required half-voxel
  adjustment for `grid_sample(align_corners=False)` and conversion to XYZ.
- A 1D convolution processes the sampled sequence; mean/max/min pooling and
  physical arc/chord lengths feed a two-logit residual scorer. Average both
  curve directions for undirected scoring. Initialize the final correction
  layer to zero, preserving original inference scores initially.
- One shared candidate-scoring function is used for matched training pairs,
  optional unmatched hard negatives, and inference. It uses canonical endpoint
  orientation and chunks pair computation at 256 candidates.
- Classification gradients pass through sampled coordinates into spline
  controls and predicted endpoints. Curves are not detached for edge scoring.
  Endpoint anchoring and existing relation/classification heads are retained.
- The feature tensor is carried through model predictions and never written
  into prediction JSON. Physical metric metadata comes from the existing crop
  affine convention; GT curve coordinates do not enter inference.

The default disabled path preserves existing models/checkpoint keys. The first
enabled implementation requires MRI input, Hungarian matching, and disabled
Betti losses; unsupported combinations fail validation rather than silently
scoring different graph heads. Existing masks/guides remain uncertain targets.

## Separate localization and connectivity errors

`scripts/diagnose_graph_connectivity.py` analyzes saved validation predictions:
role-agnostic, one-to-one raw-node matching in physical coordinates, then:

- Fraction of GT nodes recovered.
- Fraction of GT edges for which both endpoints are recovered.
- Connection precision/recall conditioned on those recovered endpoints.

Use 1 mm plus a diagnostic 2 mm sensitivity check. These diagnostics do not
replace the fixed shared-guides-v2 benchmark or tune its thresholds. They do
not contract predicted degree-2 chains and must not be reported as common
branch F1. A connection head cannot recover an endpoint removed by node
filtering; joint localization remains necessary.

## Paired pilot

Reuse the fixed 512 training / 128 validation patches and epoch-35 graph
checkpoint from the [staged pilot](spline-staged-learning.md). Both arms:

- Same architecture, initial tensors, sampling/batch order, 5,000 updates,
  fresh AdamW moments, original LR trajectory starting at update 87,500.
- Same spline weight ramp, 0 to 1.474 over 2,500 updates; all modules trainable.
- Same symmetric relation scoring in training and inference. This differs
  from the historical baseline's randomly oriented training pairs, so compare
  the new paired arms rather than attributing differences from old runs to
  image evidence alone.
- Same native/common validation metrics, same-endpoint chord comparison,
  node/link diagnostic, fixed projections, and offline W&B tracking.

Only the evidence contribution differs: **token_control scale 0** versus
**image_evidence scale 1**. Both contain the same initialized image module;
the control receives zero gradient through this module's scoring contribution.
This is a controlled pilot, not a claim that connectivity is already solved.
No full training or test evaluation is included in this pilot.

## Verification and files

Focused tests cover non-cubic voxel-center/axis alignment, fractional sampling,
zero-correction compatibility, undirected scoring, equality of training and
inference candidate scores, and edge-loss gradients into images, endpoints,
and spline controls. Existing spline and inference tests also run. A real
three-update GPU smoke exercises the complete model/loss/evaluation path.

Config: `configs/spline_curve_evidence_pilot.yaml`.
Slurm script: `cluster/jean_zay/spline_curve_evidence.slurm`.
Verification job: **778675**.
Outputs: `/lustre/fsn1/projects/rech/vnc/upz25mj/experiments/gnbm/spline_learning/runs/curve_evidence_pilot_20261008/`.
Compact evidence: `experiments/spline_learning/metadata/curve-evidence/`.
Documentation is in this folder; code and generated run outputs retain their
separate scopes. Prior checkpoints, targets, and results are preserved.

## Execution and verification

All 13 focused CPU tests passed. GPU verification job **778675** completed
successfully in 1m43s, including those tests and three actual optimizer updates
with initial/final validation and rendering. These establish implementation
execution, not an improvement in prediction quality.

Paired 5,000-update jobs submitted as **779095_0** (token control) and
**779095_1** (image evidence). Submission metadata records source SHA256 hashes.
No training completion wait is required; compare both finished summaries later.

The preceding staged pilot's raw-node diagnostic recovered 11.86% / 9.72% of
nodes within 1 mm (graph control / staged spline), leaving only 20 / 12 of 2,059
reference edges with both endpoints recovered. Conditional connection recall
was 65% / 75%, but on these very small eligible subsets. At 2 mm, endpoint
recoverability rises to 179 / 141 edges. Localization is therefore a major
limitation under these reference tolerances; edge classification alone cannot
resolve it. These are uncertain graph-reference diagnostics, not new benchmark
scores or evidence that every reference node is anatomically exact.

### Pretraining decision

Pretraining followed by joint spline fine-tuning remains a sensible strategy:
learn useful image/node features first, then adapt connectivity and curved
geometry with the whole network trainable and gradual geometry supervision.
The earlier successful fine-tuning supports feasibility; the recent staged
pilot avoided collapse but did not improve geometry meaningfully. The new
paired experiment tests image-informed connectivity on the same pretrained
initialization. It does not establish the best pretraining objective or a
superiority over scratch training at equal total compute. Any later comparison
must account for pretraining data exposure and total optimization budget.

## Report 14

<!-- BEGIN SOURCE: docs/research/spline_learning/frozen-spline-investigation.md -->

# B-spline failure: evidence review and frozen-detector diagnostic

Date: 2026-10-09. Scope: Phase 1 review and preparation/checking of **Phase 2
only**. Meaningful GPU training requires the user's approval. No Phase 3/4
training, new full run, matcher change, or new loss is authorized here.

## 1. What the evidence establishes

| Experiment | Initialization / population / budget | Finding and limit |
|---|---|---|
| Original four-patch V0 | Original straight detector or scratch; four patches from one subject; 500 updates, joint training | Pretrained fitted-curve error 0.1093 mm vs same-endpoint chord 0.4812; scratch 0.3811 vs 0.4803. Both learn some geometry. No disjoint validation. |
| Earlier full fine-tuning | Original straight checkpoint, 9,709 training / 1,952 validation patches, 50 epochs | Native test node/edge F1 0.8841/0.8157, matched decoded guide distance 0.6396 mm on 13,071 test patches. Spline success extends beyond four patches; this is not the later equal-data scratch comparison. |
| Paired 300-epoch scratch | 10,000 training / 1,952 validation / 13,071 test; identical seed, graph population and shared initialization | Final common curve F1: straight 0.23051, spline 0.00135, adaptive 0.24711. Spline training node loss remains poor, and outputs become almost input-independent. |
| BN diagnostic | Final checkpoints, eight validation patches, no optimization | Saved vs current-batch BN does not rescue spline outputs. CNN image sensitivity persists. Rules out the proposed inference-BN repair on these probes, not all possible normalization effects during optimization. |
| Attention diagnostic | Four validation patches; hooks plus disposable decoder-offset intervention | CNN difference 0.85446 becomes transformer memory difference 3.42e-8. Straight memory difference 0.87522. Resetting decoder offsets does not restore outputs. Localizes the trained failure; does not identify its initiating cause. |
| Initial gradients | One actual training batch, no update | Weighted spline/graph norm ratios: tokens 1.35, coordinates 7.49, image features 1.24; coordinate cosine +0.779. Scale imbalance demonstrated on one batch, not systematic gradient opposition. |
| Weight pilot | Scratch, 512 training / 128 validation, 5,000 updates; weights 1.474 vs 0.1474 | Both poor, both input-sensitive. Only two original full-data epochs including warmup; cannot settle the eventual collapse mechanism. |
| Staged pilot | Same-data straight checkpoint epoch 35, fresh AdamW; graph-only vs joint spline ramp; 5,000 updates | Both slightly regress. Spline common curve F1 0.15400 vs own chords 0.15448. No demonstrated geometry benefit. Graph was never frozen. |
| Curve-evidence pilot | Same epoch-35 checkpoint/subset, joint training, identical symmetric scoring; evidence off/on | Final native edge F1 0.46077/0.50654. Curve F1 0.15971/0.21339; own chords 0.15729/0.21172. Improved connectivity but small shape contribution. Not a head-only experiment. |

The evidence pilot's initialization, batch-order, schedule, and membership
hashes agree between arms. Its change to symmetric training relation scoring
was shared by both arms; comparisons against older pilots are not a pure
image-evidence ablation.

Relevant prior reports: [collapse](spline-collapse-diagnosis.md),
[four-patch results](spline-learning-results.md),
[weight pilot](spline-weight-pilot.md), [staged pilot](spline-staged-learning.md),
[curve evidence](curve-informed-connectivity.md),
[scratch comparison](scratch-comparison-results.md). Also reviewed the original
`representation-implementation.md` and the code repository's
`docs/research/vascular_graph_roadmap.md`: preserve Hungarian matching and
separate topology, geometry, and representation capacity.

### What the encoder probe actually measures

The diagnostic hooks receive attention `input_flatten` with layout `[batch,
spatial positions, channels]`. Successive encoder-attention inputs expose the
representation between encoder layers. Decoder cross-attention receives the
final encoder memory. Thus the quoted differences are correctly interpreted
as between-image differences, not attention-head or token-axis differences.
The encoder's near-constant output is real on the recorded probes. Poor
attention support also exists in the healthy straight model, so unsupported
sampling alone is not a spline-specific explanation. No repeat GPU BN or
attention experiment is needed to re-establish these answered questions.

## 2. Implementation audit and ranked hypotheses

The head predicts six residual 3D vectors from the two object tokens, two
shared relation tokens, physical endpoints, chord vector, and chord length.
There is no direct local image sampling in the original head. Image information
must arrive through detector tokens. The output is a fixed clamped cubic
B-spline with eight controls including the two predicted nodes.

For internal control k, in physical coordinates:

`C_pred[k] = (1-g[k])*x_pred_start + g[k]*x_pred_end + R_theta[k]`.

The current V0 loss is Smooth L1 of `C_pred[k] - C_GT[k]`, beta 1 mm, averaged
over six internal controls, coordinates, and matched positive branches. It is
**absolute-control supervision despite the residual output parameterization**.
Consequently it penalizes node-position errors as well as the residual shape.
Gradients reach endpoints directly through the chord and indirectly through
the MLP's endpoint inputs, and reach shared tokens/image features. With the
zero-initialized final MLP layer, residual-path input gradients initially
vanish while the chord-to-endpoint gradient remains active.

Hungarian assignment uses class probability and normalized-coordinate L1
distance only, under `no_grad`. Spline supervision neither changes the matching
cost nor differentiates through assignment. GT edge identities select query
pairs through the node assignment; predicted edge acceptance is not required
for positive-pair geometry training. Canonical physical orientation reverses
both target controls and target samples together. The cache/graph identities
and metric transform are checked when loading targets. No verified matching,
orientation, or units bug was found in this audit.

Ranked, falsifiable hypotheses:

1. **Endpoint/localization coupling during joint optimization.** Frozen graph
   learning should permit geometry improvement without detector drift if the
   features are sufficient. The one-batch gradient result motivates this; it
   does not prove it initiated the scratch collapse.
2. **Noisy or changing correspondence and endpoint error.** With frozen
   detection and evaluation mode, assignment must remain fixed. Compare all
   matched pairs with the subset whose two endpoints are within 1 mm, and
   report endpoint-neutral geometry separately. No matcher change is proposed.
3. **Insufficient transferable shape information in pair tokens/head.** If
   frozen geometry fails on training and validation despite fixed correspondences,
   this remains plausible. Failure could also reflect optimization budget or
   absolute-target compensation, so it is not proof of insufficient capacity.
4. **Generalization/initialization and data breadth.** Training improvement
   without disjoint-validation improvement supports this direction. The original
   successful detector saw 91,200 patches; the newer staged checkpoint saw
   10,000. These initializations are not interchangeable controls.

## 3. First diagnostic: freeze the successful original detector

Use the same source checkpoint as successful four-patch and full fine-tuning:

`/lustre/fsn1/projects/rech/vnc/upz25mj/experiments/gnbm/finetune_vessels_full_300ep/models/best_edge_f1_checkpoint.pt`.

Its recorded epoch is 300, iteration 855,000, with native validation edge F1
0.86321 on its original 19,200 validation patches. Those metrics do not replace
evaluation on the proposed frozen diagnostic population.

- Reuse the fixed **512 training / 128 validation** pilot membership (64/13
  subjects), eight controls, seed 364505, batch four. No test evaluation.
- Verify against pretraining membership: all 10,000 candidate training patches
  belong to original pretraining training; none of the 1,952 candidate validation
  patches or their subjects do. They belong to its validation population and
  were eligible for checkpoint selection. This is diagnostic validation,
  not a new unbiased test set.
- Freeze backbone, transformer, node and relation heads; only
  `spline_head.network.*` is trainable. Keep the detector in `eval()` throughout,
  including BN statistics and dropout. The frozen forward runs under `no_grad`.
- Keep **the existing absolute-control objective**, weight 1.474, beta 1 mm.
  Use fresh head-only AdamW at constant LR 7e-5, weight decay 1e-4, for
  **5,000 updates**. No warmup/ramp: this is an isolated head-learning diagnostic,
  not a matched causal comparison against the prior joint continuation.
  The inherited base configuration's 300-epoch field does not set this runner's
  stopping budget; the pilot config and provenance record 5,000 updates and the
  constant head-only schedule explicitly.
- Record loss/sensitivity every 500 updates; evaluate both splits at updates
  0, 1,000, and 5,000. Retain fixed projections and offline W&B records.
- Assert unchanged detector **parameters and buffers**, and unchanged
  per-sample Hungarian assignment hashes. Verify finite head gradients and
  absent detector gradients. Ordinary node/edge losses do not update anything.

Existing experiments do not already answer this experiment: all earlier
successful and staged spline training updated the detector jointly.

### Separate measurements

**GT-matched geometry:** every assigned GT-positive pair, irrespective of
classification or decoded connectivity. Report branch counts, paired curve vs
same-predicted-endpoint-chord errors against the fitted curve and original
full guide, relative improvement `(chord_error - curve_error)/chord_error`,
fraction of branches improved, and residual-control error. Aggregate errors
per branch, not per batch. Retain per-branch results and the prespecified
both-endpoints-within-1-mm subset. Empty subsets remain explicitly empty.

**Endpoint-neutral diagnostic:** evaluate the predicted deviation from its
chord after adding it to the GT chord. GT positions never enter the head input
or training objective. This removes a fixed localization contribution for
interpretation; it is not a deployable prediction or a benchmark replacement.

**Full decoded graph:** native node/edge F1 and common guide topology/geometry,
plus the exact same decoded nodes/edges represented by straight chords.
Node/edge detection should remain unchanged. This measures the effect of
geometry on a fixed predicted graph and cannot claim recovered missing links.

## 4. Residual formulation: assessment, not implementation of Phase 3

For this clamped B-spline, use the **Greville abscissae**:
`g = [0, 1/15, 1/5, 2/5, 3/5, 4/5, 14/15, 1]` for eight controls.
They satisfy `basis(t) @ g = t`, so chord control positions produce a linearly
parameterized chord. Equal control-index fractions would not.

The proposed `R_GT = C_GT - chord_GT(g)` is mathematically valid when computed
in the same physical coordinates and pair orientation. Compare to the
physical residual produced by the MLP; replacing the absolute objective would
remove its direct chord-localization term. These vectors describe deviation
from a chord, including tangential parameterization effects; they are not an
intrinsic curvature scalar.

Residual supervision alone leaves the MLP-input route from endpoint coordinates
to residuals. Detaching endpoint inputs as well would remove that route while
ordinary node losses could still train localization. Shared-token gradients
would remain and could still affect the transformer. These are distinct
interventions. Do not add both residual and absolute losses, or implement
detachment now; decide after the frozen diagnostic.

## 5. Decision rules and limits

| Result | Interpretation / next discussion |
|---|---|
| Training and validation improve over identical-endpoint chords | Frozen features and head support geometry learning. Joint optimization becomes a stronger target, but the original scratch-collapse cause remains unproven. Discuss one residual-loss or controlled unfreezing comparison. |
| Training improves, validation does not | Investigate transfer/generalization and guide/shape variation before scaling. |
| Endpoint-neutral improves but raw geometry barely changes | Fixed endpoint error limits deployed geometry; keep localization separate in conclusions. |
| Neither training nor validation improves | Check whether fixed endpoints/assignments dominate and whether the chosen budget learned anything; then isolate head/features/targets. Do not conclude B-splines are infeasible. |
| Node/edge predictions, BN buffers, or assignment hashes change | The freeze protocol failed; invalidate the experiment and fix it before interpretation. |

One checkpoint, seed, and finite budget cannot establish a universal mechanism.
The stronger original checkpoint makes this a learnability diagnostic, not an
equal-data demonstration that freezing causes success. If unfreezing is later
justified, use a graph-only continuation from the **same** checkpoint and
conditions. Stop here for approval and interpretation; no automatic Phase 3/4.

## Implementation and reproducible command

In `Graph-Native-Betti-Matching-Representation`:

- `scripts/train_spline_weight_pilot.py`: optional frozen path, training-split
  evaluation, provenance, fixed-state/assignment checks; existing pilots default
  to their original behavior.
- `scripts/frozen_spline_diagnostic.py`: head-only update and separate matched
  geometry measurements using the existing matcher, head, and loss.
- `configs/spline_frozen_head_pilot.yaml`: checkpoint, split, and update budget.
- `cluster/jean_zay/spline_frozen_head.slurm`: three-update smoke, then fresh
  initialization for the bounded trial, one H100 with a 30-minute allocation.
- `tests/test_frozen_spline_diagnostic.py`: CPU freeze/BN/gradient checks, paired
  chord measurements, Greville identity and endpoint-coupling check.

Prepared command, **not submitted**:

```bash
sbatch --output=experiments/spline_learning/logs/frozen-head-%j.out \
       --error=experiments/spline_learning/logs/frozen-head-%j.err \
       cluster/jean_zay/spline_frozen_head.slurm
```

Output root:
`/lustre/fsn1/projects/rech/vnc/upz25mj/experiments/gnbm/spline_learning/runs/frozen_head_pilot_20261009/`.
Smoke and actual run use separate directories and refuse to overwrite existing
results. Compact CPU verification is in `experiments/spline_learning/metadata/frozen-head/`.

## Local verification result

Nine focused CPU tests passed, including existing spline checks. The final three diagnostic tests also passed after the fixture refinement. Loading the real checkpoint on CPU succeeded with only the expected missing new spline tensors: exactly 1,540,098 MLP parameters are trainable, and all 89 BN layers remain in evaluation mode. Syntax and whitespace checks passed. These are correctness checks, not evidence of real-data geometry learning; GPU smoke and the 5,000-update trial have not been submitted.

## Authorized submission

The user subsequently authorized the prepared diagnostic. Submitted Slurm **812623**: one H100, 30-minute limit. It runs the three-update GPU smoke first, then restarts from the original checkpoint for the 5,000-update trial only if the smoke succeeds. Source hashes match the reviewed preparation. No completed GPU result is claimed at submission; stop after this Phase 2 experiment for interpretation. Logs: `experiments/spline_learning/logs/frozen-head-812623.{out,err}`.

## Startup correction and resubmission

Job 812623 failed after 1m02s, before any training updates: the generic evaluation loader intentionally accepts only val/test, but the new diagnostic requested train. The diagnostic now builds an unshuffled loader over a separate view of the existing selected training dataset; membership and augmentation settings are unchanged. At the user’s request, skipped a separate real-sample test and resubmitted directly after syntax/whitespace checks as **813146**. The in-job GPU smoke still gates the 5,000-update trial. New output root has suffix `_attempt2`; failed artifacts are preserved.

## Completed diagnostic — job 813146

Completed successfully in **14m17s**, including the smoke and 5,000-update
trial. The actual trial took 717s including monitoring. The saved export audit
confirmed exactly identical node coordinates, node/edge scores, edges, query
identities, and sample order before/after on all 512 training and 128 validation
patches. Detector parameter/buffer and Hungarian-assignment checks passed.
Input sensitivity also remained exactly unchanged. No new test-set evaluation.

| Metric (final; chord → spline) | Training | Disjoint validation |
|---|---:|---:|
| GT-matched branch guide distance, mm ↓ | 0.96148 → 0.57203 | 0.95368 → 1.03307 |
| GT-matched fitted-curve distance, mm ↓ | 1.25866 → 0.71961 | 1.24956 → 1.40366 |
| Full decoded common curve F1 ↑ | 0.64812 → 0.83403 | 0.65540 → 0.58567 |
| Endpoint-neutral matched guide distance, mm ↓ | 0.51414 → 0.55563 | 0.50138 → 0.70664 |
| Native node F1 (unchanged) | 0.90845 | 0.90753 |
| Native edge F1 (unchanged) | 0.86265 | 0.85858 |

GT-matched distances cover 8,454 training / 2,059 validation branches; decoded
curve F1 evaluates full predictions and is a separate measurement. Relative
matched-guide improvement is **40.5% training**, **−8.3% validation**. For the
localized subset (both endpoints within 1 mm), guide improvement is 41.2% on
2,665 training branches and −14.4% on 619 validation branches. Thus validation
failure is not confined to the worst localized endpoints.

At update 1,000, validation curve F1 improved slightly to 0.66316 before later
regressing. Validation control loss reached 0.30996 there (initial 0.31400),
then rose to 0.37477 at update 5,000 while training loss continued falling.
This is evidence of overfitting at the final budget, not proof that no early
validation benefit exists. No intermediate checkpoint was retained or selected
as a new benchmark model.

### Interpretation and next decision

Freezing works as designed and the head can learn training geometry. However,
it does **not** by itself yield transferable curvature prediction. The original
scratch-collapse cause remains unresolved; joint detector degradation cannot
explain this experiment's validation failure because the detector is unchanged.

Absolute-control learning appears to include compensation for fixed endpoint
errors: residual-control error increases (training 0.56750 → 0.96709 mm;
validation 0.55166 → 1.00938 mm), and the all-pair endpoint-neutral diagnostic
worsens despite large raw training gains. This supports a localization/shape
confounding hypothesis, not a complete causal attribution. Some genuine shape
learning is present in the localized training subset: endpoint-neutral guide
error improves 20.9%; its validation counterpart worsens 33.1%.

The smallest next discriminative experiment is a **frozen-detector residual-
control objective replacing the absolute-control objective**, with the same
checkpoint, seed, samples, head initialization, optimizer, and budget. The
existing completed run supplies its absolute-loss control. All endpoints are
already detached by freezing, so no separate detachment intervention is needed
for that experiment. Compare residual/endpoint-neutral and raw guide geometry,
including the same early monitoring points. Do not unfreeze, add an image
module, or launch a long run on these results. Await discussion/approval before
implementing or launching Phase 3.

Compact verified summary, history, comparison CSV, and completion audit:
`experiments/spline_learning/metadata/frozen-head/`. Full output remains in the
`frozen_head_pilot_20261009_attempt2/absolute_controls/` run directory.

## Authorized parallel follow-up

The user authorized next tests and requested multiple diagnostics together. Submitted **815195_0/1/2**, completing a frozen 2×2 absolute/residual × full-token/endpoint-only comparison using job 813146 as the existing fourth arm. No unfreezing or long training is included. [Protocol and interpretation](residual-token-diagnostics.md).

# Full validation comparison — 2026-10-09

The user authorized validating the observed connectivity/geometry trade-off
before further training. Evaluate three fixed checkpoints on **all 1,952
validation patches** from the original comparison manifest:

| Arm | Checkpoint | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `frozen_residual` | Frozen residual head after 15k updates, 817904_0 | Best pilot curve F1 |
| `detached_head` | Graph-only detector gradients + adapting detached head, 824964_0 | Best pilot connectivity |
| `endpoints_detached` | Joint token gradients, endpoint path detached, 824964_1 | Possible geometry/connectivity compromise |

No checkpoint selection within this evaluation, training, optimizer updates,
BN recalibration, threshold changes, or test-set scoring. All models run in
eval mode with gradients disabled; the full model state is hashed before and
after. Source checkpoint configurations supply the common evaluation protocol.
Initialization is strict; the same ordered validation IDs are asserted for all
three arms. Explicit IDs bypass the earlier diagnostic cap of 128.

## Measures

- Native node/edge F1 and existing native metrics.
- Common anchor/branch/whole-curve metrics, Betti errors, object counts and
  count errors, using the existing representation-independent guide protocol.
- Each decoded graph's own same-endpoint straight chords, to separate curve
  benefit from differing detection/connectivity.
- GT-matched positive-pair raw guide, fitted-target, residual and endpoint-neutral
  geometry; keep these distinct from metrics on full decoded predictions.
- Decoded matched-branch tortuosity error. Guides remain uncertain references.

The primary result is the full validation aggregate. It includes the 128 cases
used for diagnostics, and these subjects were also used for earlier checkpoint
selection. This is broader model-selection evidence, not an unbiased final test
or a new seed. Keep the separate test set untouched until the recipe is fixed.

## Fixed-case visualizations

Select six subjects using seed 364505, then one validation patch per selected
subject, without examining model predictions. Use exactly those six IDs in all
arms. For each case, export the existing three orthogonal MRI/mask projections
with guide nodes/paths above predicted nodes/curves. Also export identical-node
straight-chord versions. The gallery shows models side by side with a case
selector and curves/chords toggle. Projected crossings are not necessarily
junctions; these images do not replace 3D topological evaluation.

When all evaluations complete, the last task verifies paired protocols and
automatically writes:

- `comparison.csv`: full compact metrics for all three checkpoints.
- `comparison.md`: readable main comparison table.
- `comparison.json`: table, evaluation IDs and paired-protocol audit.
- **`comparison.html`**: self-contained offline gallery with embedded images.
  Download this file alone and open it locally; no server or extra assets.

Each arm retains full predictions, native/common summaries, per-case metrics,
GT-matched per-branch errors and PNGs. W&B stays offline, storing metrics and
the selected validation projections. Large outputs remain outside `projects`.

## Execution

Config: `configs/spline_full_validation.yaml` in
`Graph-Native-Betti-Matching-Representation`.
Runner: `scripts/evaluate_spline_validation.py`, reusing existing evaluation,
geometry, plotting and tracking code. Slurm:
`cluster/jean_zay/spline_full_validation.slurm`, three independently scheduled
H100 tasks, one-hour ceiling each. Each task first evaluates two fixed cases
in a separate smoke directory, then restarts the full evaluation from its
checkpoint. No original artifact is overwritten.

Output root:
`/lustre/fsn1/projects/rech/vnc/upz25mj/experiments/gnbm/spline_learning/runs/full_validation_20261009/`.
Subdirectories: each arm and its `smoke-` counterpart. The four comparison
files above are generated at this root once all three summaries exist.

After completion, inspect paired tables and the fixed-case gallery to decide
whether a longer pretrained continuation is justified. No automatic training
is attached to these jobs.

## Submission

Submitted **826121_0/1/2** for frozen residual / detached head / endpoints detached respectively. All checkpoints load, configurations validate, evaluation/model/input/root settings agree, and the exact 1,952 validation IDs are disjoint from train/test IDs. Python and Slurm syntax checks passed. GPU smoke and full evaluations are queued. Logs: `experiments/spline_learning/logs/full-validation-826121_<task>.{out,err}`. Compact evidence: `experiments/spline_learning/metadata/full-validation/submission.json`.

Selected cases: `sample_000014_0919`, `sample_000016_0843`, `sample_000041_0761`, `sample_000070_0552`, `sample_000075_0287`, `sample_000092_0813`. No result claimed at submission.

## Completed results

All jobs completed with exit 0:0: **826121_0 9m50s**, **_1 9m47s**,
**_2 10m20s**. Each scored exactly 1,952 validation patches and 31,934
GT-matched positive branches. Ordered IDs, protocols and visual cases agree;
all model states stayed unchanged, with no BN recalibration or test scoring.

### Decoded graph metrics (F1 higher is better)

| Model | Node F1 | Edge F1 | Common branch F1 | Curve F1 | Own-chord curve F1 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Frozen residual | **0.91041** | 0.86363 | 0.27625 | **0.68441** | 0.64702 |
| Graph-only detector + detached head | 0.90910 | **0.87198** | 0.29183 | 0.67955 | 0.64762 |
| Joint tokens, endpoints detached | 0.90889 | 0.87096 | **0.29236** | 0.68296 | **0.64766** |

Native edge F1 and common branch F1 have different matching rules and should
not be read as interchangeable measures. Splines improve whole-curve F1 over
their own chords for every model. The frozen model has the largest such gain
(0.03739), versus 0.03194/detached and 0.03530/endpoints-detached.

### Geometry and topology (errors lower is better)

| Model | GT-matched raw guide mm | Endpoint-neutral guide mm | Neutral gain vs chord | Betti-0 count error | Betti-1 count error | Anchor count error |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Frozen residual | 0.89484 | 0.46094 | 10.48% | **0.56301** | 1.65984 | 2.48002 |
| Detached head | 0.89051 | 0.46107 | 10.46% | 0.83914 | **1.00512** | 1.94723 |
| Endpoints detached | **0.88814** | **0.45990** | **10.69%** | 0.84990 | 1.06096 | **1.92828** |

Raw guide errors improve 6.67% / 6.69% / 6.90% over each model's own chords.
Decoded topology-matched branch tortuosity error is 0.02547 / 0.02413 / 0.02534.
Mean predicted node counts are 21.32 / 22.20 / 22.23; predicted common branch
counts 16.07 / 15.85 / 15.93 against mean reference 16.36. Count agreement
alone does not establish correct connectivity. Betti-0 absolute count error
worsens after unfreezing even as edge/branch F1 and Betti-1 error improve:
topology gains are mixed. Absolute component-count error alone does not tell
whether the model has too many or too few components.

### Visual inspection and gallery

Inspected source projections for `sample_000014_0919` across all three models,
and `sample_000075_0287` for frozen/endpoints-detached curves and the latter's
chords. Predictions broadly localize many vessel segments but retain missed
connections, spurious structures and notably under-recovered bends. On these
cases, predicted curves often remain close to chords; numerical gains should
not be presented as solved tortuosity reconstruction. This is a limited
qualitative inspection, not a visual review of all validation cases, and 2D
projected crossings cannot certify 3D connectivity.

All 36 embedded PNGs (six cases × three models × curves/chords) were checked
against their source files. No browser was available for an interactive
rendering test. The HTML has no external image or script dependency.

**Download only this file and open it in your local browser:**

`/lustre/fsn1/projects/rech/vnc/upz25mj/experiments/gnbm/spline_learning/runs/full_validation_20261009/comparison.html`

Size: **9,808,153 bytes** (~9.8 MB). Tables are alongside it as
`comparison.csv`, `comparison.md`, and `comparison.json`.

### Decision and limits

- Full validation confirms the pilot trade-off, with a smaller difference
  between the two unfrozen alternatives. Endpoints-detached is the tentative
  compromise: nearly the detached model's edge F1, slightly better common
  branch F1 and guide geometry, and curve F1 closer to the frozen model.
- It is **not an overall winner**: frozen remains best on curve F1, node F1
  and component-count error; fully detached has the best edge F1 and cycle
  count error. Endpoint-neutral shape differences between these candidates
  are small (~0.001 mm). No statistical superiority is established.
- Keep all three fixed checkpoints. The residual representation provides
  modest transferable shape benefit, but unfreezing has not clearly increased
  curvature learning, and visual underfitting remains. Before a long run,
  discuss whether to prioritize topology or improving geometry beyond the
  current token-conditioned head. These results do not justify claiming the
  original scratch-training failure is explained.

No new training was submitted during this results review. Compact summaries,
tables and completion/visualization audit are saved in the code repository at
`experiments/spline_learning/metadata/full-validation/`. Larger artifacts and
offline W&B data remain in the run root outside `projects`.

Dataset-context follow-up (2026-10-10): the user highlighted that SyntheticMRI
has limited bends. A fitted-target audit confirms this, so small average gains
and predictions close to chords alone cannot establish curvature-learning
failure. See the [local-feature experiment and curvature audit](local-geometry-diagnostic.md)
for the corrected interpretation and IXI follow-up constraints.
