<!-- BEGIN SOURCE: docs/research/spline_learning/ixi_patch.md -->

# IXI patch: curve-valued branches with uncertain centerlines

Open [the interactive experiment](../experiments/ixi_patch/results/ixi_patch.html). This HTML is **self-contained**: download this one file and open it locally, with no assets folder or internet connection required. The expanded file is approximately 30 MiB because it embeds Plotly, image data, the vessel mesh, and all fitted curves.

Other outputs: [visual overview](../experiments/ixi_patch/results/overview.png), [per-branch metrics](../experiments/ixi_patch/results/metrics.csv), [source provenance and hashes](../experiments/ixi_patch/results/provenance.json).

## What was selected

- IXI033-HH-1259-MRA_IXI-HH, validation patch `sample_000001_0007`.
- Selection before fitting: first active validation patch from patient `000001` with 35–70 adaptive graph nodes and more than 1,500 foreground mask voxels. This is one illustrative patch, not a representative dataset sample.
- Native crop: start `(0, 107, 36)`, size `64 × 64 × 64`; source voxel spacing approximately `(0.46875, 0.46875, 0.8)` mm.
- The patch files have identity affines. Physical coordinates therefore come from the **source MRI affine and crop origin**, not the patch header.
- The existing dense graph was clipped with the project's voxel-cell crop convention, then degree-two chains were contracted while retaining their complete ordered paths. There are no rings in this patch.

The patch contains **272 dense nodes / 270 edges**, reduced to **14 anchors / 12 branches**, preserving two connected components and zero cycles. Three anchors are crop-boundary intersections and are explicitly marked in purple. The existing adaptive training graph has 45 nodes.

## Centerlines are guides, not ground truth

The study fits the available extracted centerlines to assess representation capacity. It does **not** establish whether those paths are anatomically correct. Fitting residuals measure agreement with extraction, and tortuosity differences measure agreement with its morphology.

The viewer includes the MRI volume as a movable slice and the existing vessel segmentation as a translucent surface. Mask support is the fraction of samples along the fitted curve inside that segmentation. The mask also informed graph extraction, so this is **not an independent anatomical validation**. Missing vessels, incorrect junctions, or biased centerlines can remain wrong even with excellent residual and mask support.

The alternate fitting guide applies five Laplacian smoothing iterations with weight 0.35. Endpoints are fixed, and an interior point moves only when its new position is inside the existing mask. This is an explicitly chosen sensitivity check, not a corrected annotation. Both extracted and smoothed fits remain available.

## Fitting and metrics

All representations share the same branch endpoints and connectivity:

| Representation | Geometry values per 3D branch, excluding graph anchors |
| --- | ---: |
| Straight chord | 0 |
| Single cubic Bézier | 6 |
| Cubic B-spline with `n` total controls | `3(n − 2)` |
| `s` piecewise cubic Bézier segments | `3(3s − 1)` |
| Sine series with `K` modes | `3K` |
| Endpoint-constrained Chebyshev basis with `K` terms | `3K` |

B-spline control counts are 6, 8, 10, 12, and 16; piecewise segment counts are 2, 3, and 4. The single cubic is equivalent to a clamped four-control cubic B-spline.

The added sine and Chebyshev families each use 2, 4, 6, and 8 coefficient vectors. There are now 18 variants and 432 fit records (12 branches × 2 guides × 18 variants). All 240 original fit records were checked and are unchanged.

## Additional function families

The sine representation adds endpoint-vanishing basis functions to the endpoint chord:

\[
\Gamma(t)=(1-t)A+tB+\sum_{k=1}^{K}a_k\sin(k\pi t).
\]

Each `a_k` is a 3D coefficient vector in mm. Low modes describe broad bends; higher modes permit finer oscillations. Changing a coefficient affects the whole branch. These coefficients are not spatial control points, so the viewer edits their X/Y/Z components without drawing them as pink points.

The polynomial alternative uses a Chebyshev basis with an endpoint constraint:

\[
\Gamma(t)=(1-t)A+tB+t(1-t)\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}a_kT_k(2t-1).
\]

Here `T_0(x)=1`, `T_1(x)=x`, and `T_k(x)=2xT_{k-1}(x)-T_{k-2}(x)`. This spans polynomials of degree up to `K+1` with fixed endpoints. Two terms give exactly the same curve space as the single cubic Bézier; their fitted curves were checked for numerical equality. Higher degrees add flexibility, with potential oscillations. The Chebyshev basis itself supplies no smoothing penalty.

Both new families use the same 257 guide samples and endpoint-constrained least-squares objective as the single Bézier and B-spline fits. No regularization or tuning on mask support was added. This keeps the comparison about representation capacity.

At **18 free values per branch**, the selected long branch gives:

| Function | Residual to extracted guide (mm) | Fitted tortuosity | Existing mask support |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| B-spline, 8 controls | 0.231 | 1.846 | 91.8% |
| Sine series, 6 modes | 0.242 | 1.838 | 94.2% |
| Chebyshev, 6 terms | 0.319 | 1.846 | 82.2% |

At this budget on this branch, the sine fit has slightly higher mask support while the B-spline has slightly lower guide residual. The polynomial fit has lower mask support despite a similar tortuosity ratio. These measurements do not identify a general winner or establish anatomical correctness. Global coefficients may be harder to adjust locally than B-spline controls; that is another useful distinction to explore interactively.

## Node visibility

The viewer now separates **junctions (gold)**, **terminations (blue)**, and **crop boundaries (purple diamonds)**, with larger adjustable markers and node IDs. Selected branch endpoints are labelled A/B. Click a node or use the node selector to inspect its coordinates, degree, and incident branches. Node IDs retain their indices in the cropped dense graph, so they are not consecutive 0–13 IDs.

Use **Nodes only** to remove occluding surfaces and lines, **Zoom to node** for a 6 mm neighborhood, and **Show full patch** to restore the extent. Mask opacity is adjustable and defaults to 10%. The [node overview](../experiments/ixi_patch/results/nodes.png) provides three projections; nearby nodes can overlap in a projection, so use the interactive inspector for those clusters.

## Sampling and metrics

Endpoint-constrained least squares uses 257 samples uniformly spaced along the guide's arc length. Piecewise fits use equal arc-length intervals with 129 samples per interval, sampling their internal joins from the guide and counting those joins as geometry parameters. Their joins guarantee position continuity only; smooth tangent matching is not imposed.

Metrics use physical coordinates and samples no more than 0.1 mm apart. Symmetric residual is the average of the two directed mean point-to-polyline distances. Tortuosity is length / endpoint chord. Mask membership uses the voxel cell containing each sample. Fitted curves are evaluated as dense polylines for these measurements. The patch summary uses unweighted means over all 12 branches; the selected-branch table makes long-branch failures visible that a mean over short branches can conceal.

## Initial observations

The viewer opens on branch 5, selected as the most tortuous extracted branch among those at least 5 mm long, without using curve-fitting results. Its extracted path length is 50.70 mm and tortuosity is 1.875.

Fits to this branch's extracted guide:

| Curve | Geometry values | Mean residual to guide (mm) | Fitted tortuosity | Inside existing mask |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Straight chord | 0 | 4.644 | 1.000 | 3.3% |
| Cubic Bézier | 6 | 1.149 | 1.647 | 28.4% |
| B-spline, 8 controls | 18 | 0.231 | 1.846 | 91.8% |
| Piecewise Bézier, 3 segments | 24 | 0.143 | 1.851 | 98.6% |

The extracted guide itself has 99.6% mask support. Mild smoothing changes its tortuosity from 1.875 to 1.859; the main bends persist. This supports testing richer curve families for this branch, without validating the extracted path as anatomy. The static overview shows MRI projections and how one cubic misses the larger bends.

Across all 12 branches, cubic Bézier has mean fitting residual 0.286 mm and mean mask support 85.6%; an eight-control B-spline gives 0.034 mm and 99.2%. The corresponding total edge geometry counts are 72 and 216 scalar values. All cases keep 14 object anchors. This reduces the anchor count relative to both dense (272) and adaptive (45) graphs, but **does not prove lower total network cost**: an eight-control spline on every short branch spends many unnecessary edge parameters.

The representation remains worth investigating. A single cubic is insufficient for the long winding branch in this patch; splines or several cubic segments can represent its large bends. The next useful study is a small set of additional patches, with image review and sensitivity to guide extraction/smoothing, followed by selecting curve complexity per branch. This one patch cannot settle anatomical accuracy, learnability, or generalization.

## Interaction and verification

Select a branch, fitting guide, and curve family. Toggle the MRI slice and change its orientation/index to inspect the vessel in depth. Click a pink control, or choose it under **Edit edge parameters**, and edit its X/Y/Z coordinates in physical mm. The curve and selected-branch measurements update. Restore fit returns to the saved least-squares result; comparison tables always show the saved fits.

Source images and datasets were read only. Endpoint constraints, graph edge coverage after contraction, patch dimensions, units, and foreground counts were checked during generation. JavaScript curve evaluation, residuals, and mask support were compared numerically with Python for the selected branch's cubic, spline, and piecewise fits; control editing and restoration were exercised with a mocked Plotly/DOM. The generated MRI/curve overview was visually inspected. A browser was unavailable on the cluster, so the full WebGL viewer still needs a local browser check.

For the added families, JavaScript and Python residuals, curve lengths, and mask support also matched for 2- and 6-term/mode fits. Coefficient edits/restoration and node selection, isolation, zoom, and extent reset were exercised with mocked Plotly/DOM. The node projections were visually inspected; the full browser interaction limitation still applies.

Reproduce from the shared projects directory using the existing scientific environment:

```bash
MPLCONFIGDIR=/tmp/gnbm-curve-mpl \
  "$WORK/venvs/vascular-graph-extraction-h100-torch231/bin/python" \
  graph-representation/experiments/ixi_patch/src/build.py
```

The builder, HTML template, and viewer code are in `experiments/ixi_patch/src/`; generated artifacts are in `experiments/ixi_patch/results/`. Documentation remains here in `docs/`.

## Catmull–Rom comparison

Centripetal Catmull–Rom with 6/8/10/12/16 total points is now available, alongside an equal-budget B-spline overlay. Volumes, guides, mesh, topology and original fits are unchanged. See [the construction and comparison notes](catmull-rom-single-cases.md).


<!-- END SOURCE: docs/research/spline_learning/ixi_patch.md -->

<a id="report-17"></a>

## Report 17

Source: `docs/research/spline_learning/local-geometry-diagnostic.md`

<!-- BEGIN SOURCE: docs/research/spline_learning/local-geometry-diagnostic.md -->

# Local image information for geometry — 2026-10-10

## Why this experiment

The user authorized a short geometry-specific local-feature comparison and
then pointed out that SyntheticMRI contains mostly small bends. This is a
material limitation: predictions close to chords can reflect the data's
geometry, not necessarily missing image information or a failed representation.
Keep the successful frozen SyntheticMRI detector for an interpretable matched
comparison, but stratify geometry evaluation by target tortuosity. IXI is the
next useful strongly curved-data study; its existing one-case oracle confirms
geometric capacity, but is not a population training benchmark.

The current geometry MLP receives object/relation tokens and predicted endpoint
geometry. These tokens summarize image information and may omit local details
along a vessel. The new question is whether early CNN features sampled on the
predicted path provide useful additional shape information. This is different
from the earlier [curve-informed connectivity](curve-informed-connectivity.md)
experiment, which sampled an added image encoder to change edge scores.
Here connectivity and detector state are fixed; only curve geometry learns.

## Dataset curvature check and corrected interpretation

Quick audit of the existing **128 SyntheticMRI validation patches**, using
cached eight-control fitted target curves and retaining branches >=5 mm:

- 1,509 eligible branches; median fitted tortuosity **1.0159**.
- 90th/95th/99th percentiles **1.0576 / 1.0821 / 1.1584**.
- **12.8%** exceed tortuosity 1.05; **2.5%** exceed 1.10.
- 567 long branches have maximum fitted-curve deviation from the chord >1 mm;
  low length/chord ratio does not imply a globally straight long branch.

In the existing illustrative single cases, 6/12 IXI branches exceed extracted
guide tortuosity 1.05, with maximum **1.8745**; 0/19 SyntheticMRI branches do,
with maximum **1.0308**. These cases were selected before fitting but are not
representative dataset samples. Guides/fits remain uncertain references.
Do not use these figures to claim a population difference without a broader
IXI audit, or use the small SyntheticMRI average gains alone to diagnose failure.

The available IXI checkpoint has reported validation Branch F1 around 0.0068
under its existing adaptive-graph protocol. A direct switch to that detector
would confound geometry with its detection/connectivity quality and a different
representation. No IXI model, dataset or target cache was changed in this task.
The strongly curved follow-up needs a separately specified IXI geometry study
and reliable endpoints/connectivity (or an explicitly labeled geometry oracle).

## Three matched arms

| Arm / task | Existing geometry MLP | New local correction | New CNN values |
|---|---|---|---|
| `token_control` / 871744_0 | Learns | Multiplied by zero | Sampled but inactive |
| `local_features` / 871744_1 | Learns | Learns | Actual local feature map |
| `zero_features` / 871744_2 | Learns | Learns | Zeroed before sampling |

All instantiate identical learned tensors/parameter counts. The correction's
final weights/bias start at zero, preserving the source curves in all arms.
The control's inactive branch gives the original token-head training behavior.
The zero-feature arm uses the same extra architecture to distinguish local
information from additional capacity. It retains physical predicted-endpoint
features and valid-support samples; it is not image-independent, since endpoints
and original tokens are image-predicted. Feature masking changes input statistics
as well as information, so it is a controlled ablation, not a perfect causal
decomposition of all capacity effects.

### What the head does

1. The existing model predicts an eight-control B-spline from the same frozen
   nodes and object/relation tokens as before.
2. Reuse the frozen CNN's first activation **before max pooling**: 64 channels
   at stride two (32³ positions for a 64³ MRI patch). Capturing this tensor
   adds no image encoder, detector computation or trainable CNN parameters.
3. Sample 32 uniformly selected parameter positions along that current base
   predicted curve. No target guides, controls, nodes or segmentation enter
   sampling. Sampled coordinates and CNN values are detached.
4. A small 1D convolution plus MLP reads this sequence, valid-support values,
   and the same ten physical endpoint/chord features. It predicts **six × three
   millimetre offsets** for the existing internal controls. Add them to the
   base controls. Endpoints remain exact copies of the detector's nodes.

This is one refinement per forward pass, not an iterative tracker. New module
size: **37,778 parameters**. The representation, cubic degree, knots, number
of controls and existing residual supervision remain unchanged. There is no
additional loss term or image-alignment objective.

Coordinate checks use the actual SENet first convolution: kernel 7, stride 2,
padding 3. Its feature centers correspond to raw voxel indices 0,2,4,... .
Convert raw normalized DHW coordinates to the feature grid before applying
the existing half-voxel `align_corners=False` trilinear sampler. Tests cover
fractional coordinates and odd/non-cubic input sizes. Paths are detached to
avoid an additional geometry feedback path through sampling locations.

## Fixed training and evaluation protocol

- Start from the successful frozen residual head after 15k updates, source
  `frozen_followup_20261009/residual_continue/model.pt`.
- Same 10,000 SyntheticMRI training patches; existing ordered 128 validation
  patches; fixed 512 training-monitoring patches. No new train/val membership,
  augmentation, oversampling of curved branches or test evaluation.
- **5,000 additional updates per arm**, batch four, seed 364505, fresh AdamW,
  constant LR **7e-5**, weight decay **1e-4**, spline weight **1.4739989613**.
- Train existing spline MLP plus the optional local module only. CNN,
  transformer, queries, node/edge heads, matching and all BN buffers stay fixed.
  Existing targets and the residual-control loss remain unchanged.
- Three-update GPU smoke per arm in a separate folder, then a fresh actual
  run from the identical source state. Checkpoint loading permits only the
  explicitly new local-module keys to be absent; all source weights load.
- Existing monitoring at 0/1k/5k: decoded graph metrics, same-endpoint chords,
  GT-matched positive-branch geometry, endpoint-neutral shape, endpoint-localized
  subset, fixed projections, losses, sensitivity and offline W&B.
- Additional **diagnostic-only** matched-positive strata: fitted GT length
  >=5 mm and tortuosity >1.05 (`curved_long`); other long branches
  (`near_straight_long`); length <5 mm (`short`). They partition evaluated
  positives and do not alter targets, losses, sampling, or primary metrics.
- Detector digests, assignment hashes and source initial decoded metrics are
  checked. Initial aggregate tolerance is 1e-5, following the previously
  measured numerical roundoff. Save actual initial tensors and batch-order
  hashes for a final cross-arm pairing audit. First gradients must be finite
  and active/inactive on the added branch according to its scale.

Initial CPU checks passed 11 tests across the new sampler/head routing, existing
frozen geometry and curve-evidence behavior. Eight relevant tests passed again
after adding strata, and the actual source checkpoint/model construction passed
after correcting the pre-pool activation hook name (`relu1`). An initial local
model check needed escalation because MPI initialization uses local sockets;
no scientific configuration was changed to resolve that environment restriction.
Python/Slurm syntax and diff checks passed. GPU smoke is still required.

## Interpretation and stopping point

- Local features outperform both controls on validation **curved** branches:
  supports additional usable local information under this sampling/feature recipe.
- Local and zero-feature arms both outperform the inactive token control:
  extra geometry capacity/endpoint conditioning is a plausible contributor;
  do not attribute the whole gain to image information.
- Training gain without validation gain: generalization remains the issue.
- No benefit on curved branches: this setup does not establish a useful gain;
  it does not prove images are unnecessary. Rare curved training examples,
  image/guide uncertainty, receptive-field coverage, feature choice and budget
  remain limitations. Sampling near a base curve can miss vessels with large
  displacements; this experiment does not test all image-aware representations.

Connectivity should remain exactly unchanged. The next result review should
keep geometry improvements distinct from detection and examine fixed visuals.
No automatic unfreezing, 300-epoch training or dataset switch follows these jobs.
An IXI curved-data study requires its own justified protocol.

## Files and jobs

Submitted **871744_0/1/2**: token control / local features / zero features.
One H100 each, one-hour ceiling, independently smoke-gated. Actual parallel
execution depends on scheduler availability. No results claimed at submission.

Code: `models/local_spline_geometry.py`; optional head construction and shared
feature plumbing in model, criterion, inference and matched evaluator;
`tests/test_local_spline_geometry.py`; reusable pilot runner.
Config: `configs/spline_local_geometry_pilot.yaml`.
Submission: `cluster/jean_zay/spline_local_geometry.slurm`.

Run root:
`/lustre/fsn1/projects/rech/vnc/upz25mj/experiments/gnbm/spline_learning/runs/local_geometry_pilot_20261010/`.
Contains each named arm and `smoke-<arm>` folders. Original files are preserved.
Logs: `experiments/spline_learning/logs/local-geometry-871744_<task>.{out,err}`.
Compact evidence/curvature audit:
`experiments/spline_learning/metadata/local-geometry/` in the code repository.

GPU startup confirmed: all three `smoke-<arm>/summary.json` files report **3 updates completed** and **detector unchanged**. No traceback/assertion markers were found in their logs at the check. All three Slurm tasks were running on separate one-GPU allocations (two may share a multi-GPU node). Full trial results remain pending; no performance conclusion from smoke runs.

## Completed results: local image information improves geometry

All three tasks completed successfully (14:53 / 15:28 / 14:48), each 5,000 additional updates. Initial state, detector state and batch-order hashes match across arms; validation assignments match, and every final detector digest is unchanged.

Validation: 128 patches, 2,059 matched positive branches, including 193 curved long branches. Train monitoring uses 512 patches.

| Arm | Train decoded curve F1 | Validation decoded curve F1 | Matched guide error (mm) | Endpoint-neutral error (mm) | Curved-long neutral error (mm) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| token_control | 0.7110 | 0.6905 | 0.8941 | 0.4509 | 1.2927 |
| local_features | 0.8455 | 0.8454 | 0.7399 | 0.3496 | 0.8985 |
| zero_features | 0.7108 | 0.6905 | 0.8945 | 0.4510 | 1.2940 |

Same-endpoint validation chords: decoded curve F1 0.6554, endpoint-neutral error 0.5014 mm overall and 1.6712 mm on curved long branches. Local features reduce endpoint-neutral error versus chords by 30.3% overall and 46.2% on curved long branches. Native node F1 0.9075 and edge F1 0.8586 are identical across arms.

The local-feature arm improves both training and validation; the zero-feature capacity control remains almost identical to the token control. This supports useful local image information for geometry under this protocol. It does not establish the initiating cause of the original scratch collapse or solve connectivity, which was frozen. Single seed, reused diagnostic validation and imperfect guide targets remain limitations. Short branches still worsen on endpoint-neutral error (local 0.1016 mm versus chord 0.0669 mm), so gains are not universal.

Decision point: validate the promising geometry result on the full existing validation split and inspect fixed predictions before another controlled joint-training comparison. No further jobs submitted during this result review. Per user clarification, remain on SyntheticMRI; defer IXI, where continuous branch targets and a reliable detector have not been established.

Compact evidence: `experiments/spline_learning/metadata/local-geometry/results.json`.

# Local geometry: full validation and controlled unfreezing

User authorized both experiments in parallel after the local-feature pilot.
Remain on SyntheticMRI; defer IXI until the representation learns reliably and
an appropriate continuous-branch target protocol is established.

## Evidence and purpose

The 5k frozen-detector pilot improved diagnostic validation curve F1 from 0.6905
to 0.8454 with local CNN features. Zeroing those features gave 0.6905. Detector
weights, assignments, initialization and batch order matched. This supports
useful image information for geometry, with a single seed and 128 validation
patches; it does not establish the cause of the original scratch collapse.

1. Full validation evaluates all three heads on exactly 1,952 existing validation
   patches. It compares decoded graphs, identical-endpoint chords and matched
   geometry separately, including the predeclared curvature strata. Six fixed
   cases (same seed/selection as earlier full-validation comparison) provide a
   portable HTML gallery of 2D projections of 3D predictions. No model updates or
   BN recalibration; these remain validation/model-selection results.
2. Controlled unfreezing starts all arms from `local_features/model.pt` after
   20,000 cumulative geometry updates. It asks whether graph learning can
   continue while preserving the newly improved geometry.

## Matched training protocol

- 10,000 existing SyntheticMRI training patches, batch 4, 5,000 updates.
- Same 128 validation and 512 training monitoring cases; no new sampling.
- Seed 364505; fresh AdamW; constant detector LR 7e-6, spline-head LR 7e-5.
- Residual supervision and spline weight 1.4739989612791453 unchanged.
- Unfreeze transformer encoder/decoder, queries, input projections and graph
  heads. The CNN, all normalization buffers and dropout mode remain fixed.
- Both the original spline MLP and local correction module train in every arm.
- `graph_only`: geometry inputs detached, so detector gradients come only from
  graph losses; geometry adapts to the changing detector.
- `tokens_only`: geometry also updates shared tokens, with predicted endpoint
  coordinates detached from the geometry loss.
- `joint`: geometry can also update predicted endpoint coordinates.
- Local feature sampling coordinates and CNN features remain detached in all
  arms, as in the successful pilot; no additional sampling-coordinate gradient
  is introduced. Thus `joint` names the existing token/endpoint routes, not a
  newly differentiable image sampler.
- Geometry monitoring 0/1k/5k, loss/sensitivity every 500. Gradient probes at
  1/1k/5k, assignment changes, frozen CNN/buffer digests and initial-source
  metric agreement are checked. Each run performs a fresh 3-update GPU smoke
  before its full trial. Evaluation jobs smoke on two samples first.

The new local-module gradient-routing unit test checks identical forward losses,
active head gradients, intended token/endpoint routes and no CNN-feature gradients.
Existing local sampling/inference tests are reused. Changes are limited to
configurable source update count/tracking groups, optional curvature summaries,
config selection in existing submission scripts and two new configs.

## Interpretation and stopping point

A joint arm should retain the frozen local geometry gain and improve detection
relative to the graph-only continuation. Compare topology as well as edge F1;
previous unfreezing improved some topology metrics and worsened others. Track
curved and short branches separately. Degradation relative to the matched
control implicates optimization coupling under this protocol; it is not evidence
against spline representability. No automatic scratch/300-epoch run follows.
Review full-validation images/results and all three continuations together.

## Reproducibility

Configs: `configs/spline_local_full_validation.yaml` and
`configs/spline_local_controlled_unfreeze.yaml` in the representation code repo.
Use existing Slurm scripts with `DIAGNOSTIC_CONFIG` exported via `sbatch`.

Output roots under
`/lustre/fsn1/projects/rech/vnc/upz25mj/experiments/gnbm/spline_learning/runs/`:

- `local_full_validation_20261010/`: per-arm evaluation and, when all finish,
  `comparison.html`, `.csv`, `.md`, `.json`. Download just `comparison.html`.
- `local_controlled_unfreeze_20261010/`: `graph_only`, `tokens_only`, `joint`,
  plus separate smoke folders; configs, provenance, metrics, checkpoint and
  offline W&B records. No original output is overwritten.

Submission IDs and checks are recorded below after submission.

Submitted evaluation array **875855_0/1/2** (token/local/zero) and controlled-unfreezing array **875856_0/1/2** (graph-only/token-route/joint-route). Six targeted CPU tests passed, plus syntax/diff checks. GPU smokes are pending at submission. One H100 per task, one-hour ceiling; concurrency depends on scheduler availability. Logs: `local-full-val-875855_<task>.{out,err}` and `local-unfreeze-875856_<task>.{out,err}` under `experiments/spline_learning/logs/`.

## Completed results — 2026-10-10

All six jobs COMPLETED (exit 0:0). Full validation took 10:08–10:22 per arm; unfreezing took 17:04–17:33. All unfreezing arms completed 5,000 updates with identical initial-state and batch-order hashes, and frozen CNN/buffers unchanged.

Full validation (1,952 patches, 31,934 matched branches):

| Head | Curve F1 | Endpoint-neutral error mm |
|---|---:|---:|
| token_control | 0.68411 | 0.46036 |
| local_features | 0.84012 | 0.35986 |
| zero_features | 0.68475 | 0.46009 |

Local features reduce endpoint-neutral error versus same-endpoint chords by 30.1% overall and 47.2% on 3,116 curved long branches. Native node F1 0.91041, edge F1 0.86363 and branch F1 0.27625 remain identical across frozen arms.

Unfreezing results on the original **128 diagnostic validation patches**, not the full split:

| Route | Node F1 | Edge F1 | Branch F1 | Curve F1 | Endpoint-neutral error mm |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| graph_only | 0.90590 | 0.86392 | 0.27125 | 0.84159 | 0.34037 |
| tokens_only | 0.90599 | 0.86786 | 0.27160 | 0.84678 | 0.34016 |
| joint | 0.90716 | 0.86679 | 0.28253 | 0.84290 | 0.34261 |

Frozen local source on these same 128 patches: node F1 0.90753, edge F1 0.85858, branch F1 0.25497, curve F1 0.84542, endpoint-neutral error 0.34958 mm. All continuations retain the large geometry gain. Token-route has the highest edge/curve F1; joint-route has the highest branch F1. No decisive overall winner or statistical significance established. Geometry improvement relative to graph-only continuation is small; the larger gain remains local image conditioning. Transformer memory sensitivity stays near 0.92 and GT assignment changes are similar (6.64–6.72%); no collapse detected.

Topology errors (graph-only / tokens / joint): Betti0 1.01563 / 0.97656 / 1.02344; Betti1 1.11719 / 1.00781 / 1.03125. These are diagnostic subset scores; avoid comparing directly with full-validation scores.

Gallery generated: `local_full_validation_20261010/comparison.html` (9,818,757 bytes). Inspected token/local projections for sample_000075_0287 and local sample_000014_0919. Visible residual localization/connectivity errors remain; individual branches are still nearly straight. The gallery is illustrative, not evidence of universal improvement. Original records contain distinct learned controls and 64-point sampled curves; the images plot sampled curves.

Next decision: compare the three unfreezing checkpoints on the full validation split before selecting a continuation. Remain on SyntheticMRI. No additional jobs launched during this result review.

# Longer stability continuation after local-geometry unfreezing

User authorized full validation, selection and the longer continuation together.
This follows the successful frozen local-image geometry experiment and three
short controlled-unfreezing runs. Remain on SyntheticMRI.

## Selection fixed before full-validation results

Evaluate graph_only, tokens_only and joint on all 1,952 existing validation
patches, using the same protocols and fixed six visualization cases. The frozen
local-image checkpoint's completed full validation is the reference.

A candidate must retain curve F1 and node F1 within 0.01 absolute of the reference,
and endpoint-neutral matched geometry error within 1.05 times the reference.
Among eligible candidates choose highest common branch F1, breaking ties by
curve F1 then native edge F1. These are pragmatic retention tolerances, not
statistical significance bounds. Branch F1 prioritizes recovered connectivity;
the separate guards retain the geometry benefit and node detection. Other
metrics, including Betti errors, remain reported rather than hidden in a score.
If none passes, selection raises before any continuation training.

The selected route and every candidate's values are recorded in selection.json.
This is validation-based model selection, not an unbiased test claim.

## Longer continuation

- Load the selected 5k-unfreezing checkpoint: 25,000 total geometry updates so far.
- Resume both model and AdamW state; no optimizer reset. Existing older checkpoint
  metadata provides cumulative updates as source updates plus completed steps.
- Another 25,000 updates, batch 4 on the same 10k patches: 10 more dataset passes.
- Same constant detector LR 7e-6, spline/local head LR 7e-5, residual objective,
  weight 1.4739989612791453 and selected gradient route.
- Same CNN/BN freeze and eval-mode/dropout policy. No additional unfreezing.
- Shuffle stream restarts with seed 364505; this is an explicitly restarted data
  order, not an exact uninterrupted RNG/data-loader resume.
- Monitor the same 128 validation and 512 training cases. Loss and sensitivity
  every 1k updates; decoded and matched geometry every 5k, including curvature
  strata, node/edge/branch metrics and fixed images.
- Save intermediate model+optimizer snapshots at 5k and 15k; final at 25k.
  Count/digest/finite-gradient checks remain active. Offline W&B records retained.
- First run a 3-update GPU smoke from the selected checkpoint with optimizer
  restoration. The full continuation starts afresh from that source afterward.

After success, evaluate the final checkpoint on all 1,952 validation patches.
Reuse the already completed selected-baseline evaluation through a read-only
symlink in the final comparison directory. No duplicate baseline inference is
needed. Generate before/after tables and a portable six-case projection gallery.
No test samples enter selection or training.

This is a bounded longer-stability experiment, not a 300-epoch training claim.
The full validation comparison, intermediate trajectories and images are needed
before deciding whether further training or additional unfreezing is justified.
No automatic further experiment follows this pipeline.

## Reproducibility and outputs

- `configs/spline_local_unfreeze_full_validation.yaml`: three-candidate evaluation.
- `configs/spline_local_stability.yaml`: fixed selection and extension settings.
- `scripts/select_spline_stability.py`: deterministic selection and resolved configs.
- `scripts/controlled_spline_unfreeze.py`: existing training, with opt-in optimizer
  restoration and intermediate checkpoints; prior runs retain default behavior.
- `cluster/jean_zay/spline_local_stability.slurm`: selection, smoke, continuation.

Outputs under
`/lustre/fsn1/projects/rech/vnc/upz25mj/experiments/gnbm/spline_learning/runs/`:

- `local_unfreeze_full_validation_20261010/`: candidate evaluation and gallery.
- `local_stability_20261010/selection.json`: chosen route, rule and candidate values.
- `local_stability_20261010/training/<selected>/`: continuation and monitoring.
- `local_stability_20261010/full-validation/comparison.html`: final portable gallery.

The Slurm dependency chain enforces full-validation completion before selection
and successful training before final evaluation. Selection, smoke or training
failure prevents later expensive stages. Existing results remain untouched.

Submitted candidate evaluation **876609_0/1/2**, selection/continuation **876621** (`afterok:876609`), final evaluation **876622_1** (`afterok:876621`). Five targeted CPU tests passed, with Python/Slurm syntax and diff checks. GPU smokes remain queued with each stage. Estimated pipeline wall time excluding queue: roughly 1–1.5 hours; continuation has a two-hour ceiling. Selection is pending full validation.

## Startup failure and correction

Candidate evaluations 876609_0/1/2 completed (9:12–9:39). Continuation 876621 failed after six seconds while staging runtime packages: `mkdir: cannot create directory /lustre/fsn1/jobscratch/upz25mj_876621: Permission denied`. Selection and training never started. Removed blocked final evaluation 876622 and resubmitted continuation as 877101. The two launch scripts now unset JOBSCRATCH before environment setup, using existing node-local /tmp runtime and temporary-file defaults. Syntax/diff checks passed; existing three-update GPU smoke still gates full training. Scientific settings unchanged.

Full validation: graph_only branch F1 0.292610 / curve F1 0.843311; tokens_only 0.290941 / 0.842957; joint 0.291344 / 0.843841. All satisfy the predeclared geometry/node guards. Thus graph_only is selected by branch F1, with small differences and no significance claim. This route continues training the graph detector on graph losses while adapting the local spline head through detached detector inputs.

Replacement final evaluation: **877103_1**, dependency `afterok:877101`.

## Completed stability result

Continuation **877101** completed 25,000 updates in **51:28**; final evaluation **877103_1** completed in **9:04**, both exit 0:0. CNN/buffers remained fixed, and final evaluation did not change model state.

Full validation (1,952 patches):

| Metric | Before extension | After extension |
|---|---:|---:|
| node_f1 | 0.909016 | 0.909413 |
| edge_f1 | 0.872307 | 0.874605 |
| branch_f1 | 0.292610 | 0.281353 |
| curve_f1 | 0.843311 | 0.844922 |
| endpoint_neutral_mm | 0.352656 | 0.343019 |
| matched_guide_mm | 0.730113 | 0.731221 |
| betti0_error | 0.871926 | 0.981557 |
| betti1_error | 1.024078 | 0.793545 |

The local-geometry gain persists without transformer collapse. However, branch F1 decreases by 0.01126 and Betti0 error worsens, while native edge F1, endpoint-neutral geometry and Betti1 error improve. Raw matched guide error is essentially unchanged/slightly worse. Thus longer training is stable in the sense of no collapse, but is not an overall connectivity improvement; do not automatically replace the earlier checkpoint.

The selected graph_only route lets geometry adapt to a detector trained on graph losses, with geometry inputs detached. This does not establish stability of fully coupled geometry gradients or learning from scratch. Full validation remains used for selection, not an unbiased test claim.

The old cache symlinks may require repointing to restored images if those experiments are extracted for reproduction.

The visible active folder now has one current dataset link, one current run-output link, current logs, a clearly named `metadata` directory, and a README explaining them. Current metadata includes exact accepted membership, preparation plan, source graph hashes, source crop configuration, restoration checks and active job IDs. Restore tools use this metadata rather than an ambiguous `source_snapshot` directory.

The initial 2D/3D, IXI and SyntheticMRI interactive representation examples remain under graph-representation/experiments as reference examples; their role is explained in the README. They are distinct from current model-training outputs.

Runtime recovery update: the fixed 1.4 GB package archive is stored outside projects at `/lustre/fswork/projects/rech/vnc/upz25mj/experiments/gnbm/spline-runtime-20261006/site-packages.tar`. Job-local extraction uses node temporary storage. It prevents the training job from repeatedly importing packages from the changing shared installation; it is required for the current resumed run, not an obsolete experiment folder.

<a id="report-21"></a>

## Report 21

Source: `docs/research/spline_learning/representation-implementation.md`

<!-- BEGIN SOURCE: docs/research/spline_learning/representation-implementation.md -->

Given our current representation, I would **not replace the relation head outright**. I would reinterpret an edge as having two outputs:

\[
e_{ij}=
\left(
p_{ij}^{\text{edge}},
\;P_1,\ldots,P_8
\right)
\]

because

\[
P_0=x_i,\qquad P_9=x_j
\]

are already fixed by the two graph nodes. With our fixed cubic degree and fixed knot vector, the network only has to predict **16 values in 2D or 24 in 3D**.

The current RelationFormer relation mechanism is already based on a pair representation built from the two object tokens and the shared relation token; the natural modification is therefore to make that pair representation produce geometry as well as existence.

## The approaches I would seriously consider

| Approach | Edge existence | 8 internal controls | Complexity | My view |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A. Parallel flat spline head** | existing relation head | one MLP → 16/24 values | Low | **Start here** |
| **B. Shared multi-task edge head** | shared pair trunk → classifier | same trunk → geometry | Low | Also very reasonable |
| **C. Per-control shared head** | relation classifier | same small head called for \(k=1...8\) | Medium | **Best structured alternative** |
| **D. Image-conditioned control decoder** | relation classifier | 8 control queries attend to image features | High | Likely strongest long-term |
| E. Autoregressive controls | relation classifier | predict \(P_1\to P_2\to...\) | Medium/high | I would avoid initially |

The difference among A–D is mostly **where the information for the spline comes from and how much structure you impose on the 8 controls**.

---

# A. Parallel spline head — the cleanest first experiment

Keep our current relation classifier:

\[
z_{ij} = f_{\rm pair}(o_i,r,o_j)
\]

\[
p_{ij}^{edge}
=
h_{\rm cls}(z_{ij})
\]

and simply add:

\[
\Delta_{ij}
=
h_{\rm spline}(z_{ij},x_i,x_j)
\in\mathbb R^{8d}.
\]

So in 3D:

\[
h_{\rm spline}\rightarrow24
\]

and in 2D:

\[
h_{\rm spline}\rightarrow16.
\]

I would explicitly include endpoint geometry in this head, perhaps something like

\[
[z_{ij},x_i,x_j,x_j-x_i,\|x_j-x_i\|].
\]

The object embeddings already contain spatial information, but making the actual chord explicit makes the regression problem easier.

### Don't predict absolute controls

Initialize them along the straight chord:

\[
B_k
=
(1-t_k)x_i+t_kx_j,
\qquad
t_k=\frac{k}{9}.
\]

Then predict:

\[
P_k=B_k+\Delta P_k,
\qquad k=1,\ldots,8.
\]

So a straight vessel corresponds approximately to

\[
\Delta P_k=0.
\]

This is the version I would implement first.

```text
                         ┌── current classifier ──> edge / no edge
[o_i, r, o_j] ── pair ──┤
                         └── spline MLP ─────────> ΔP1 ... ΔP8
                                      ↑
                                  x_i , x_j
```

The major advantage is that you can initialize the existing network from our pretrained GrEVE checkpoint and **randomly initialize only the spline head**.

---

# B. A genuinely shared edge head

Slightly different architecture:

\[
[o_i,r,o_j,\text{geometry}]
\rightarrow
z_{ij}^{edge}
\]

and then:

\[
z_{ij}^{edge}
\rightarrow
\begin{cases}
p_{ij}^{edge}\\
\Delta P_{1:8}
\end{cases}
\]

The edge-existence and edge-shape tasks therefore share more computation.

This is conceptually attractive because:

> “Does a vessel connect these points?” and “What path does that vessel take?” are related questions.

For example, the shared representation may learn:

```text
these two nodes belong to the same vessel
                  +
the vessel bends upward between them
```

rather than learning those things independently.

But this modifies the currently trained relation head more substantially.

For our first experiment, I prefer **A** because you preserve the edge classifier exactly. If A works, B becomes an interesting ablation.

---

# C. Per-control shared prediction

I actually like this one quite a lot as a second experiment.

Instead of one MLP outputting all 24 coordinates at once,

\[
z_{ij}\rightarrow
[\Delta P_1,\Delta P_2,\ldots,\Delta P_8],
\]

introduce a small embedding identifying each internal control position:

\[
q_k=[z_{ij},e_k,t_k,B_k].
\]

Then use the **same MLP** for each control:

\[
\Delta P_k=h_{\rm ctrl}(q_k).
\]

So:

```text
                            k=1 ──> ΔP1
                            k=2 ──> ΔP2
                              ...
pair representation ------ k=8 ──> ΔP8
                    same control MLP
```

The network knows that \(P_2\) is near the beginning and \(P_7\) is near the end because it gets \(t_k\).

There are several nice properties:

- weight sharing across controls;
- explicit ordering along the branch;
- fewer arbitrary output dimensions;
- potentially easier to move later from 10 controls to another \(K\);
- natural starting point for image-conditioned control queries.

It's essentially saying:

> “Given this vessel relation, tell me where the control at relative branch position \(t_k\) should move.”

I think this is more elegant than a flat `Linear(hidden_dim, 24)` head, although the flat head is the correct baseline.

---

# D. Image-conditioned control decoder

This is the one I think could eventually be strongest for real data.

The problem with A–C is that after RelationFormer creates \(o_i,o_j,r\), the spline head has no new opportunity to look closely at the **image along the vessel between the endpoints**.

For a highly curved branch:

```text
i
 \
  \
   \____
        \____ j
```

the exact trajectory is encoded in the raw volume.

So initialize our eight control references:

\[
B_1,\ldots,B_8
\]

along the straight chord.

Create eight control queries conditioned on the relation:

\[
q_{ij}^{k}
=
f(z_{ij},e_k).
\]

Then let them cross-attend to image features around \(B_k\).

Conceptually:

```text
                  image feature volume
                       ↑ ↑ ↑ ↑
                       │ │ │ │
i --- B1 --- B2 --- B3 --- ... --- B8 --- j
      ↓      ↓      ↓             ↓
     q1     q2     q3            q8
      │      │      │             │
     ΔP1    ΔP2    ΔP3           ΔP8
```

That is very compatible with the deformable-attention philosophy already used in RelationFormer.

Each control effectively asks:

> “I currently think the vessel should pass around here. Where does the image evidence tell me to move?”

I would consider this the **proper architectural extension** if the simple MLP cannot recover tortuous branches.

But not the first implementation.

---

# One detail I would change from our current description: controls in mm are good, but consider residual scaling

You said:

> Spatial controls and segment joins are edge parameters in mm.

I agree that the final representation should be physical.

But raw regression of a displacement such as

\[
\Delta P_k=(+5.2,-3.4,+1.7)\text{ mm}
\]

may have a very different scale across tiny and very long branches.

I would test two parameterizations.

### Physical residual

\[
P_k=B_k+\Delta P_k^{mm}.
\]

Very interpretable.

### Relative residual

\[
P_k
=
B_k+
L_{ij}\Delta \tilde P_k,
\]

where

\[
L_{ij}=\|x_j-x_i\|.
\]

Then the network predicts a dimensionless relative deformation.

At rendering/output time, everything still becomes mm.

I wouldn't decide theoretically which is better. This is a cheap ablation.

---

# The undirected-edge problem needs to be solved explicitly

This becomes more important now.

For vessel graphs,

\[
i\leftrightarrow j
\]

is the same edge as

\[
j\leftrightarrow i.
\]

But:

\[
[P_0,P_1,\ldots,P_9]
\]

becomes

\[
[P_9,P_8,\ldots,P_0]
\]

when traversed backward.

our current binary relation head can be order invariant. A spline-control head **cannot simply be invariant**, because control order has meaning.

I would choose a deterministic orientation before passing a pair through the spline head.

For example:

\[
i\rightarrow j
\]

according to lexicographic physical position:

1. lower \(x\);
2. then lower \(y\);
3. then lower \(z\).

Then GT splines are stored/reversed to follow the same convention.

That way there is always one canonical sequence:

\[
P_0\rightarrow P_9.
\]

Alternatively, use an orientation-invariant loss:

\[
L=
\min
\left[
L(P,P^*),
L(P,\operatorname{reverse}(P^*))
\right].
\]

I slightly prefer **canonical orientation** because it also gives the network a deterministic learning target.

---

# What I would use for the loss

With our fixed basis, one very nice thing happens.

For the fixed cubic B-spline:

\[
C(t)=
\sum_{i=0}^{9}
P_i N_{i,3}(t),
\]

the basis functions are always the same.

Choose, say, \(M=32\) or \(64\) values of \(t\), and precompute

\[
B_{mi}=N_{i,3}(t_m).
\]

Then:

\[
X=BP
\]

gives the whole sampled curve.

This operation is differentiable and almost free.

So I would compare two losses.

### Baseline

Direct control regression:

\[
L_{\rm ctrl}
=
\frac18
\sum_{k=1}^{8}
\operatorname{SmoothL1}
(P_k,P^*_k).
\]

### More representation-aligned version

Curve regression:

\[
L_{\rm curve}
=
\frac1M
\sum_m
\operatorname{SmoothL1}
(
\hat C(t_m),C^*(t_m)
).
\]

I suspect the second may be better because the **controls themselves are not what you care about**; the curve is.

And critically, I would start with:

\[
L_{\rm edge}
=
L_{\rm focal}
+
\lambda_{\rm geom}L_{\rm curve},
\]

only for GT-positive edges.

Not five spline losses.

---

# There's also a fifth possibility, but I wouldn't prioritize it

You could predict a set of sampled centerline points first:

\[
\hat X_1,\ldots,\hat X_M
\]

and then solve for the ten B-spline controls through a fixed least-squares mapping.

Since knots and basis are fixed:

\[
P \approx B^\dagger X.
\]

This could even remain differentiable.

But this effectively asks the network to predict many centerline samples just to compress them afterward, which starts moving back toward the dense-centerline methods you are trying to avoid.

So I see no reason to start there.

---

## My experimental tree would therefore be

**V0 — sanity check**

\[
[o_i,r,o_j,x_i,x_j]
\rightarrow
24
\]

flat residual controls, direct control SmoothL1.

If this doesn't even overfit a small dataset, something is wrong upstream.

**V1 — actual baseline**

Same flat spline head, but train through the sampled B-spline curve:

\[
L_{\rm curve}.
\]

**V2 — structured controls**

Shared per-control MLP:

\[
(z_{ij},t_k,B_k)
\rightarrow
\Delta P_k.
\]

Compare to V1.

**V3 — only if geometry remains the bottleneck**

Per-control queries with image/deformable cross-attention.

And throughout V0–V3:

- keep the existing edge classifier;
- keep endpoints fixed;
- keep \(K=10\);
- keep degree and knots fixed;
- keep Hungarian initially;
- keep focal edge classification;
- supervise spline geometry only for positive matched relations.

That progression would tell you something meaningful at every step instead of jumping immediately to a completely new edge decoder.

## Report 22

Source: `docs/research/spline_learning/residual-token-diagnostics.md`

<!-- BEGIN SOURCE: docs/research/spline_learning/residual-token-diagnostics.md -->

# Frozen residual loss and token-input diagnostics — 2026-10-09

## Why these tests

The completed [frozen absolute-control diagnostic](frozen-spline-investigation.md)
learned training geometry but regressed on validation. Detector state and
correspondences remained fixed. Its endpoint-neutral results suggest that
absolute-control supervision partly learns compensation for localization error.
It remains unclear whether detector tokens supply transferable shape information.

The user authorized the next tests and requested several diagnostics together.
Run three new arms in parallel to complete a small 2×2 comparison. Reuse the
completed absolute/full-token run as the fourth arm; do not repeat it.

| Arm | Geometry objective | Spline-head token input | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Existing `absolute_controls` | Absolute control coordinates | Original tokens | Completed, job 813146 |
| `residual_full` | Control deviation from chord | Original tokens | New task 0 |
| `absolute_endpoints` | Absolute control coordinates | Zeroed token features | New task 1 |
| `residual_endpoints` | Control deviation from chord | Zeroed token features | New task 2 |

Endpoint-only arms still use **image-predicted endpoints**, their physical
coordinates, chord direction/vector, and length. They are not image-blind.
Zeroing pair-token features preserves the MLP architecture, initial tensors,
and nominal parameter count. It reduces effective input information/capacity;
interpret any change as this specific ablation, not proof that tokens contain
no geometric information.

## Fixed conditions

All four arms use the original successful straight checkpoint, the same
512 training / 128 validation patches (64/13 subjects), seed 364505, batch four,
eight controls, fresh head-only AdamW with constant LR 7e-5 and weight decay
1e-4, 5,000 updates, and spline weight 1.4739989612791453. All detector parameters
and BN buffers remain frozen in evaluation mode. No new data, test-set scoring,
matching changes, image-feature module, or unfreezing is introduced.

Monitoring matches the completed control: loss/sensitivity every 500 updates;
full training/validation matched-positive and decoded-graph evaluations at
0, 1,000, and 5,000 updates. Each curve is compared with its own identical-
endpoint chord. Save raw-guide errors, fitted-target errors, residual errors,
endpoint-neutral diagnostics, the localized endpoint subset, fixed projections,
and W&B offline data. Do not compare total losses across different objectives.

## Residual objective and implementation

Only the spline objective changes in residual arms; it replaces the absolute
error instead of adding a second term. For an internal control at its fixed
Greville coordinate g, in physical millimetres:

```
endpoint_delta = predicted_endpoints - GT_endpoints
residual_error = (predicted_control - GT_control)
                 - ((1-g)*endpoint_delta[start] + g*endpoint_delta[end])
loss = SmoothL1(residual_error, beta=1 mm)
```

This equals predicted residual minus GT residual. Physical coordinate mapping
and canonical pair orientation are unchanged. Predicted endpoints still anchor
the output curve; GT endpoints only define supervision. Detachment is already
provided by the frozen detector's `no_grad` forward, so there is no additional
detachment intervention. The existing absolute geometric error metrics retain
their original meanings regardless of objective.

- `loss.spline.target` selects `absolute` (unchanged default) or `residual`.
  Validation restricts the new residual option to B-spline control loss.
- `model.spline.token_inputs` selects `full` (unchanged default) or `zero`.
  The head applies masking in its shared forward, including inference.
- The pilot runner records these settings and verifies initial tensor hash,
  checkpoint, detector hash, loss weight, learning rate/schedule, membership,
  probe IDs, assignment hashes, and final batch-order hash against the saved
  corresponding smoke/trial control. Comparison failures invalidate the run.

Eleven focused CPU tests passed, including residual error in physical units,
removal of direct translation coupling at zero residual, finite/nonzero head
gradients, the remaining endpoint-feature route once residual weights are
nonzero, token masking in train/eval modes, exact detector/BN freezing, and
existing B-spline behavior. Syntax/Slurm checks passed. Each new GPU task runs
its own three-update smoke before restarting the actual trial from the original
checkpoint and seed. Original results remain untouched.

## Interpretation and stopping point

- Residual/full vs absolute/full tests whether replacing localization-contaminated
  targets improves held-out residual shape and raw geometry. Improvement would
  support this target-confounding explanation; it would not by itself identify
  the initiating cause of the original scratch encoder collapse.
- Full vs endpoint-only, within each objective, tests the incremental predictive
  value of tokens under this recipe. A training-only advantage suggests
  memorization; a validation advantage supports transferable token information.
- If residual helps only endpoint-neutral geometry, fixed node localization may
  still limit deployed curves. If raw error improves while endpoint-neutral
  geometry worsens, avoid labeling the gain as pure curvature recovery.
- Inspect the shared early evaluation (1,000 updates) as well as the fixed
  final budget; the control previously overfit after an early small gain.
- If all variants fail validation, do not automatically unfreeze or launch a
  full training. Revisit feature/target generalization with the measured evidence.

Stop after these frozen diagnostics to discuss results. Phase 4 joint training
would need a justified, matched graph-only continuation from the same checkpoint.

## Locations

Config: `DenseVesselGraph/configs/spline_frozen_factorial_pilot.yaml`.
Submission: `cluster/jean_zay/spline_frozen_factorial.slurm` in that repository.
Each array task requests one H100 for at most 30 minutes; tasks may run in
parallel subject to scheduler availability.

Output root:
`/lustre/fsn1/projects/rech/vnc/upz25mj/experiments/gnbm/spline_learning/runs/frozen_factorial_pilot_20261009/`.
It contains each named arm and separate `smoke-<arm>` directories. Existing
directories are never overwritten.

Compact submission evidence:
`experiments/spline_learning/metadata/frozen-factorial/` in the code repository.

## Submission

Submitted array **815195**: `_0` residual/full tokens; `_1` absolute/endpoints only; `_2` residual/endpoints only. The three tasks are independently smoke-gated and may run concurrently. No completed result is claimed at submission. Logs: `experiments/spline_learning/logs/frozen-factorial-815195_<task>.{out,err}`.

## Completed results

All three jobs completed 5,000 updates with exit 0:0. Elapsed times including
smoke/staging: 815195_0 **14m25s**, _1 **14m27s**, _2 **14m00s**. Initialization,
checkpoint, batch-order, membership and fixed-assignment checks agree with the
completed control. Detector state and image sensitivity remain fixed. Native
validation node/edge F1 is unchanged at 0.90753 / 0.85858 for every arm.

### Full decoded graph: common whole-curve F1 (higher is better)

| Representation / objective / input | Training | Validation |
|---|---:|---:|
| Same-endpoint straight chords | 0.64812 | 0.65540 |
| Absolute / full tokens (previous control) | 0.83403 | 0.58567 |
| Residual / full tokens | 0.79694 | 0.61590 |
| Absolute / endpoints only | 0.65511 | 0.65584 |
| Residual / endpoints only | 0.65447 | 0.64957 |

### GT-matched branch geometry (millimetres; lower is better)

These rows concern 8,454 training / 2,059 validation positive pairs regardless
of decoded edge acceptance, not the subset of recovered decoded branches.

| Objective / input | Train raw guide error | Val raw guide error | Train endpoint-neutral error | Val endpoint-neutral error |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Chords | 0.96148 | 0.95368 | 0.51414 | 0.50138 |
| Absolute / full tokens | 0.57203 | 1.03307 | 0.55563 | 0.70664 |
| Residual / full tokens | 0.78370 | 0.97352 | 0.25340 | 0.53300 |
| Absolute / endpoints only | 0.94720 | 0.94739 | 0.53434 | 0.53041 |
| Residual / endpoints only | 0.95061 | 0.95500 | 0.50488 | 0.50778 |

At update 1,000, residual/full validation curve F1 was 0.65541 (essentially
its chord baseline) and endpoint-neutral error 0.49803 (a small improvement
from 0.50138). Later it overfits. Endpoint-only validation F1 at update 1,000
was 0.65964/absolute and 0.65733/residual. Small early gains are not evidence
of robust generalized curvature recovery or a statistical advantage.

### What these tests establish

1. **The residual objective changes what is learned.** With full tokens,
   endpoint-neutral training error falls 50.7% below chords, versus worsening
   8.1% under absolute supervision. Thus the large absolute-loss training gain
   was partly localization compensation, while residual training can learn
   actual deviation from the GT chord on training data.
2. **Residual targets alone do not solve generalization.** Validation raw
   guide error remains 2.1% worse than chords, endpoint-neutral error 6.3%
   worse, and decoded curve F1 below the chord baseline. It substantially
   reduces the damage relative to absolute/full but is not a validated fix.
3. **Token inputs enable training fit, not demonstrated validation transfer
   under this recipe.** Removing them nearly eliminates large training gains
   and the large validation deterioration. The endpoint-only models mostly
   match the chord baseline; they are not a successful curved representation.
   Their lower effective input capacity is a confound when interpreting token
   usefulness. These results do not prove that tokens lack shape information.
4. **This failure is broader than detector drift.** Geometry generalization
   fails with weights, BN statistics and matching fixed. The original scratch
   encoder collapse is still an observed final-state failure whose initiating
   cause remains unidentified; these frozen experiments do not reproduce it.

### Next decision (not launched)

Before unfreezing or adding a new architecture, test whether limited geometry
training data explains the gap: keep the residual/full frozen setup and expand
only training membership to the already prepared 10,000 patches, retaining
these 128 validation patches and a matched update budget. This is a proposed
short diagnostic of data breadth, not a long run or claimed solution. A failure
would still need interpretation against training fit and optimization budget;
it would not prove features are uninformative. Alternatively, a local-feature
head would test a different architectural hypothesis and should be discussed
explicitly before implementing it. No further training was submitted while
recording these results.

Verified summaries, histories, comparison CSV and completion audit are saved
in `experiments/spline_learning/metadata/frozen-factorial/`. Full models,
predictions, projections, per-branch results and offline W&B data remain in the
run directories listed above. Original results are preserved.

## Authorized follow-up: broader geometry training data

The user approved the next diagnostic. Run one new residual/full-token frozen
arm on the existing **10,000 training patches**, reusing completed 512-patch
residual/full job 815195_0 as the control. Keep the original checkpoint, head
initialization, loss weight, optimizer, constant LR, 5,000-update budget, batch
size, and ordered 128 validation patches. The detector and BN remain frozen.
Training geometry evaluation retains exactly the original 512 training cases;
this is a fixed monitoring subset, not an estimate across all 10,000 cases.
Validation and train metrics remain directly comparable on their fixed cases.

Five thousand batch-four updates expose 20,000 examples: approximately two
passes over 10k instead of 39 over 512. Thus the intervention tests broader
membership with less repetition at equal update budget. A negative result can
still reflect insufficient optimization per sample, and cannot establish that
tokens contain no usable geometry. Batch order necessarily changes; its hash
is recorded but is not asserted equal. Initialization, settings, validation
membership, and assignments on the fixed evaluation cases are still checked
against the saved control. No original results are overwritten.

Minimal implementation: generalize the runner's hard-coded 512/128 assertion,
add an explicit expanded-training reference comparison, and evaluate training
geometry on the control's saved membership. No model, loss, matcher, or data
cache changes. Config `configs/spline_frozen_breadth_pilot.yaml`; submission
`cluster/jean_zay/spline_frozen_breadth.slurm`. A separate three-update GPU smoke
must pass before the fresh 5,000-update trial. One H100, 30-minute limit.
Outputs: `runs/frozen_breadth_pilot_20261009/{smoke-residual_full,residual_full}`
under the same spline-learning root. W&B remains offline.

**What this says about the 300-epoch failure:** joint optimization and training
setup remain plausible contributors, but there is no evidence that a single
setup mistake is the sole cause. Original BN diagnostics did not rescue the
collapsed model, and frozen-detector experiments exhibit a separate geometry
generalization problem without detector drift. Successful fitting establishes
representational feasibility on training cases, not reliable transfer. This
follow-up tests data breadth; it does not directly reproduce or identify the
initiating cause of encoder collapse. Stop after results for interpretation.

Submitted as **816293**, initially pending for priority. Syntax/shell checks, five CPU unit tests, and exact dataset-membership checks passed. The first local unit-test attempt encountered stale SymPy files in a reused temporary runtime directory; rerunning in a fresh unique directory passed. Slurm uses its own job-specific staged runtime. Logs: `experiments/spline_learning/logs/frozen-breadth-816293.{out,err}`. Submission evidence: `experiments/spline_learning/metadata/frozen-breadth/submission.json`. No results yet.

## Broader-data result: 816293 completed

Completed successfully in **14m19s**, exit 0:0, with 5,000 trial updates after
the separate smoke. Initialization/settings checks passed against residual/full
815195_0. Detector parameters, BN buffers, sensitivity, matching, and native
node/edge detection remained fixed. Exact ordered evaluation membership was
verified: original 512 training cases and 128 validation cases. The expanded
training set still covers the same 64 subjects; this adds patches, not subjects.

### Fixed-case decoded curve F1 (higher is better)

| Representation / head training population | Training subset | Validation |
|---|---:|---:|
| Same-endpoint straight chords | 0.64812 | 0.65540 |
| Residual/full, 512 patches | 0.79694 | 0.61590 |
| Residual/full, 10,000 patches | 0.67275 | 0.67865 |

The new validation curve F1 improves **0.02325 absolute** over identical-endpoint
chords. At update 1,000 it was 0.66275; the final value improves further rather
than showing the deterioration seen in the 512-patch control.

### GT-matched geometry (millimetres; lower is better)

| Representation | Train raw guide | Val raw guide | Train endpoint-neutral guide | Val endpoint-neutral guide |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Chords | 0.96148 | 0.95368 | 0.51414 | 0.50138 |
| Residual/full, 512 patches | 0.78370 | 0.97352 | 0.25340 | 0.53300 |
| Residual/full, 10k patches | 0.92181 | 0.91881 | 0.47632 | 0.47094 |

These are the same 8,454/2,059 GT-positive pairs as before, independent of
decoded edge acceptance. New validation raw guide error improves **3.66%**
against chords, and endpoint-neutral error **6.07%**. The localized-endpoint
subset (619 validation branches) also improves: 5.83% raw / 6.57%
endpoint-neutral. Native validation node F1 / edge F1 remains
**0.90753 / 0.85858**. Connectivity did not improve; this gain is geometric.

### Interpretation and next decision

- Broader patch coverage with fewer repetitions at equal update budget reduces
  the observed overfitting and yields a modest validation curvature gain. This
  supports usable geometric information in the frozen detector features under
  residual supervision; the earlier 512-patch failures do not establish that
  these features are intrinsically insufficient.
- This is one seed and 128 validation patches from 13 subjects. Endpoint-neutral
  mean error improves, but only about 49.9% of branches improve individually;
  benefit is not uniform. No statistical significance or held-out test claim.
  Centerline guides remain imperfect references.
- It still does **not** establish that the original 300-epoch collapse was
  caused only by its training setup, nor isolate a particular setting. This
  run starts from a successful detector, freezes it, and uses residual targets;
  the scratch experiment changed all these conditions. It also does not prove
  residual supervision is necessary: no 10k frozen absolute-target arm was run.
- Recommended next decision: a bounded continuation of this frozen residual
  head, retaining the same monitoring, to assess whether gains grow beyond two
  data passes before risking detector unfreezing. This would test optimization
  budget, not directly identify the scratch-collapse trigger. Any later joint
  continuation should include the matched graph-only control required by the
  original investigation plan. **No new jobs launched in this results review.**

Compact results, history, comparison CSV and completion audit are preserved in
`experiments/spline_learning/metadata/frozen-breadth/`. Full model, branch-level
metrics, projections and offline W&B run `b4exe3tv` remain in the run directory.

## Authorized parallel follow-up: budget and objective

The user approved continuation and requested another diagnostic in parallel.
Training the whole model from scratch remains excluded at this decision point.
Prepare two independent jobs with unchanged detector/BN, eight controls, 10k
training patches, fixed 512 training monitoring cases and 128 validation cases:

| Arm | Initialization | Objective | New updates | Comparison |
|---|---|---|---:|---|
| `residual_continue` | Full model weights from completed 816293 | Residual | 10,000 (15,000 cumulative) | Its own starting metrics and completed 816293 |
| `absolute_full` | Same original straight detector and fresh head initialization as 816293 | Absolute controls | 5,000 | Completed 816293 at the identical 5,000-update budget |

The parallel absolute arm tests whether residual supervision helps once data
breadth is matched. Do not compare it directly against the longer continuation
as if they had equal optimization budgets. Initial tensors, batch-order hash,
matching, detector digest, LR, weight and dataset membership are checked against
816293 for the absolute arm. Its only intended training difference is objective.

The prior checkpoint saved model weights but **not AdamW moments**. Therefore
the residual continuation explicitly restarts AdamW and the seeded loader
shuffle, with unchanged constant LR 7e-5 and weight decay 1e-4. This is a weight
continuation, not an exact interrupted-run resume, and its effect cannot be
attributed exclusively to extra updates. Source checkpoint loading is strict;
model/loss configurations must match, detector digest and evaluation assignment
hashes must remain fixed. Source and new checkpoints remain separate. New final
checkpoints also save optimizer/scheduler states and cumulative update count.

Both use the existing reusable runner. The only additions are optional saved
evaluation membership and optional checkpoint weight continuation with explicit
provenance; no model/loss/matcher modifications. Configs:
`configs/spline_frozen_residual_continue.yaml` and
`configs/spline_frozen_absolute_10k_pilot.yaml`. Submission:
`cluster/jean_zay/spline_frozen_followup.slurm`, array tasks 0/1 respectively.
Each gets one H100 and a 30-minute limit; each runs a separate three-update GPU
smoke before its fresh trial. Monitoring and same-endpoint chord comparisons
remain unchanged; continuation full geometry is evaluated at 0/5k/10k new
updates, absolute at 0/1k/5k. Offline W&B and projections remain enabled.

Output root: `runs/frozen_followup_20261009/`, separate arm and smoke directories.
After results, decide whether longer frozen learning helps and whether the
absolute objective damages shape generalization. No unfreezing, new architecture,
scratch training, or 300-epoch run is part of this submission.

Submitted as **817904_0** (residual continuation) and **817904_1** (absolute control), independently schedulable on one H100 each. Five CPU tests, configuration/checkpoint compatibility, fixed evaluation-membership and syntax checks passed. GPU smoke is queued within each task. Logs: `experiments/spline_learning/logs/frozen-followup-817904_<task>.{out,err}`. Compact submission evidence: `experiments/spline_learning/metadata/frozen-followup/submission.json`. No completed result claimed.

## Parallel follow-up completed: 817904_0/1

Both completed with exit 0:0: residual continuation **17m51s**, absolute
**13m58s**. Comparison audit verified identical training/evaluation membership,
fixed detector digest, sensitivity, matching, and native node/edge scores.
Continuation's initial decoded and matched geometry metrics exactly match the
source checkpoint's final metrics. Absolute and original residual 5k runs have
identical initialized tensors and actual training batch sequence.

### Decoded curve F1 on the fixed evaluation cases

| Objective / cumulative head updates | Train subset | Validation |
|---|---:|---:|
| Same-endpoint chords | 0.64812 | 0.65540 |
| Absolute / 5k | 0.66996 | 0.67461 |
| Residual / 5k (816293) | 0.67275 | 0.67865 |
| Residual / 10k (intermediate evaluation) | 0.69014 | 0.68682 |
| Residual / 15k (continuation final) | 0.70144 | 0.68995 |

### GT-matched validation geometry, all 2,059 pairs

| Objective / updates | Raw guide error mm | Endpoint-neutral guide error mm | Endpoint-neutral improvement vs chord |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Chords | 0.95368 | 0.50138 | — |
| Absolute / 5k | 0.92239 | 0.51964 | **−3.64%** |
| Residual / 5k | 0.91881 | 0.47094 | **+6.07%** |
| Residual / 15k | 0.89677 | 0.44987 | **+10.27%** |

Final residual raw guide error improves 5.97% against chords. On the 619
validation pairs with both endpoints within 1 mm, raw guide error improves
9.47% and endpoint-neutral error 12.02%. Native node/edge F1 remains
0.90753 / 0.85858; there is no connectivity change. Training endpoint-neutral
error improves 15.15% for the final residual model, versus a 2.36% worsening
for absolute supervision. The intermediate 10k point is an evaluation, not a
separately saved model checkpoint.

### What is now supported

1. **Keep residual supervision for shape learning.** At the matched 5k budget,
   decoded F1 differs modestly (+0.00404 for residual), but residual improves
   endpoint-neutral shape while absolute worsens it. Absolute fitting improves
   raw geometry without improving transferred residual shape, consistent with
   learning some compensation for localization error. This is not a significance
   claim, nor evidence that absolute losses cannot work in any other setting.
2. **Longer frozen learning improves validation here.** Validation F1 progresses
   0.67865 → 0.68682 → 0.68995, with a smaller later gain. Improvement is not
   restricted to training cases. The continuation restarted AdamW/shuffle, so
   the effect cannot be isolated to extra updates alone. Shape gains are not
   uniform: about 50.7% of validation branches improve endpoint-neutral error.
3. **Frozen pretrained features can support useful curved geometry.** The
   previous small-subset overfitting was not a demonstration of an inherently
   unusable spline head or representation. The causal trigger for original
   scratch encoder collapse is still unproven, and this does not justify a
   new scratch or 300-epoch run.

Next research decision: keep this residual frozen model as the reference. If
the next priority is connectivity and the joint-optimization hypothesis, a
short controlled unfreezing experiment against matched graph-only continuation
is now more informative than another unpaired long run. The exact unfreezing
scope and treatment of endpoint-feature gradients should be specified before
submission; no such job was launched during this results review. All results
remain single-seed diagnostic validation, not held-out test results.

Evidence and comparison audit saved in
`experiments/spline_learning/metadata/frozen-followup/`; full models, metrics,
projections and offline W&B data remain under `runs/frozen_followup_20261009/`.
