# SyntheticMRI: paired scratch comparison, 300 epochs

## Decision (2026-10-06)

The user requested two scratch runs, each on exactly 10,000 vessel patches for
300 epochs. They clarified that the old representation should also use only
junctions, terminations, and boundary nodes, without intermediate degree-two
nodes. Consequently this experiment isolates **straight versus spline edge
geometry**, rather than testing degree-two node removal. A degree-two baseline
is a useful later experiment and has not been submitted as a third job.

## Shared population and supervision

- SyntheticMRI only; no plants; original subject-disjoint splits preserved.
- 10,000 train patches from the available training subjects: retain the existing
  9,709 compatible patches and add the next 291 eligible patches in the same
  seed-364505 hash ranking. Closed/parallel branches remain excluded; no quality
  or model-score filtering. Never fill training from validation/test.
- Keep the existing 1,952 validation and 13,071 test patches exactly unchanged.
- Both arms consume identical MRI, masks, VTP endpoint nodes, and edge pairs.
  The straight arm decodes each edge as a chord. The spline arm additionally
  consumes eight fitted controls per branch (six internal predicted controls).
- Both preserve existing boundary supervision: voxel-cell crop bounds, snap
  to the first/last existing inside guide samples within each component, with
  the recorded exact-intersection fallback for undersampled components.
- Original full generator guides are uncertain supervision, not perfect anatomy.
- Common exclusions mean these results apply to the eligible population;
  closed/parallel branches are not evaluated by this experiment.

## Training protocol

- Entire model initialized from scratch: no pretrained checkpoint and no resume.
- Shared seed 364505; verify all common initial model weights are identical.
- Same 120 object queries and two relation tokens; same encoder/decoder and
  original edge existence head. Extra spline MLP enabled only in spline arm.
- Native 64³ MRI, batch 4, validation batch 4, no augmentation in either arm.
- AdamW: learning rate 7e-5, weight decay 1e-4, betas (0.9,0.999), epsilon 1e-8.
  One warmup epoch; polynomial schedule power 0.9; 300 epochs, no early stopping.
  Exactly 2,500 batches per epoch, 750,000 optimizer steps per arm.
- Shared loss weights: boxes 3, class 4, cardinality 0.8, nodes 2, edges 6.
  Same edge focal classification and candidate/balancing policy.
- Spline arm adds control loss weight **1.4739989612791453**, retaining the
  previously recorded training-only calibration. It has not been tuned on the
  new scratch results or held-out test set. Scratch-specific tuning is a later
  sensitivity study if necessary, not a hidden difference in this first pair.
- Validation every five epochs; select best checkpoint using the weighted sum
  of the **five common graph losses**, excluding spline loss in both arms.
  Keep the final/latest full-state checkpoint too. Full validation totals have
  different meanings between arms and must not be compared as one metric.
- Four fixed validation subjects/examples use the same MRI/mask/full-guide
  projections. Old predictions display chords, new predictions display splines.
- W&B compute logging is offline, with distinct runs in a common comparison
  group; sync from the login node, avoiding the previous compute connectivity
  failure. Metrics and validation images remain saved locally before upload.

## Storage and scripts

Targets and memberships:
`$SCRATCH/experiments/gnbm/spline_learning/scratch_comparison_10k_300ep/`.
`comparison-manifest.json` records exact IDs, source metadata and extra exclusions.
Each arm has its own dataset root; shared volumes/graphs are symlinked, not copied.

Code on the `representation` branch:
- `scripts/prepare_scratch_comparison.py`: extend eligible train membership and pair roots.
- `scripts/check_scratch_comparison.py`: config, exact IDs, real validation batch,
  control shapes, common initialization and projection checks.
- `configs/scratch_comparison_{old,spline}_300ep.yaml`.
- `cluster/jean_zay/train_scratch_comparison.slurm` selected with `COMPARISON_ARM`.

The immutable verified runtime archive is staged job-locally for both jobs.
Each requests one H100 and 20 hours. Previous spline throughput suggests roughly
17–19 hours per run, excluding queue time; this is an estimate, not a guarantee.
If interrupted by the time limit, resume the full latest state to complete the
same 300-epoch protocol; never restart silently with a changed schedule.

## Interpretation and next steps

10,000 patches are sufficient for an informative first paired experiment;
they are correlated crops from 64 training subjects, not 10,000 independent
observations. A single seed does not establish statistical significance.
Evaluate both arms on the unchanged held-out subjects with the same decoding
thresholds, endpoint/branch connectivity, physical curve distance and tortuosity.
Always report unmatched branches/coverage along with matched curve errors.
Compare both best-by-common-validation and final-epoch checkpoints explicitly.
Use subject-level intervals and repeated seeds before paper-level conclusions.
Then consider the degree-two-node baseline, augmentation and spline-loss
sensitivity without retroactively changing this pair's protocol.

Submission IDs and preflight outcome will be recorded after submission.

## Preparation checks

Preparation finished with the requested 10,000 / 1,952 / 13,071 membership.
The next 323 ranked training candidates yielded 311 compatible and 12 excluded;
the first 291 compatible IDs were retained. Endpoint graphs have at most 54
nodes, fitting the common 120-query budget. All MRI/mask/graph triplets, exact
arm memberships, one real validation batch per arm, cache-control shapes,
shared initial weights and projection generation were checked.

An older temporary package copy contained an incomplete SymPy installation.
Fresh archive staging resolved it; staging now also uses the protected cluster
module interpreter, keeping mutable venv fallback packages out of import search.
The two jobs use the same checksum-verified archive and interpreter selection.

## Submitted jobs

- Straight-edge scratch arm: **708757** (`scratch_old_graph_10k_300ep`).
- Eight-control spline scratch arm: **708759** (`scratch_spline_k8_10k_300ep`).
- Stable implementation commit: `dacb858` on `representation`.
- Final CPU preflight passed with the protected interpreter and fresh archive;
  full training entrypoint imports also passed.
- Job IDs, manifest checksum and verification are recorded in
  `DenseVesselGraph/experiments/spline_learning/metadata/scratch-comparison-jobs.json`.
- Both are independent Slurm jobs, with no dependency on the other's completion.
  Compute W&B logs are offline and need login-node syncing for cloud visibility.

Submission check: both jobs are **PENDING (Priority)**; neither has started yet.

## Third arm requested

The user subsequently requested the intermediate-node baseline and selected the
compact adaptive version. This supersedes deferring that variant to a follow-up.
See [the degree-two protocol](adaptive-degree2-scratch-comparison.md). The first
two jobs and their targets/configurations are unchanged.

## 2026-10-07: spline filesystem interruption and recovery

Spline job 708759 stopped after epoch 171 during a training DataLoader file
stat, with filesystem error 108 (`Cannot send after transport endpoint shutdown`)
on `sample_000128_0705_graph.vtp`. A subsequent real VTP read succeeded. This
evidence supports a storage-access failure; the underlying storage cause is
not known. No target file was changed, removed or replaced.

`latest_checkpoint.pt` was fully read and verified at epoch 171 / iteration
427,500, with model, optimizer, scheduler, RNG and trainer state present.
Recovery job **721673** uses `--resume` to continue at epoch 172 under the same
300-epoch config, data, loss weights and schedule. The original baseline job
708757 remains running (observed epoch 223 during diagnosis). Stable recovery
implementation commit: `edb30bc`. This restores a scratch-trained run; it does
not initialize from an unrelated pretrained model.

Recovery startup verified: **721673 is RUNNING**. The offline tracker started
with the original run ID after strict model/optimizer/scheduler/RNG restoration
(the tracker is constructed only after the resume load succeeds). It continues
the same scratch experiment from epoch 172. Adaptive **709924 is also RUNNING**
after verification job 721618 completed successfully.

## Held-out tests and common representation-independent evaluation

Straight-edge job 708757 completed all 300 epochs (13:29:14, exit 0).
Test job **730103** evaluates both the validation-selected best checkpoint
(epoch 35, common validation graph loss 2.629155270050692) and the final
300-epoch checkpoint on the exact same 13,071 held-out IDs, saving predictions.
No test-based threshold tuning or checkpoint selection is performed.

Native box-based node/edge metrics remain diagnostics against each arm's own
native targets. They are not the primary comparison with adaptive degree-two
nodes. The common protocol (`shared-guides-v2`) reads saved predictions and uses
identical full generator guides, target endpoints, and physical units for every
arm:

- Contract all degree-two chains in predictions and targets while retaining
  their geometry. Straight graphs retain chords; adaptive graphs retain their
  piecewise-linear paths; splines retain sampled curves reconstructed from the
  predicted controls. No fitted GT controls are substituted into predictions.
- Common anchor F1 and Branch F1: one-to-one role-aware physical matching
  within 1 mm. Report branch coverage, false/missing branches, component (β0)
  and cycle (β1) errors and topological-anchor count error.
- Whole-vessel curve precision/recall/F1: all predicted and reference branches,
  fixed 1 mm tolerance, uniform 0.25 mm arc-length sampling. This includes
  missing and extra geometry without requiring a successful branch match.
- Symmetric guide distance and tortuosity error on topology-matched branches;
  always report their branch coverage alongside conditional shape errors.
- Report raw predicted nodes, predicted degree-two nodes, topological anchors,
  junctions/endpoints/isolates, and internal spline controls separately. Crop
  boundary endpoints are included in endpoint counts. Controls are additional
  geometric parameters, not additional anatomical objects or object tokens.

Both native and common results are retained. Common v2 results use separate
`common-v2-summary.json` / `common-v2-per-patch.csv` files so earlier metrics
remain available. Source guides are shared, uncertain references; agreement
with them is not independent anatomical validation. Common metrics preserve
subdivision invariance and were checked on straight subdivision, curved spline
geometry, missing vessels, and the existing branch-connectivity regression tests.

The common scorer is representation-independent and uses only saved prediction
JSON and existing caches. It needs CPU scoring, not another GPU prediction run.
Per-patch source IDs remain available for later subject-level uncertainty estimates.

GPU test job 730103 **COMPLETED (exit 0)**: best and final each evaluated all
13,071 held-out patches. CPU-only job **733084** scores both saved exports with
the finalized `shared-guides-v2` protocol, preserving earlier result files.
No new GPU inference is required. Stable common-protocol commit: `9980965`;
14 focused branch/geometry regression tests passed.

## Straight-edge held-out results (13,071 patches)

CPU scoring 733084 completed successfully. Common protocol uses fixed 1 mm
anchor/curve tolerances and 0.25 mm arc-length sampling.

| Metric | Validation-selected epoch 35 | Final epoch 300 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Native node F1 | 0.5779 | 0.6534 |
| Native edge F1 | 0.4499 | 0.5449 |
| Common anchor F1 | 0.0811 | 0.1353 |
| Common Branch F1 | 0.0033 | 0.0114 |
| Common branch coverage | 0.27% | 0.94% |
| Whole-vessel Curve F1 | 0.1650 | 0.2305 |
| Mean predicted topological anchors | 15.79 | 15.49 |

Reference topological anchors average 21.39 per patch. The final model predicts
21.35 raw nodes, but only 15.49 remain topological anchors after degree-two
contraction; raw count agreement does not establish correct topology.
Matched-branch guide errors are 0.643/0.671 mm, applying only to the very small
0.27%/0.94% recovered subset, not the complete vessel graphs.
These independent physical scores indicate weak topology/geometry recovery for
this baseline. Native box-based F1 alone would overstate its reconstruction
quality. The final checkpoint scores higher on these tests despite higher
validation loss; the validation-selected checkpoint remains epoch 35. Do not
change checkpoint selection based on held-out test results. Spline/adaptive
conclusions await their completed training and identical held-out scoring.

## Spline scratch training completed; held-out tests submitted

Recovery 721673 completed successfully, finishing epoch 300 / iteration 750,000.
The original scratch run and its recovery together complete the unchanged
300-epoch protocol. The common validation-loss-selected checkpoint is epoch 170.
GPU test job **737021** evaluates epoch 170 and the final epoch-300 checkpoint
on the identical 13,071 held-out IDs. Saved predictions are scored with the same
`shared-guides-v2` topology, whole-curve geometry and object-count protocol as
the straight baseline. No checkpoint/threshold selection uses test metrics.
Actual spline geometry uses predicted endpoints and predicted internal controls,
never target controls. Native and common summaries are saved under
`scratch_spline_k8_10k_300ep/test/{best,final}`.
Stable generic evaluation update: `120419e`.

# Three scratch trainings: completed held-out comparison

All three train from scratch for 300 epochs on the same 10,000 vessel patches, with 1,952 validation and 13,071 held-out test patches. All use 120 object queries, batch 4, the same seed and shared optimizer/schedule. The spline arm adds its head and fixed geometry loss weight 1.4739989612791453.

The source guide paths and masks remain uncertain references; agreement with them does not establish anatomical accuracy.

## Checkpoint selection

| Representation | Validation-loss-selected epoch | Final epoch |
|---|---:|---:|
| Straight edges | 35 | 300 |
| B-spline, 8 controls | 170 | 300 |
| Adaptive degree-2 | 25 | 300 |

“Best” means the lowest weighted validation graph loss (boxes/class/cardinality/nodes/edges, weights 3/4/0.8/2/6), not highest reconstruction F1. No checkpoint or threshold was selected using test scores. Final and selected checkpoints are both reported; these measurements do not justify retrospective test-based model selection.

## Shared evaluation protocol

Degree-two chains are contracted while retaining their full predicted geometry. All arms use the same target endpoint topology and full guides, physical matching at 1 mm, and curve sampling every 0.25 mm. Anchor matching is role-aware (junction, endpoint, isolate); virtual pure-cycle anchors are used only for topology. Whole-curve precision/recall/F1 include missing and extra geometry. Matched guide distance and tortuosity apply only to recovered branches and must be read with coverage. Dataset-level anchor/branch F1 are micro counts; curve precision/recall use pooled arc-length samples. Count/error entries are patch means.

## Final checkpoints, epoch 300

| Metric | Straight edges | B-spline, 8 controls | Adaptive degree-2 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Anchor F1 ↑ | 0.135344 | 0.000084 | 0.103053 |
| Branch F1 ↑ | 0.011416 | 0.000000 | 0.005017 |
| Branch coverage ↑ | 0.940% | 0.000% | 0.491% |
| Whole-curve precision ↑ | 0.268873 | 0.003784 | 0.276281 |
| Whole-curve recall ↑ | 0.201725 | 0.000825 | 0.223516 |
| Whole-curve F1 ↑ | 0.230508 | 0.001355 | 0.247114 |
| Matched guide distance, mm ↓ | 0.67129 | N/A | 0.57151 |
| Matched tortuosity error ↓ | 0.02085 | N/A | 0.01900 |
| Absolute component-count error (β₀) ↓ | 2.58297 | 29.95004 | 3.50409 |
| Absolute loop-count error (β₁) ↓ | 2.13909 | 0.02930 | 4.35827 |
| Topological-node count error ↓ | 5.98187 | 15.63408 | 3.52903 |

## Validation-loss-selected checkpoints

| Metric | Straight edges | B-spline, 8 controls | Adaptive degree-2 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Anchor F1 ↑ | 0.081095 | 0.000053 | 0.060244 |
| Branch F1 ↑ | 0.003307 | 0.000000 | 0.001926 |
| Branch coverage ↑ | 0.270% | 0.000% | 0.173% |
| Whole-curve precision ↑ | 0.235393 | 0.003950 | 0.222295 |
| Whole-curve recall ↑ | 0.127004 | 0.001234 | 0.113864 |
| Whole-curve F1 ↑ | 0.164989 | 0.001881 | 0.150592 |
| Matched guide distance, mm ↓ | 0.64255 | N/A | 0.56546 |
| Matched tortuosity error ↓ | 0.01830 | N/A | 0.01679 |
| Absolute component-count error (β₀) ↓ | 4.35590 | 28.95004 | 7.28085 |
| Absolute loop-count error (β₁) ↓ | 2.85923 | 0.02930 | 3.17298 |
| Topological-node count error ↓ | 5.75977 | 17.62107 | 3.28070 |

## Predicted object and geometry counts: final checkpoints

| Metric | Straight edges | B-spline, 8 controls | Adaptive degree-2 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Raw predicted nodes | 21.34840 | 38.00000 | 28.85456 |
| Predicted degree-2 nodes | 5.85403 | 1.00000 | 9.59406 |
| Topological nodes (includes isolates) | 15.49438 | 37.00000 | 19.26050 |
| Junctions | 3.14513 | 0.00000 | 5.78930 |
| Endpoints (includes crop boundaries) | 10.11032 | 4.00000 | 11.45643 |
| Isolated nodes | 2.23893 | 33.00000 | 2.01477 |

Shared reference means: 21.39255 topological anchors, 5.65710 junctions, 15.70056 endpoints and 16.37189 branches per patch. Spline control points are geometry parameters, not object tokens or anatomical junctions. A predicted degree-two node is contracted regardless of the intended native node role; false degree-two structure remains visible in raw counts and native diagnostics. Count agreement alone does not imply correct connectivity.

## Native diagnostics: final checkpoints

| Metric | Straight edges | B-spline, 8 controls | Adaptive degree-2 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Native node F1 ↑ | 0.653409 | 0.000000 | 0.567310 |
| Native edge F1 ↑ | 0.544920 | 0.004376 | 0.511229 |
| Native target nodes / patch | 21.39255 | 21.39255 | 28.41213 |
| Native target edges / patch | 16.37189 | 16.37189 | 23.39148 |

## Native diagnostics: validation-loss-selected checkpoints

| Metric | Straight edges | B-spline, 8 controls | Adaptive degree-2 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Native node F1 ↑ | 0.577861 | 0.000000 | 0.489399 |
| Native edge F1 ↑ | 0.449901 | 0.005019 | 0.422493 |

Native node/edge metrics use each arm’s own targets. The adaptive arm has extra degree-two target nodes/edges; native scores are therefore diagnostics, not the representation-independent headline comparison.

## Interpretation and limitations

- All three current runs show weak physical topology recovery under the fixed 1 mm protocol. Small conditional shape errors describe very few recovered branches.

- The final adaptive model has higher whole-curve F1 (0.24711 versus 0.23051 for straight edges), while straight edges have higher anchor and Branch F1. No single representation wins every relevant quantity, and no statistical-significance claim is made.

- The current spline run is degenerate: node/branch counts are constant across all 13,071 patches and no branches are recovered. Saved prediction checks across two distinct test subjects showed identical edge indices and coordinate differences of only approximately 7.6e-6 mm. Coordinates are not bit-identical. This is a warning about this training/evaluation outcome, not proof that spline representation learning is infeasible.

- Spline guide/tortuosity errors are N/A because zero branches match, not because the geometry is perfect. Its small loop-count error is also trivial: predicting essentially no cycles does not imply correct vessels.

- Final checkpoints outperform loss-selected checkpoints on several measures. The current validation-loss selection is poorly aligned with reconstruction metrics; a future validation-only topology/geometry selection protocol must be predefined.

- This is a single-seed comparison using correlated patches from 14 test subjects and the common eligible subset. Subject-level uncertainty estimates and repeated seeds remain necessary for paper-level claims.

## Next steps

Diagnose the near-input-independent spline predictions before launching another large spline run or deciding between spline families. Check the input dependence, shared-head gradients, and scratch-versus-finetuning geometry-loss calibration. Keep these current results as the reproducible baseline. Validate any revised checkpoint-selection policy on validation subjects only, then repeat controlled runs and common held-out scoring.

## Files and reproducibility

Full-precision CSV: `/lustre/fswork/projects/rech/vnc/upz25mj/projects/DenseVesselGraph/experiments/spline_learning/metadata/comparison/comparison.csv`. Source checksums: `/lustre/fswork/projects/rech/vnc/upz25mj/projects/DenseVesselGraph/experiments/spline_learning/metadata/comparison/provenance.json`.

Underlying results: `/lustre/fsn1/projects/rech/vnc/upz25mj/experiments/gnbm/spline_learning/runs/scratch_{old_graph,spline_k8,adaptive_degree2}_10k_300ep/test/{best,final}/`.

Regenerate from the representation repository: `python scripts/build_scratch_comparison_tables.py`. This reads existing results and changes no dataset, checkpoint or metric source files.

# Scratch geometry with detector gradients isolated

Authorized after scratch run 885337 showed learning in the graph-only control
but near-zero image sensitivity and node F1 in the local-spline arm. Initial
weights and actual target-batch hashes matched. Those runs used geometry
gradients through tokens, with predicted endpoints already detached.

## Single intervention

Use the existing `graph_only` gradient route in the spline criterion: detach
object/relation tokens as well as predicted endpoint coordinates when forming
the geometry loss. CNN image values and sampling coordinates were already
detached by the local geometry module. Graph losses still train every active
CNN/transformer/node/edge parameter; spline losses still train both geometry
MLPs. This is **not a frozen detector** and loads **no pretrained weights**.

Reuse the completed `scratch_local_pilot_20261010_attempt2/graph_control`
reference. Only the positive spline loss with isolated gradients differs from
that control; versus the failed local-spline arm, only the token gradient route
changes. There is no reason to repeat either completed reference run.

## Matched conditions

- Same random seed 364505, eight controls, image sampler, residual targets,
  Hungarian matcher, 10k training patches and batch 4.
- Same AdamW LR 7e-5, weight decay 1e-4, 2,500-update warmup and original
  polynomial schedule horizon. Hard stop at 25,000 updates, approximately 10
  data passes; this is not a full 300-epoch run.
- Spline weight 1.4739989612791453; both spline modules train from step one.
- Normal CNN/BN training; saved BN statistics for evaluation, no recalibration.
- Same 512 training-monitor and 128 validation cases, monitored at 5k/15k/25k;
  losses and fixed-probe sensitivity every 1k. Geometry metrics remain separate
  from decoded graph metrics and are compared with identical-endpoint chords.
- Intermediate 5k/15k and final25k checkpoints; offline W&B and projections.
- Before starting: compare reference initial-state hash, configs (excluding spline
  loss weight), data/evaluation membership, update budget and schedule metadata.
  After training: assert actual target-batch hash matches the completed control.
- A targeted real train-step test verifies that three isolated-geometry updates
  change the head but leave detector parameters/BN buffers identical to the
  graph-only control. Existing local gradient-routing checks are reused.
- Independent three-update GPU smoke before the full run, starting afresh from
  random weights afterward; no smoke-trained weights are reused.

## Interpretation

Detector learning should track the graph-only reference closely. If it avoids
collapse, this supports the remaining token-mediated geometry gradient route
as the destabilizing intervention in the earlier experiment. It does not explain
why those gradients harm optimization internally, or prove every coupled setup
fails. If detector behavior differs strongly, first verify routing and pairing.

If curvature also improves, isolated concurrent learning becomes a candidate
scratch recipe. If curvature fails while detector learning is healthy, poor
localization and changing early image features remain likely difficulties;
a later graph-first warm-up would then be a justified next question. Common
branch recovery was still poor in the control at 25k, so modest geometry progress
would not establish a usable graph extractor. No additional follow-up auto-runs.

## Reproduction

Config: `configs/spline_scratch_detached_pilot.yaml`.
Submission: `cluster/jean_zay/spline_scratch_detached.slurm`.
Existing runner `scripts/train_spline_weight_pilot.py` now accepts
`scratch_gradient_route` (default retains `tokens_only`) and optional
`scratch_reference_run` pairing checks. No matcher or architecture changes.

Outputs:
`/lustre/fsn1/projects/rech/vnc/upz25mj/experiments/gnbm/spline_learning/runs/scratch_detached_pilot_20261011/`
with `detached_spline` and `smoke-detached_spline` directories.

Submitted **903323**. Five targeted CPU tests passed, including detector/BN equivalence while the isolated head learns. Syntax/diff checks passed. GPU smoke pending at submission. Expected runtime around 45–50 minutes after allocation, based on matched 25k runs; three-hour ceiling. Logs: `experiments/spline_learning/logs/scratch-detached-903323.{out,err}`.

## Completed result and narrow follow-up (2026-10-12)

903323 completed 25,000 updates in 45:11 (exit 0:0). Initialization and batch-order
hashes match the graph-only reference. Final diagnostic validation (128 cases):

| Arm | Node F1 | Edge F1 | Curve F1 | Memory sensitivity |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Graph-only control | 0.23642 | 0.19574 | 0.05641 | 0.89433 |
| Geometry through tokens | 0.00000 | 0.00828 | 0.00400 | 0.00000338 |
| Geometry detached | 0.20566 | 0.19278 | 0.05605 | 0.85032 |

Isolation avoids the observed collapse, but does not produce useful branch
recovery yet: validation branch F1 remains zero. Endpoint-neutral guide error
0.49984 mm versus chords 0.50138 mm gives only 0.31% relative improvement. This
is not evidence that scratch geometry is solved. The detached detector does
not exactly match the graph-only reference despite paired inputs; numerical
variation is plausible but has not been established as the explanation.

User authorized needed tests. Submitted short GPU diagnostic **948360**:

1. At the coupled scratch 5k checkpoint, compare geometry gradients into all
   active detector parameters under token vs detached routes; assert detached
   gradients are zero on the real GPU model.
2. Restore identical model/optimizer/scheduler/RNG state and take three real
   updates for two repeated graph controls and one detached-geometry condition.
   Compare detector/BN changes against the repeated-control numerical variation.
   Controls use the same 5k optimizer state, including spline momentum; geometry
   head movement in these short zero-loss controls is not a detector-gradient leak.
3. Probe all three final checkpoints with saved BN statistics versus current
   batch statistics using the original fixed four images. Restore buffers after
   each probe. This measures image sensitivity only, not full dataset accuracy.

These are bounded checks, not another 25k run. No checkpoint is overwritten.
The initial 25k outcomes support a role for geometry feedback but do not prove
an internal mechanism or exclude BN-mediated changes. Resolve these checks
before choosing a longer graph-first/warm-up experiment.

Code: `scripts/diagnose_scratch_isolation.py` and
`cluster/jean_zay/spline_scratch_isolation_checks.slurm`.
Output: `runs/scratch_isolation_checks_20261012/summary.json` under the same
scratch experiment root. Logs: `experiments/spline_learning/logs/isolation-checks-948360.{out,err}`.
Python/Slurm syntax checked; the submitted small GPU diagnostic is itself the
real-data correctness test, with a 20-minute ceiling.

## Isolation/BN diagnostic results (2026-10-12)

Job **948360** completed successfully in **1:07**.

- Real-model detached geometry gradient into the detector: exactly zero across
  all active tensors. Token-coupled geometry has nonzero gradients in 569 tensors.
- Same-start three-update detector differences: repeated graph control relative
  L2 1.153e-6 versus detached/control 1.253e-6. This supports numerical variation
  as an explanation for short-run differences; it does not quantitatively explain
  every difference accumulated across 25k updates or establish seed robustness.
- The collapsed model's memory sensitivity stays near 3.4e-6 with either saved
  BN statistics or current batch statistics (3.379e-6 versus 3.451e-6).
  Graph control remains about 0.894 under both; detached remains 0.850/0.828.
  Thus changing inference BN statistics does not restore image sensitivity on
  the fixed four-image probe. It does not exclude a role for BN during training.
- At the 5k checkpoint on this one batch, weighted geometry gradient norm is
  0.002369 versus graph 15.582 (ratio 0.000152). No evidence here for a simply
  overwhelming geometry gradient; this late probe cannot describe earlier
  gradients, layer-specific alignment or nonlinear optimization trajectories.

Together with the matched scratch runs, the evidence points to harmful early
geometry feedback through shared tokens under this setup. The exact internal
mechanism remains unresolved. Correct detachment avoids collapse but curves
remain near chords while scratch node/branch localization is still poor.

Next proposed research decision: extend graph-only and detached scratch training
with matched budgets to see whether stronger localization allows curvature
learning without external pretraining. Do not select a coupled scratch recipe
or assume eventual success from this short test. No new jobs submitted in this
result review. Evidence copy: `metadata/local-geometry/scratch-isolation-results.json`.

# Scratch extension to 300 epochs — 2026-10-12

## Question and decision

User explicitly authorized extending the successful graph-only and detached
B-spline scratch pilots to 300 total epochs. Neither uses an external pretrained
detector. The collapsed token-coupled arm is not extended. The question is whether
curvature learning becomes useful as scratch graph localization improves, while
geometry gradients remain isolated from graph learning.

The preceding [isolation diagnostics](scratch-detached-geometry.md) verified zero
detector gradients from the detached geometry objective. This experiment tests
longer-term learning and stability; it does not identify the exact mechanism of
the earlier coupled collapse, nor demonstrate that curves improve connectivity.

## Fixed conditions and continuation

- Same 10,000 SyntheticMRI training patches, batch 4, no augmentation, seed 364505.
- Same ordered 128 validation and 512 training monitoring cases; memberships
  verified identical across source arms. Full validation remains 1,952 cases.
- Sources: `scratch_local_pilot_20261010_attempt2/graph_control/model.pt` and
  `scratch_detached_pilot_20261011/detached_spline/model.pt` under the existing
  `spline_learning/runs` root. Both completed 25,000 updates / 10 epochs.
- Continue weights **and AdamW moments**, no new warmup. Preserve the original
  750,000-update polynomial schedule, base LR 7e-5, power 0.9, weight decay 1e-4,
  2,500 warmup updates. Existing scheduler formula is unchanged.
- Control spline weight 0, `tokens_only` route. Detached spline weight
  1.4739989612791453, `graph_only` route: detector receives graph losses;
  residual geometry head learns from detached tokens/endpoints/local CNN values.
  Same eight-control B-spline head and local geometry implementation.
- BN updates normally during training; evaluation uses saved running statistics.
- Original checkpoints did not store RNG/sampler state. Both extensions restart
  their random/shuffle streams identically. This is **not** an exact uninterrupted
  continuation of the old random stream. New stage checkpoints preserve Python,
  NumPy, CPU/CUDA torch and loader generator states at exhausted epoch boundaries.
  CUDA arithmetic remains nondeterministic as established by the earlier probe.

## Monitoring and selection

Validation losses, graph metrics, same-endpoint chord comparison, fixed projection
images and image sensitivity every 5 epochs. Fixed 512-case training geometry and
separate GT-matched geometry on train/validation every 20 epochs and at stage ends.
This reduces monitoring frequency versus the short pilots; losses and update
budgets are unchanged. W&B uses the existing offline workflow, group
`spline-scratch-extend300-20261012`.

Save rolling `latest.pt`, final `model.pt` for each stage, and `best.pt`. Best is
selected by **highest validation common branch F1, then native edge F1**; the
source checkpoint is included and the best carries across stages. No selection
on total loss or the test set. Scheduled full validation evaluates both best and
final models, preserving the distinction between GT-matched shape metrics and
full decoded-graph performance. It produces comparison tables and a portable
six-case HTML gallery using existing evaluation code. These are validation
results, not an unbiased held-out test claim.

## Jobs, outputs and reproducibility

The partition allows 20 hours per job. Each model therefore uses two dependent
stages on one H100 each:

| Array | Task 0 | Task 1 | Dependency |
|---|---|---|---|
| 949063 | control, epochs 11–150 | detached, epochs 11–150 | three-update GPU resume smoke in each task |
| 949065 | control, epochs 151–300 | detached, epochs 151–300 | corresponding task in 949063 succeeds |
| 949071 | four full-validation tasks, maximum two concurrent | best and final for both arms | all of 949065 succeeds |

Initial arrays 949026/949030/949034 were cancelled before Python started: Slurm
held the first array with `user_env_retrieval_failed_requeued_held`. Local Slurm
documentation confirms `--export=ALL,NAME=value` implicitly retrieves the login
environment. Replacement submissions use plain `--export=ALL` and positional
arguments; experiment settings were unchanged.

Code/configs in `Graph-Native-Betti-Matching-Representation`:

- `scripts/extend_scratch_geometry.py`: bounded scratch continuation; reuses
  existing training, criterion routing, monitoring and geometry evaluation.
- `configs/spline_scratch_extend300.yaml`: paired source runs and monitoring.
- `cluster/jean_zay/spline_scratch_extend300.slurm`: smoke then continuation.
- `configs/spline_scratch_extend300_validation.yaml`: four checkpoint evaluations.
- `cluster/jean_zay/spline_full_validation.slurm`: accepts optional config argument
  in addition to the existing environment-variable/default interface.

Commands: `sbatch --export=ALL cluster/jean_zay/spline_scratch_extend300.slurm 150`,
then the same with `--dependency=aftercorr:<first-array-id>` and argument `300`.
Evaluation: `sbatch --export=ALL --array=0-3%2 --dependency=afterok:<second-array-id>
cluster/jean_zay/spline_full_validation.slurm configs/spline_scratch_extend300_validation.yaml`.
Use distinct output roots if repeating the experiment; existing directories are
deliberately rejected to preserve artifacts.

Output root:
`/lustre/fsn1/projects/rech/vnc/upz25mj/experiments/gnbm/spline_learning/runs/scratch_extend300_20261012/`

Each arm has `epoch150/` and `epoch300/`; evaluation uses `full_validation/`.
Logs are `experiments/spline_learning/logs/scratch-extend{150,300,val}-<array>_<task>.{out,err}`.

## Checks and time estimate

Python/Slurm syntax passed. Two focused CPU tests passed: restored AdamW produces
the identical next parameter update/LR/moments, and epoch-boundary RNG restoration
reproduces the next shuffled epoch and torch random draws. Real GPU smoke gates
check strict model loading, restored scheduler position, finite losses/gradients,
active detector updates, the expected spline gradient, and decoded/matched metrics
on four cases before long training starts.

Both epoch-150 GPU smokes **passed** (25,000→25,003 updates); restored LR was
6.810713331450913e-5 and reached 6.810688054571481e-5 after three updates in
both arms. Both production tasks are running, one H100 each. Initial 128-case
decoded metrics and fixed-probe image sensitivity reproduce the source pilot
values. The first production forward/backward/AdamW update also passed.

Pilot elapsed times were 2,538.6 s (control) and 2,461.4 s (detached) for 25k updates.
Scaling the remaining 725k gives **20.45 h / 19.83 h**. Allow approximately
**20–24 h per model**, **40–48 GPU-hours combined**, or **20–24 h elapsed when
parallel**, plus scheduling delays between stages. Full validation previously
took about 10 minutes per checkpoint: four tasks at concurrency two add roughly
20–30 minutes plus queue time. Later decoded graphs may cost more to evaluate.

Next review: inspect learning/validation trajectories, image sensitivity, curve
gain over identical-endpoint chords, curved-branch strata and overfitting. Retain
best and final evidence even if the last checkpoint is worse. No automatic new
training phase beyond these authorized continuations.

Both runs completed **300 total epochs / 750,000 updates**, with exit code 0.

all four full-validation jobs completed by **04:54:07**, before 08:30 maintenance.

### Paired full validation: all 1,952 patches

Same ordered samples, input/configuration/evaluation protocol and six fixed

Saved BN statistics, no recalibration; weights/buffers unchanged by evaluation.
Actual epoch 150 and epoch 300 training batch-order hashes match across arms.

| model | epoch | node_f 1 | edge_f 1 | branch_f 1 | curve_f 1 | chord_curve_f 1 | endpoint_neutral_gain |

Positive endpoint-neutral gain means shape error improved over chords after

separates shape from localization; decoded curve F1 evaluates complete predicted
geometry with its predicted nodes/connectivity. They answer different questions.

### Discoveries and limits

1. **Scratch learning is possible with detached geometry.** The previous coupled
   token-supervision run collapsed, while this isolated residual/local-image
   setup retained graph learning and image sensitivity for 300 epochs. This supports
   harmful early geometry feedback as a cause under the tested setup, without
   identifying its exact mechanism. BN recalibration is not the explanation
   supported by the existing diagnostic. A single seed is not proof of robustness.
2. **Curves improve decoded vessel overlap:** final B-spline curve F1 0.34261 versus
   its same-endpoint chords 0.22633 (absolute gain 0.11628). Final graph-only curve
   F1 0.20201. Curvature comparisons within one model hold nodes and edges fixed.
   Native node/edge differences between models cannot be attributed causally to
   geometry, because geometry gradients are detached from the detector.
3. **Geometry overfits.** Final endpoint-neutral shape error on full validation
   is 0.53715 mm versus chord 0.51493 mm (**4.32% worse**), despite a 57.64% improvement
   on the 512-case training monitor. The selected spline best checkpoint (epoch 170)
   retains a modest full-validation neutral gain 2.37%, whereas its final checkpoint
   has higher decoded curve F1. More epochs did not uniformly improve shape.
4. On the **128-case monitoring subset only**, the final model improves neutral
   shape on 193 curved long branches by 22.00% (1.30356 vs 1.67118 mm); near-straight
   long branches worsen 11.36%, and 550 short branches worsen 117.36%
   (0.14544 vs 0.06691 mm). Short branches and subtle bends dominate the aggregate
   weakness. Full-validation curvature strata were not enabled in this evaluation
   configuration; do not present the 128-case percentages as full-population results.
5. **Topology is not solved:** final common branch F1 is 0.00793/0.01179. The models
   predict approximately 10.91/10.92 common branches per patch versus 16.36 targets,
   and Betti errors remain substantial. Better native edges and curve overlap
   do not establish accurate complete vessel graphs. Native node boxes and strict
   spatial branch/anchor correspondence use different matching criteria.
6. **Best-checkpoint selection is noisy and objective dependent.** Selected control
   epoch 255 and spline epoch 170 maximize 128-case common branch F1, then native
   edge F1. These choices do not maximize every full-validation metric; selected
   spline best has edge F1 0.54407 vs final 0.54195, but curve F1 0.32358 vs 0.34261.
   Retain both outcomes; do not relabel a different checkpoint as best after
   inspecting the full validation or test set.

### Next research decisions

- Inspect the gap between native detection and common complete-branch recovery
  with the existing fixed cases and exact metric/spacing/matching definitions,
  including boundary, loop and parallel-branch rules, before claiming topology
  success or changing the architecture.
- Address shape generalization and short-branch behavior in a bounded comparison;
  choose geometry checkpoints using an explicit validation geometry objective.
  Any chord fallback/regularization is a proposal requiring a controlled experiment,
  not a modification made during this review. Preserve successful detector training.
- After settling selection and evaluation, use a second seed and the held-out
  test set for a paper-quality comparison. No additional GPU jobs launched here.

### Artifacts and publication

Full tables and portable six-case HTML gallery: `full_validation/comparison.{csv,md,json,html}`
under the run root. Best/final models: `<arm>/epoch 300/{best.pt,model.pt}`.
Final compact evidence is tracked at
`experiments/spline_learning/metadata/local-geometry/scratch-extension-final-results.json`;
all source summary hashes and the paired audit are recorded there.

`--approve-for-me` with explicit`--sandbox`. No model or report ran in that attempt.
Removed the redundant sandbox flag (automatic approval review already selects
workspace-write), and completed the authorized documentation/commit/push in this
active review. No approval/sandbox bypass was introduced. The 15:00 fallback will
skip once the published-completion marker is verified.

# Scratch learning with residual local-image geometry

User authorized proceeding after the pretrained stability phase. This is a
bounded paired diagnostic, not another full 300-epoch training.

## Why investigate overfitting and scratch learning separately?

The 25k pretrained continuation's fixed 512-case training monitor showed branch
F1 rising from 0.32094 to 0.39205 and edge F1 from 0.87553 to 0.90534. On the
fixed 128-case validation monitor, branch F1 went from 0.27125 to 0.26933
(peaking at 0.28466 after 5k), while edge F1 went from 0.86392 to 0.85943.
Together with full-validation branch decline, this supports overfitting in
connectivity; it does not prove a unique cause. Geometry continued improving.
The earlier full-validation-selected checkpoint remains preserved.

Pretraining supplies graph localization/connectivity already. Successful local
geometry with that detector does not establish scratch learning. The next test
removes all pretrained weights while holding graph training conditions matched.

## Two arms

- `graph_control`: spline weight 0; graph losses alone train the detector.
- `local_spline`: spline weight 1.4739989612791453; graph losses plus residual
  control supervision train from update one.

Both construct the same eight-control B-spline MLP and local-image correction
module, initialized identically alongside the detector. Only the geometry loss
weight differs. The control's zero-initialized output layers receive no geometry
updates, so its curves remain exact chords; this invariant is checked after
training. This retains paired parameter construction while reproducing a
straight-edge graph-learning control.

The spline arm uses the existing `tokens_only` gradient route: predicted node
coordinates are detached for geometry supervision; geometry gradients can
propagate through object/relation tokens into the transformer and CNN. The
local sampler retains its existing detached CNN values/sampling coordinates.
The CNN still learns from graph losses and token-mediated geometry gradients.
No GT coordinates enter the head or sampling path. Matcher and targets unchanged.

This selects endpoint detachment as the first minimal scratch recipe because
it retained geometry/edge performance in the prior controlled experiment. It
is not a claim that the alternative route is invalid. This two-arm experiment
cannot isolate the separate contributions of residual targets, local features
and detachment; it tests whether this recipe interferes with graph learning.

## Fixed protocol

- All model modules, including CNN, randomly initialized; no checkpoint loaded.
- Exactly the existing 10,000 SyntheticMRI train patches, batch 4, seed 364505.
- 25,000 updates per arm (10 passes), one H100 per arm, independent parallel jobs.
- Original scratch AdamW LR 7e-5, WD 1e-4, 2,500-update warmup from 1e-9.
  Preserve the original polynomial LR horizon of 750k updates (300 epochs),
  but the job **stops at 25k**; the horizon is not authorization to train 300 epochs.
- Ordinary train mode, including BN updates, in both arms. Saved BN statistics
  used for evaluation; no recalibration. Unlike frozen/pretrained diagnostics,
  the entire detector and CNN now learn.
- No augmentation, target, sampler, graph/node-budget or split changes.
- Reuse the same 512 train-monitor and 128 disjoint validation cases. The source
  run supplies sample IDs only, never weights or predictions.
- Loss/image sensitivity every 1k; decoded graph/chord metrics, separate
  GT-matched geometry, curvature strata and fixed projections at 5k/15k/25k.
- Initial-weight and actual batch-order hashes saved for paired verification.
- Model+optimizer+scheduler snapshots at 5k, 15k, final25k. Offline W&B retained.
- Each task passes a fresh 3-update GPU smoke before its full run. Check finite
  gradients, active CNN gradients, intended active/zero spline gradients and
  control's exact-chord preservation. Targeted CPU checks use the real training
  step to verify BN updates and the supervision toggle, plus existing routing tests.

## Interpretation

- Both learn detection, spline gains curvature without substantial graph harm:
  evidence the improved representation can start learning without pretraining;
  longer scratch evaluation is still needed.
- Graph-only learns but spline loses detection/image sensitivity: evidence of
  geometry coupling under this recipe. A same-run graph-first warm-up is then
  a justified follow-up, not automatically launched now.
- Both fail/learn slowly: initialization, shared training settings or short
  budget remain explanations; cannot attribute failure specifically to splines.
- Training improves while validation stalls: inspect generalization instead of
  interpreting lower training loss as reconstruction success.

Original 300-epoch collapse may occur later than this diagnostic. Absence of
collapse at 25k does not rule it out. No test-set inference, IXI switch or further
training is queued automatically.

## Files and outputs

Config: `configs/spline_scratch_local_pilot.yaml`.
Runner: existing `scripts/train_spline_weight_pilot.py` with explicit opt-in
`scratch_geometry`; defaults for earlier frozen pilots remain unchanged.
Submission: `cluster/jean_zay/spline_scratch_local.slurm`.

Output root:
`/lustre/fsn1/projects/rech/vnc/upz25mj/experiments/gnbm/spline_learning/runs/scratch_local_pilot_20261010/`
with `graph_control`, `local_spline` and separate `smoke-*` directories.

Submitted **878748_0** (graph-only control) and **878748_1** (local-image residual spline). Four targeted CPU tests passed, including real train-step BN and zero/active geometry supervision checks. Syntax/diff checks passed. GPU smokes pending at submission. Each task has a three-hour ceiling. Logs: `experiments/spline_learning/logs/scratch-local-878748_<task>.{out,err}`.

## First smoke failure and correction

Both 878748 tasks stopped before training during model setup (48–50 seconds). The diagnostic asserted every stored parameter was trainable, but the real decoder deliberately keeps `cross_attn2` and `norm12` frozen because the legacy relation cross-attention block is not called by forward. The miniature CPU fixture did not contain that block. This was a diagnostic guard error, not evidence of learning collapse.

The guard now requires exactly those known inactive tensors to be frozen and rejects freezing any active parameter. Model architecture, forward computation, optimizer and scientific settings are unchanged. A real decoder regression check and full actual-model construction verify the correction. The first local construction attempt was blocked by sandbox MPI sockets and required execution outside the sandbox; no experiment setting changed.

Resubmission uses a new `scratch_local_pilot_20261010_attempt2` output root to preserve failed smoke artifacts. The original array started no full 25k training, and no results from it should be interpreted scientifically.

Actual full model construction passed the revised guard: exactly 24 intentionally inactive tensors; an injected CNN freeze was correctly rejected. Both targeted tests passed, including the real decoder regression and the existing three-step scratch supervision test. Resubmitted **885337_0/1**, unchanged settings, separate attempt2 output directory. GPU smokes pending at submission.

## 2026-10-11 — Completed scratch comparison

Jobs 885337_0/1 completed successfully, including smokes, in 47:08 / 44:12. Each completed 25,000 updates. Initial-state and actual batch-order hashes are identical; no checkpoint was loaded.

Validation results on the fixed 128 cases (not the full validation split):

| Arm | Node F1 | Edge F1 | Curve F1 | Memory image sensitivity |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| graph_control | 0.236421 | 0.195736 | 0.056406 | 0.89432681 |
| local_spline | 0.000000 | 0.008279 | 0.004004 | 3.3786341e-06 |

Graph-control edge F1 rises 0.00665 → 0.14435 → 0.19574 at 5k/15k/25k; node F1 reaches 0.23642. It is learning but still far from a usable graph: common branch F1 remains zero. Local-spline final train-monitor node F1 is also zero, so its failure is not explained as ordinary train-good/validation-bad overfitting.

Spline transformer-memory sensitivity drops from 0.8491 at 4k to 0.001600 at 9k and 0.000003379 at 25k; graph control reaches 0.8943. These are fixed-probe eval-mode measurements, not proof that every representation has collapsed on every image. CNN projected-feature sensitivity remains 0.1381 for spline versus 2.7208 for control. Final spline endpoint-neutral guide error 0.50264 mm is slightly worse than the chord reference 0.50138 mm. Curvature did not improve.

This matched experiment supports destabilization associated with geometry supervision from initialization, despite residual targets, local image features and endpoint detachment. It does not isolate the exact internal mechanism, exclude BN-mediated effects, or prove all scratch recipes fail. The only intended arm difference is spline loss weight; head sampling and targets are unchanged. The successful pretrained geometry experiments therefore do not yet transfer to scratch learning.

Next discriminative proposal: train the spline head from scratch while detaching both tokens and endpoints from its loss, allowing the detector to learn only from graph losses. This directly tests the remaining geometry-to-detector gradient route, before adding a graph-first warm-up or changing architecture. The completed graph-only run supplies the matched reference if initialization, batch order and settings are preserved. No new experiment launched during this review.

# V0 SyntheticMRI training with up to 10,000 patches

Date: 2026-10-06. Status: training completed all 50 epochs; all 13,071 compatible test patches evaluated. Test job 687813 failed only during W&B initialization; saved results verified and logging recovered from the login node.

## Protocol fixed before training

- Main method: cubic B-spline, eight controls (six free internal 3D controls), fixed knots, 64 samples, V0 internal-control SmoothL1 in mm. Predicted graph nodes anchor endpoints; entire model fine-tuned jointly.
- Initialization: original SyntheticMRI graph checkpoint `finetune_vessels_full_300ep/models/best_edge_f1_checkpoint.pt`, not the four-patch overfit checkpoint. The supplied training manifest contains 91,200 training and 19,200 validation samples; neither sample IDs nor patient IDs overlap the test population.
- Original dataset population: 91,200 train patches / 95 subjects; 19,200 validation patches / 20 subjects; 20,160 test patches / 21 subjects. Subject-disjoint splits are preserved.
- Training membership: rank source training IDs by SHA256 of seed, split and sample ID; select at most 10,000 before target compatibility checks. Seed 364505. No foreground, node-count, fit-quality or tortuosity filtering. Validation uses a fixed, seeded subset of at most 2,000 candidates before compatibility checks; test has no cap. Membership is restricted to subjects with preserved complete source graphs, as authorized by the user. Any unsupported patches are listed by split and reason; test metrics must report the eligible fraction of the complete test population.
- Batch four, one H100, 50 epochs, augmentation off until geometric transforms are implemented correctly. AdamW LR 7e-5, weight decay 1e-4, betas (0.9, 0.999), epsilon 1e-8; one epoch of warmup followed by polynomial decay (power 0.9). This is a bounded first generalization experiment, not a claim that 50 epochs establishes convergence.
- Retain V0 graph loss weights (boxes 3, class 4, cardinality 0.8, nodes 2, edges 6), and spline weight 1.4739989613 from the training-only prototype calibration. No tuning on test data; no topology/domain/node-type losses.
- Validate every five epochs on the fixed compatible validation subset (up to 2,000 patches). Select the checkpoint with the lowest combined validation loss (`best_checkpoint.pt`), including spline loss; do not select by test scores. Keep a complete latest training-state checkpoint each epoch. No early stopping for this fixed-budget experiment.
- Final evaluation runs once after successful training, using the validation-selected checkpoint and the full compatible test split. No BN recalibration or threshold search on test data.

## Boundary correction requested by the user

The source prepared MRI patches were generated with version-3 center-coordinate crop bounds `[start, start+size-1]`. The current graph-extraction repository also contains a newer exact voxel-cell policy and the earlier last-inside-centerline-sample policy. For this spline run, the user requested the latter behavior: preserve a boundary endpoint and its incident branch instead of dropping a boundary-crossing vessel.

New targets clip full paths in voxel coordinates to the complete image voxel cells, `[start-0.5, start+size-0.5]`. Where a clipped component contains at least two distinct original samples, an interpolated boundary endpoint is moved to its nearest existing sample inside that same ordered component. This prevents selecting a point from another branch or another re-entry of the same vessel. True source nodes remain shared across incident branches.

If fewer than two usable existing samples remain, retain the positive-length clipped component with exact intersections as a recorded fallback rather than silently lose its vessel segment. A genuinely singleton contact with the full voxel-cell box is retained as an isolated boundary node, with node supervision and no fictitious zero-length spline. Counts of snapped endpoints, remaining singleton contacts and sparse-component fallbacks are recorded per split. This differs from the earlier four-patch experiment; its cache and results remain separate and unchanged.

Source index counts: 40,447 train, 8,626 validation and 9,023 test patches contained a singleton contact under the **old center-coordinate bounds** (~44%). This is not a measured failure rate of the corrected voxel-cell targets. The distinction is necessary because a boundary voxel can contain a short vessel segment even when the center-coordinate box sees only a point.

## Closed and parallel branches

A closed branch returns to the same topological anchor, or forms a pure degree-two cycle. A parallel pair consists of two distinct vessel paths connecting the same anchors. Splines themselves can describe those shapes, but the current decoder predicts one spline for each pair of distinct nodes: no self-edge output and no multiple-edge output for a pair. Preparation detects and reports these whole-patch incompatibilities instead of merging or silently dropping branches. Their prevalence is not assumed; preparation must measure it. Results on an eligible test subset must state coverage and exclusions.

## Validation visualization and W&B

Four fixed validation samples from different subjects are chosen deterministically, without predicted scores or visual quality selection. At each validation event, save a two-row, three-column PNG: original guides above, decoded predictions below, in projections along D/H/W. Background is the MRI maximum-intensity projection with translucent mask support; anchor nodes are visible. A crossing in a projection is not necessarily a junction in 3D.

Images are logged as `validation/projections` against `validation/epoch` in the existing W&B entity/project; PNGs also remain under `runs/spline_v0_k8_10k_val2k_50ep/validation-projections/epoch-XXX/`. No test examples are used for training monitoring. Validation loss scalars are retained locally in `validation-losses.jsonl` and in W&B.

## Test measurements

Use existing box-based node/edge detection and Betti metrics, plus separate physical spline metrics. Detection `max_detections` is 120 for this run so a 40-detection cap does not artificially truncate larger anchor graphs; other box/SMD settings remain unchanged. Standard SMD still uses chords in normalized coordinates.

Additional branch correspondence uses one-to-one spatial node assignment accepted only within 1 mm, then endpoint identities. Report matched, missing and extra branches, micro branch F1, and recovered target-branch coverage. Shape errors apply only to recovered branches and must always accompany coverage. Report equal-branch mean curve error against fitted targets, symmetric distance to original full guides, tortuosity absolute error, and complementary existing-mask support. Guide comparison uses 257 parameter samples and 0.25 mm arc-length query spacing with exact point-to-polyline distance. Both guides and masks are uncertain references, not independent anatomical truth. Export per-patch metrics and graph/spline predictions for later subject-level analysis.

## Implementation and launch gates

Representation worktree additions: `scripts/prepare_spline_dataset.py`, `scripts/smoke_spline_dataset.py`, `training/evaluation/spline_metrics.py`, `training/evaluation/spline_visualization.py`, `scripts/log_spline_test.py`, and `configs/finetune_spline_v0_10k.yaml`. Generic training optionally saves/logs validation projections; evaluation exports geometry and its coverage separately from standard graph metrics.

Launch stages:

1. Pilot preparation, boundary/basis/tracking tests, three real-batch GPU updates, validation loss, decoded geometry metrics, and real W&B image logging.
2. CPU preparation of capped training (10,000), fixed validation (2,000), and uncapped available test targets.
3. After successful GT preparation and manifest checks, start the 50-epoch joint fine-tuning run. The user requested skipping another GPU smoke because job 615708 already passed.
4. After training succeeds, evaluate the validation-selected checkpoint on test and attach metrics/population coverage to the same W&B run.

First pilot job 614887 failed before training because original full raw MRI volumes are no longer present for most subjects. The prepared MRI patches and full segmentations remain available. The generator required raw/seg affine equality; preparation now uses the retained full segmentation header and verifies it against every stored source VTP before constructing new targets. No affine is guessed. Corrected pilot job: **615011**. Long training has not been submitted at this point.

### Source availability problem discovered before long-run submission

Job 615011 exposed missing full graph files (not a training failure). Of the 136 graph directories, 27 do not contain the required original `nodes.csv`, `edges.csv`, and `graph.vvg`:

- Train: 2, 6, 7, 11, 17, 21, 23, 31, 33, 50, 62, 63, 65, 67, 81, 87, 89, 95, 99, 112, 124.
- Validation: 32, 77, 102.
- Test: 45, 64, 107.

The user was asked for a restoration/archive path. Original curved paths cannot be recovered from the chord-only patch VTPs without changing the supervision assumptions.

Preparation now checks full graph availability before an expensive run and refuses to silently change the complete experiment population. A separately labelled, source-complete pilot subset (`--pilot-available-subjects`) can still verify implementation and W&B images; pilot job **615230**. It must not be used for the main experiment. The training launcher checks that its target manifest is not a pilot and that all 20,160 source test candidates were considered. **Long-run submission waits for complete GT extraction, as requested by the user.**

### Dataset health and conditional relocation request

The user asked to move the upz73jr source to their own dataset folder and replace the old version **if healthy**. Inventory against the source index found all 130,560 prepared image/mask/VTP triplets (91,200 train / 19,200 val / 20,160 test), but only one of 136 full raw MRI volumes, all 136 full segmentation volumes, and 109 of 136 complete full graphs. Prepared patch completeness is a filename/readability inventory, not exhaustive content validation. Complete dataset relocation would additionally require restoring the missing full MRI volumes.

### Completed boundary and visualization smoke

Job **615708** completed in **1 minute 26 seconds**, exit **0:0**. Ten focused boundary/basis/loss/tracking tests passed. Three GPU updates on real pilot training patches had finite losses and nonzero spline-head gradients. Four validation projections were saved and visually inspected; decoded graph and physical geometry evaluation also completed on four pilot validation patches. These are smoke checks, not generalization results.

The separately labelled pilot prepared 31 training, 16 validation and 15 test-compatible caches from 64 requested pilot candidates, excluding one training and one test patch with parallel branches. No model was evaluated on pilot test patches. There were 593 snapped endpoints and 38 sparse-component exact fallbacks across the compatible pilot caches; two genuine singleton voxel-cell contacts were preserved as isolated nodes. These counts are pilot-specific and do not establish the full-data prevalence.

Online W&B initialization on the compute node timed out (job 615230). Tracking now records offline rather than lose images when online initialization raises a communication error. Job 615708 used offline W&B deliberately, then its metrics and four PNGs were successfully synced from the login node. [Actual smoke run in W&B](https://wandb.ai/alessandrobenvenuti2002-politecnico-di-torino/focal-loss/runs/8gzgsw6k). Inspect `validation/projections`. This establishes actual W&B image logging and upload; live streaming from compute nodes is not established.

Example [validation projection PNG](../../Graph-Native-Betti-Matching-Representation/experiments/spline_learning/runs/dataset-smoke-615708/validation-projections/epoch-000/sample_000013_0603.png). Full smoke outputs: `runs/dataset-smoke-615708/`, including `smoke.json`, `validation-evaluation/`, `wandb-run.json` and `wandb-sync.json`.

Next required input: a backup/restoration location for the original full graphs of the 27 listed subjects. Then resume complete target extraction, inspect population/exclusion counts, smoke the completed cache, submit the long run, and arrange the final test evaluation after successful training. No permission to change the test population or reconstruct missing paths from straight-edge labels was inferred.

## Latest launch update: available subjects, smaller validation, and resubmission

The user authorized using only subjects with complete original full graphs and reducing validation to 2,000 candidates. The original split membership remains unchanged. During resubmission, the source inventory changed from 109 complete subjects to 27; the cause has not been established. ## Failure diagnosis and resumption (2026-10-06)

Job 646175 failed on duplicate undirected edges before training. Reproduced on real patch **sample_000001_0272**. Source CSV edge **806** has endpoints **2488 → 2488**, recorded length **1.28088 mm**, and one interior guide sample. Its dense crop is **A → B → A**; generic simple-graph contraction rejects the two opposite segments as duplicate edges before it can classify the closed branch. This is a closed source-guide component, not a learned prediction or evidence of two anatomical vessels.

`crop_dense_paths` now records closed components. `contract_spline_graph` excludes such whole patches as `closed_branch` before contraction, and rejects duplicate direct connections as `parallel_branches` without deduplicating source records. Existing longer closed/parallel branches and object capacity checks remain. Regression coverage includes a two-segment source loop, short parallel branches and a valid one-edge graph. The cache was moved, preserving those completed results, to `/lustre/fsn1/projects/rech/vnc/upz25mj/experiments/gnbm/spline_learning/synthetic_mri_k8_10k_val2k`; its repository path is now a link. All accepted target NPZ files in those 88 patient results were confirmed retained. Approximately **97,700 file entries** were freed initially. Resume reuses complete patient results and reprocesses unfinished patients with unchanged selected membership.

Job 676478 failed at startup because the installed PyVista package lacked `typing/mypy_plugin.py`. Reinstalled **exactly PyVista 0.46.3**, without changing dependencies. A real relocated VTP was successfully read and checked against its target NPZ. No repeated model/GPU smoke was run. The cause of missing environment files is not established.

Scheduler-held jobs 676486/676532 were replaced after the scheduler refused dependency update/release. Previous failed chains are historical, not active. Configuration, sampling caps, original split membership, losses and initialization are unchanged.

Stable Git commits on representation: **24c2605** (spline training/evaluation/validation projections plus topology eligibility) and **98eb6a9** (verified staged dataset restoration). External documentation stays in graph-representation/docs; the code repository includes a short documentation index.

Job **676631 completed in 3 min 15 s, exit 0:0**, resuming the three unfinished patients. Final target cache:

Current immutable manifests/configuration are now under `experiments/spline_learning/metadata/`. The main dataset/run links and active logs remain. Compute-node W&B initialization fell back to offline recording (run ID **pnbftfvi**), retaining scalars/images locally for later upload. ## Epoch-9 interruption and strict resume

Training **676650 failed after 33 min 27 s** inside the epoch-10 DataLoader, because the shared environment no longer contained `medpy.io.header`. Nine complete training epochs and an epoch-5 validation event had succeeded. Recorded combined validation loss at epoch 5: **2.092977**. This is an optimization diagnostic, not held-out test performance.

The atomically saved latest checkpoint was read and verified: **epoch 9 / iteration 21,852**, with model, optimizer, scheduler and runtime state. Existing strict checkpoint resume restores these states, plus prior checkpoint-selection state. Partial epoch-10 work after that checkpoint is replayed; no completed epochs are discarded and no optimizer reset is performed.

Reinstalled **exactly MedPy 0.5.2**, with no dependency changes. A targeted RECORD audit found other missing package entries, including stale duplicate-version metadata and unused assets/tests; it is not evidence that every missing entry is an active runtime fault. Given the earlier missing PyVista file and the later MedPy file disappearance, preserved the current repaired site-packages tree outside projects at `/lustre/fswork/projects/rech/vnc/upz25mj/experiments/gnbm/spline-runtime-20261006/site-packages.tar` (1.4 GB). Both train and test now extract this fixed package copy into job-local storage and prepend it to PYTHONPATH. System PyTorch/CUDA remain supplied by the same cluster module. Targeted verification using that job-local copy passed: actual 64³ MRI loaded with finite values through the real MedPy reader, real checkpoint read, and MedPy/PyVista imports confirmed from the local copy. No repeated GPU/model smoke was run. The source package snapshot is kept outside projects.

The old segment and resumed segment must both be synced from a login node to the same run. Test job **681013** depends on successful resume. Replaced blocked test 676692. Model/loss/data/scheduler configuration and all exact patch memberships are unchanged.

Stable commit: **81b21ec**, adding job-local package staging and optional checkpoint-resume submission support. Active job IDs are recorded in `experiments/spline_learning/metadata/current-jobs.json`.

### Complete library availability audit and final runtime repair

Resume 681009 failed during startup on Matplotlib's missing `tri.tricontour`, before modifying the epoch-9 checkpoint. Reinstalled **Matplotlib 3.8.4**, matching the version actually imported before failure; conflicting newer distribution metadata had been present. The cause of shared package-file disappearances remains unconfirmed. Current run resumes from the full **epoch 9 / iteration 21,852** checkpoint with optimizer/scheduler/RNG and checkpoint selection state retained. Jobs **687805 → 687813** are resume → held-out evaluation; 681009 failed and its blocked test 681013 was cancelled. Tracking keeps W&B ID pnbftfvi offline.

Reusable audit: `scripts/check_spline_libraries.py`, after sourcing cluster env and fixed runtime. Stable audit/checksum commit **26d1630**. Do not claim GPU execution from the CPU import audit: actual resumed epochs remain to be observed.

### Why fewer than the requested caps?

Caps apply to the seeded candidate selection **before** graph compatibility checks. From 10,000 training candidates, 133 closed-branch and 158 parallel-branch patches are excluded whole, leaving 9,709. Validation: 2,000 − 22 − 26 = 1,952. Test: 13,440 − 156 − 213 = 13,071. ## Report 29

Source: `docs/research/spline_learning/spline-approach-selection.md`

<!-- BEGIN SOURCE: docs/research/spline_learning/spline-approach-selection.md -->

# Selection after the initial spline experiments

Date: 2026-10-05. **Select V0 control supervision with joint SyntheticMRI fine-tuning as the main approach for the next experiment. Keep V1 sampled-curve supervision as an ablation.** This is a working research decision, not a claim of universal superiority.

## Verification

Reviewed both loss implementations, resolved settings, calibrated weights, decoded overlays, and fresh saved-checkpoint evaluation (job 613399). Both fine-tuning arms start from the same original graph checkpoint and use the same architecture, seed, four training patches, 500 updates and optimizer schedule. V1 inherits V0 settings and changes spline supervision from internal controls to sampled curves. Spline weights are separately calibrated using the same procedure (1.474 / 1.479). V1 is not initialized from trained V0 weights. Neither variant adds test-time target connections in decoded mode.

Fresh inference exactly reproduced the nodes, edges and curves in the viewers. Both fine-tuned variants recover 98 nodes and 79 edges, with node/edge F1 1.00 under the existing box-based protocol. These detection scores do not distinguish shape quality.

Additional verification uses actual decoded controls from the fresh evaluation exports, original complete paths rather than fitted curve targets, and physical coordinates. Cubic splines are sampled at 801 parameter positions. Symmetric mean distance averages both directed distances, using 0.1 mm arc-length sampling and exact distance to each polyline segment. Tortuosity is path length divided by endpoint chord length; report mean absolute error. All metrics below equally weight the 79 branches, not the four patch means. The metric denominator uses each curve's own endpoints. Full paths remain uncertain references, not perfect anatomical truth.

| Approach | Error to fitted spline at corresponding samples (mm) | Symmetric distance to original guide (mm) | Tortuosity absolute error |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| V0 joint fine-tuning | 0.1093 | **0.1010** | **0.01013** |
| V1 joint fine-tuning | 0.1311 | 0.1214 | 0.01128 |
| V0 scratch | 0.3811 | 0.3498 | 0.02459 |
| Chord with V0 fine-tuned endpoints | 0.4812 | 0.4731 | 0.02286 |
| Eight-control fitted oracle | — | 0.0242 | 0.00182 |

V0 fine-tuning improves original-guide distance over its same-endpoint chord by approximately 79%, and tortuosity error by approximately 56%. V0 scratch improves guide distance but its aggregate tortuosity error is slightly worse than the chord baseline; successful shape optimization alone does not establish accurate tortuosity.

Reproduction from the representation worktree:

```bash
python scripts/verify_spline_variants.py --run-root experiments/spline_learning/runs/job-612351
```

Full branch-level results: `experiments/spline_learning/runs/job-612351/guide_verification.json`. No new training was performed for this verification.

## Why select V0 now

V0 gives the strongest measured curve and guide agreement, including lower tortuosity error, at this matched update budget. It is straightforward to inspect and reproduce: fixed knots, fixed degree, deterministic endpoint-constrained fitting, and direct internal-control regression. Fixed knots and parameterization are essential to make this coordinate target well-defined.

V1 is a useful geometric alternative because it penalizes curve locations directly. However, the implemented V1 still compares corresponding parameter samples against the same fitted reference; it is not parameterization invariant and does not solve unreliable guide supervision. Control loss can amplify noise in fitted controls, while sampled-curve loss can constrain some combinations of controls weakly. The four-patch results do not establish how either behaves under noisy targets or on unseen subjects. Do not compare their raw spline loss or total loss values to choose a winner: their objectives differ.

The representation and loss comparison are distinct from the initialization comparison. Fine-tuning is currently the practical initialization. Scratch remains necessary as a controlled ablation to test whether conclusions depend on prior graph learning; equal 500-update budgets do not establish its converged performance. Joint representation learning from the beginning has not been compared with fine-tuning at a matched total training budget.

## Evidence needed for a paper

1. Audit subject-level train/validation/test separation, including data used by the original 300-epoch checkpoint. A patch unused for spline fitting is not automatically unseen by the initialized model. If prior checkpoint exposure conflicts with the intended split, create a clean initialization trained only on the permitted training subjects.
2. Train V0 and V1 on the same expanded training set and budgets; use validation subjects for model/loss selection and keep test subjects untouched. Repeat with at least three seeds and report variation. Account for subjects as the independent units rather than treating adjacent branches as independent statistical replicates.
3. Report decoded topology, guide distance, endpoint error, tail geometry errors and tortuosity separately. Include vessel-mask support as complementary image evidence, with uncertainty in guides and masks acknowledged. Evaluate all patches and count missing/extra branches; geometry restricted to recovered pairs must include its coverage.
4. Compare same-endpoint chords, the original dense-node graph approach, and fitted spline oracles. Ablate 6/8/10 controls and fine-tuning versus scratch under explicit budgets. Demonstrate the intended reduction in required object tokens: these first runs still used 120 object queries, so token independence has not been established.
5. Include substantially more tortuous branches (current maximum guide tortuosity is only about 1.197), and report the rate of excluded tangent contacts, loops and parallel branches. The current selected subset does not establish support for those cases.

The defensible current conclusion is that this compact branch representation can be learned on the four selected training patches and captures bends substantially better than a chord with identical predicted endpoints. Generalization, anatomical fidelity and a reduction in object-query requirements remain to be demonstrated. The paper's final loss choice should follow held-out validation evidence; V0 is the selected main candidate now.
