# IXI source-domain comparison, representation trained in both stages

Date: 2026-10-15. User authorized three data strategies, each with straight edges and B-splines during BOTH pretraining and fine-tuning. This differs from the preceding plant/leaf→SyntheticMRI experiments, which pretrained graph detection only and introduced spline loss during fine-tuning. Those existing runs are preserved.

## Six arms

| Array index | Arm | First stage | Second stage |
|---|---|---|---|
|0|ixi_straight|IXI, straight|IXI, straight|
|1|ixi_spline|IXI, B-spline|IXI, B-spline|
|2|plants_straight|Plants + IXI, straight|IXI, straight|
|3|plants_spline|Plants + IXI, B-spline|IXI, B-spline|
|4|synthetic_straight|SyntheticMRI + IXI, straight|IXI, straight|
|5|synthetic_spline|SyntheticMRI + IXI, B-spline|IXI, B-spline|

All first stages start from random weights; the base YAML supplies configuration, not pretrained parameters. Each second stage loads its own validation-selected first-stage checkpoint, INCLUDING learned spline parameters, with fresh optimizer/scheduler. The IXI-only second stage is continued training on the same population, not a domain transfer.

## Controlled training recipe

- First stage50epochs,50,000 replacement draws/epoch, batch32 (1563updates/epoch).
- Same10,000 compatible IXI training patches across all six arms, selected by seeded hash ranking; subject-disjoint original splits preserved.
- Mixed sources25,000 plants or25,000 SyntheticMRI patches. Equal expected source/target draws via target weight2.5. IXI-only uses50,000 IXI draws. This matches updates, not IXI exposure or exact GPU compute. Edge-geometry loss averages matched positives, so sample balance does not imply equal per-domain geometry gradient magnitude.
- Second stage up to100epochs on the same IXI training population; existing patience30/minimum30 policy and monitoring every5epochs retained.
- AdamW LR7e-5, decay1e-4, one-epoch warmup and existing polynomial schedule. Graph losses unchanged; spline residual-control weight1.4739989612791453. This weight is reused from SyntheticMRI, not newly calibrated to IXI.
- Mixed pretraining uses domain adaptation weight1.0, image/instance adversarial losses and consistency. IXI-only and all second stages disable domain adaptation.
- All arms use256object queries, following existing IXI configurations; original SyntheticMRI study used120. Node-type prediction remains disabled. All other architecture choices follow the prior controlled setup.
- Cubic B-splines have8total controls (6internal). Retain the tested detached gradient route: residual geometry learns from relation/object tokens and local image features without sending geometry gradients into the shared detector or predicted endpoints. Graph losses still train the detector. Thus “B-splines throughout” means geometry supervision in both stages, not fully coupled optimization.
- Straight controls retain a frozen zero-residual spline head for common geometry inference. Their curves are straight chords.
- Same approved quarter-turn/noise MRI augmentation; no zoom. Plants retain quarter-turns/flips and five-slice projection into padded64³ volumes.
- BN training statistics during updates, saved running statistics during evaluation. Offline W&B and fixed validation projections retained.

## Data and geometric supervision

New derived vascular caches are under `/datasets`, not the experiment output directory:

- IXI: `/lustre/fsn1/projects/rech/vnc/upz25mj/datasets/IXI/transfer_splines_k8_20261015`.
- Auxiliary SyntheticMRI: `/lustre/fsn1/projects/rech/vnc/upz25mj/datasets/syntheticMRI/transfer_source_k8_25k_20261015`.
- Plants reuse the existing25k contracted source and retained branch-path cache from the previous experiment.

IXI uses the existing `optimal_radius_0p75x_c095_vedo_original` sources/patches. Trace full stored paths before fitting, preserve junctions/endpoints and boundary anchors using the established closest-inside-centerline-sample policy, with exact intersection fallback for sparse clipped components. Straight and spline arms use identical nodes, edges, membership and full-path evaluation references. Intermediate degree-2 samples remain in curve guides, not object targets.

Unsupported parallel/closed branches and capacity overflow exclude the entire patch for EVERY arm; reasons are recorded. Original IXI active pool has13,742train/2,961val/2,384test patches, before this common compatibility check. All compatible validation/test patches are retained; final counts are only established by preparation. Failure to supply10k IXI or25k SyntheticMRI training patches blocks training. Source SyntheticMRI is limited to original training subjects with available full graphs; missing subjects are reported. Original source validation/test subjects are not imported as training data.

IXI graph paths are segmentation-derived uncertain references, not perfect anatomical truth. MRI metrics use original full-volume affines, never identity patch headers.

### Plant spline targets: previously missing integration

`PlantsDataset` optionally reads cached controls/curves/guides, verifies node/edge correspondence, swaps PNG axes, embeds curves at z=.5, applies the SAME sampled rotations/flips as the graph, and maps them through final padding. Controls are never clipped. Its returned geometry dictionary is supervised by the existing residual-control loss.

Plants have no physical millimetres. Define virtual isotropic voxel spacing as the median geometric-mean spacing across selected IXI TRAINING subjects. This scales the projected source geometry to the target loss's physical range; it is an explicit rendering assumption, not measured plant anatomy. Maintain a metric matrix through augmentation/padding so distances and canonical edge orientation remain consistent. The exact value is recorded in `monitoring.json` and each run's provenance. The source cache stays in original PNG units; only loading transforms it.

## Evaluation and execution gates

- Fixed hash-selected128validation and512training monitors, identical across arms; length-bin cutoffs computed on IXI training guides only.
- Checkpoint selection: validation common branch-F1, then native edge-F1. Full compatible validation evaluated for final and selected checkpoints, including common geometry and topology suite.
- After fine-tuning, evaluate the validation-selected checkpoint once on the fixed compatible IXI test set. Test outcomes never select checkpoints or adjust the setup.
- GPU smoke checks run three updates per stage/arm. They assert finite gradients, active domain classifiers in mixed runs, spline gradients in spline runs, and nonzero geometry loss gradients separately for source and target domains. Shared initialization hashes must agree across all six before production training starts.
- CPU smoke1125311 failed because the IXI source path required `graphs/adaptive/`; corrected without changing data. Replacement1125734 passed, accepting2train/2val/2test targets;3parallel-branch exclusions among24attempted candidates. No performance conclusion from this extraction check.
- Targeted coordinate tests:3passed (plant embedding and existing MRI spline rotation). All12stage configurations validated. GPU checks remain pending until full target preparation completes.

## Submitted jobs

Record: `experiments/ixi_transfer/submission-20261015.json`.

| Stage | Job |
|---|---|
|IXI target preparation|1126571|
|SyntheticMRI source preparation|1126575|
|GPU verification, six arms|1126576|
|Pretraining to25|1126577|
|Pretraining to50|1126578|
|Fine-tuning to50|1126579|
|Fine-tuning to100|1126580|
|Validation-selected held-out tests|1126581|

GPU arrays use indices0–5 with at most3concurrent tasks per array. Each task uses oneH100. `afterok` gates preparation/verification; `aftercorr` links the corresponding arm's later stages. Failed prerequisites cancel dependent jobs instead of launching an incomplete experiment.

Output: `/lustre/fsn1/projects/rech/vnc/upz25mj/experiments/gnbm/spline_learning/ixi_transfer_20261015/runs/`.
Config: `configs/ixi_transfer.yaml`. Runner: `scripts/train_ixi_transfer.py`; it reuses the existing loss, optimizer, matcher, augmentation, monitoring and metrics infrastructure. `source_mri` is an additional loader name for the existing vascular loader; `synthetic_mri` remains the internal target key but points to IXI here.

## Next research decision

First inspect full-population exclusions and GPU checks; then compare learning curves and final held-out metrics. This experiment tests auxiliary biological versus synthetic vascular sources under a fixed update budget. It does not isolate a single causal “biological alignment” mechanism or establish source-independent superiority. No new sweep or loss terms are authorized by this setup.

Submission check: both full preparation jobs are running; all GPU stages and tests are registered with the intended dependencies. The two training smoke targets were visually inspected in `previews/ixi-target-smoke.png`: retained paths align with the masks, but source-derived graphs do not explain every foreground fragment. This is a limitation of the existing extracted references, not evidence of anatomical completeness.

## Added matched protocol: graph-only pretraining → spline fine-tuning (2026-10-15)

All original jobs above are preserved. The original six-arm study includes spline supervision in both stages; earlier SyntheticMRI experiments introduced spline supervision only during fine-tuning. To distinguish these protocols, three additional fine-tunings reuse the existing graph-only pretraining checkpoints:

# HALVS replacement of the plant source domain — 2026-10-15

## Question and controlled comparison

Does a leaf-vein source improve SyntheticMRI graph generalization relative to plants?
Reuse the completed MRI-only control from `plant_generalization_20261014_da_b32_w1_restart`; it is identical and does not need another training. Run a new mixed HALVS/MRI pretraining from random initialization, followed by separate straight-edge and detached residual B-spline MRI fine-tunings. Do not mix plants and leaves yet.

## Plant field of view

The requested native64 crop was a separate inspection, not the training patching policy. The recovered plant generator downsamples by6 before cropping118 content pixels with5-pixel padding to128. This covers about708 original pixels, then the loader resizes to54 with padding into64³ and projects a five-slice slab.

`plants_3d2cut/prova/field_of_view/comparison.png` compares source crops64,256,708,1024 at the same original junction, displayed at64 pixels. They contain1,3,12,24 annotated points respectively (including degree-2). Wider crops capture more structure at the expense of fine-branch resolution. This illustration uses the photograph and occupancy-resized mask; actual training uses smoothed mask-derived images. Existing data were not overwritten. A larger plant FOV is feasible, but not yet applied to a new training population.

## HALVS extraction choices

- Dataset: `/lustre/fsn1/projects/rech/vnc/upz25mj/datasets/HALVS_DATASET`.
- Original parent-leaf split:144 train,6 validation. No cross-leaf resplitting; no patch-level random split.
- Reuse `leaf-veins-extractor` full-resolution skeleton tracing, snapshotted under `experiments/leaf_pretraining/reference/` with hashes.
- Primary+secondary veins (red+green). Tertiary veins excluded from BOTH image mask and graph; this experiment is not supervision of all leaf venation.
- Downscale5.42, effective source crop about640pixels,128px padded output, same plant loader and64³ slab projection.
- Keep extractor defaults: prune short terminal branches8pixels, merge junctions6pixels, curvature approximation tolerance6pixels. The segmentation still contains small traces pruned from the graph: extraction is an approximate annotation, not exact ground truth.
- Overlap87.5% to provide a pool for deterministic selection of25,000 accepted training patches and480 source validation patches. These are spatially correlated crops of144 leaves, not25,000 independent biological samples. Full extraction is uncapped so early filenames do not consume the budget.
- Existing extractor filters graphs with more than80 pre-contraction nodes. These exclusions are logged; source population is conditional on these filters.
- Preserve intermediate curve points during extraction; reuse our existing degree-2 contraction afterward, preserving boundary anchors at5/128 and122/128. Keep full paths in the spline cache. Existing unsupported closed/parallel branches are excluded and recorded, never silently collapsed into a different graph.
- Require exactly25,000/480 accepted patches; insufficient population fails preparation and blocks all training.
- Raw network inputs are smoothed/dilated selected-vein masks, as for the recovered plants recipe, NOT original leaf photographs. This tests morphology transfer under the existing pipeline.
- Pretraining supervises nodes/connectivity only. Stored source spline targets are in PNG coordinates/pixel units and are not used as MRI geometry targets.

## Training unchanged

Config: `configs/leaf_generalization_da_b32.yaml`; same training implementation as plants.

-50 pretraining epochs, batch32, seed364505, AdamW LR7e-5, weight decay1e-4, same polynomial schedule and one-epoch warmup.
-25k HALVS source + identical10k SyntheticMRI target.50k replacement draws/epoch, target upsampling2.5 for expected50:50 source/target exposure.
-Domain adaptation enabled with user-selected weight1.0 (image, instance and consistency components).
-Same approved augmentations: source quarter-turns/flips; MRI quarter-turns and Gaussian noise(probability.35,max std.015); no zoom; spline-safe coordinate transforms.
-Two100-epoch maximum vessel-only continuations from the best leaf mixed pretraining checkpoint: straight edges and8-control detached residual B-splines. Same graph losses and spline weight1.4739989612791453. Same early-stopping policy.
-Identical MRI training membership and1952 validation patches, common branch-F1 checkpoint selection, same final/best validation metrics. Held-out test remains untouched by this submission.
-W&B offline logs and validation projections retained. Internal arm/loader names retain `mixed`/`plants` for compatibility; this config's source is HALVS.

## Execution and artifacts

Output root: `/lustre/fsn1/projects/rech/vnc/upz25mj/experiments/gnbm/spline_learning/leaf_generalization_20261015`.

CPU extraction smoke → full extraction/contraction/audit → GPU smoke checks → pretraining25+25 → parallel straight/spline fine-tunings50+50. Slurm `afterok`/`aftercorr` dependencies and invalid-dependency cancellation prevent training after failed preparation/checks.

Preview cyan chords/red anchors show contracted GT, not model predictions. Continuous guides are retained separately. Run outputs: `runs/pretrain_mixed`, `runs/mixed_straight`, `runs/mixed_spline`.

## Pending interpretation

CPU smoke1093471 succeeded:2 train+2 val leaves,209/288 raw patches at80% overlap, and2/2 contracted targets. This small pool suggested80% overlap may not supply25k patches; full extraction uses87.5% overlap instead (same FOV, denser crop grid). No leaf performance result yet. Compare final and best MRI validation with the completed plants and MRI-only controls, separating geometry from graph detection. Check source graph density and coverage before proposing a larger plant FOV or joint plant+leaf pretraining. Overlapping leaf crops and approximate extracted targets limit any attribution to dataset diversity alone.

### Submission status

- Full preparation1094726: running at submission check.

### Dataset placement update

Dataset entries are now available at `/lustre/fsn1/projects/rech/vnc/upz25mj/datasets/HALVS_DATASET/patches_3d_transfer_20261015/`. They currently link to the experiment storage to avoid interrupting active readers. The attempted atomic directory exchange was unsupported by Lustre and made no data changes. CPU job1127211 waits for leaf fine-tuning array1094739, then moves the actual directories into the dataset folder and leaves reverse aliases at the old experiment paths. ## Completed training and held-out comparison submission

Leaf pretraining 1094733 and both continuation stages 1094737/1094739 completed successfully. These use `best.pt` selected by validation, not final checkpoints. This distinction can explain differences from previously reported final-checkpoint metrics.

Matched comparison includes leaves+MRI, plants+MRI and the equal-update MRI-only control, each with straight edges and detached residual B-splines. All six used graph-only pretraining; geometry is introduced only in spline fine-tuning. The fine-tuning data, training settings, model architecture and evaluation configuration were checked for equality. The source-domain difference is intentional, including its rendering/extraction and graph distributions; it is not an isolated test of biological species. Single-seed results do not establish statistical significance.

Validation on 1,952 patches: leaf spline edge F1 0.68793, plant spline 0.68524, MRI-only spline 0.72243; curve F1 0.45700, 0.45580 and 0.50357 respectively. New held-out evaluation uses all 13,071 original test IDs, verified against the existing comparison manifest with a recorded ordered-ID hash. All six validation-selected checkpoints use identical native node/edge mAP/mAR/F1, common curve/branch metrics, same-endpoint chord comparison and the existing core geometry/topology/Betti/APLS/TOPO diagnostics. No augmentation, BatchNorm recalibration, checkpoint reselection, threshold tuning or retraining. Saved running statistics are used.

- GPU smoke checks on two test patches for each leaf model: array **1145697**.
- Six full test evaluations, gated by smoke success: array **1145698**, at most three concurrent GPUs.

## Report 47

Source: `docs/research/pretraining/nonplanar-source-prototype.md`

<!-- BEGIN SOURCE: docs/research/pretraining/nonplanar-source-prototype.md -->

# Two-sample nonplanar plant prototype

## Question

Can we move plant nodes away from their original plane while applying the same deformation to the raw image and segmentation, then use the existing random rotations?

This is a separate rendering experiment. Existing datasets, training configurations and results are unchanged. It does not evaluate a model or demonstrate a transfer-learning improvement.

## Construction

Use two plant training patches selected deterministically: first two sample IDs in lexical order among existing accepted patches with at least six nodes and five edges. This structural eligibility makes nonplanarity observable; no selection by model performance. Read each through the actual `PlantsDataset`, including the original five-slice slab embedding, padding and axis convention.

1. Sample independent Gaussian depth offsets at nodes (standard deviation 5 voxels), then remove their mean.
2. Fit a smooth Gaussian radial-basis displacement field over the image plane (length scale 10 voxels, ridge 0.05). Smoothing means realized node shifts need not exactly equal the independent draws.
3. Apply one common amplitude scale if necessary to bound absolute displacement at 10 voxels and maximum depth slope at 1. This limits extreme stretching from neighbouring nodes with opposing shifts. Requested and realized offsets are recorded.
4. Deform every graph node and densely sampled reference path using `F(x,y,z)=(x,y,z+h(x,y))`. The graph's edge indices remain unchanged.
5. Resample the raw volume with the inverse mapping `I_new(x,y,z)=I_old(x,y,z-h(x,y))`, using linear interpolation. Warp the segmentation with the same mapping and nearest-neighbour interpolation. Never independently move nodes while leaving image pixels fixed.
6. Apply the existing quarter-turn and flip implementation identically to the image, mask, nodes and sampled paths. Coordinates follow the repository's voxel-index/axis-size convention.

The continuous warp has unit Jacobian determinant and an explicit inverse, so it does not fold space. Voxel resampling can still alter tiny details, and the prototype reports guide support in the masks before/after. Graph connectivity is preserved exactly, but branch lengths and directions change intentionally. Crop-face nodes on the original in-plane boundaries stay on those boundaries before rotation.

## Scope and limitations

This bends a planar slab into a nonplanar **height-field sheet**. It is a useful first augmentation but does not create arbitrary 3D anatomy or depth-separated projected crossings. Thickness remains the existing five-slice extrusion, now warped; no noise or tubular re-rendering is added in this experiment.

Dense paths are warped directly. Do NOT simply apply this nonlinear map to B-spline control points and assume the resulting spline is the exact transformed curve: a future training integration should refit controls to warped paths and recheck fit/coordinate units. The prototype exports nodes and warped paths, not misleading transformed K8 spline targets.

## Artifacts and reproduction

Code: `experiments/source_augmentation/prototype_nonplanar_plants.py`.
Run in the project's fixed training environment:

```bash
python experiments/source_augmentation/prototype_nonplanar_plants.py
```

Output (separate from original datasets): `/lustre/fsn1/projects/rech/vnc/upz25mj/experiments/gnbm/source_nonplanar_20261016/`.

- `nonplanar-plants.html`: self-contained interactive 3D comparison; download this single file and open locally. Original, warped, and warped+rotated panels. Select the sample; drag/zoom and toggle raw surface/reference paths/nodes in the legend.
- Per-sample PNG: raw-image isosurface + graph, plus side projection of the actual raw volume.
- Per-sample NPZ: original, warped and rotated raw/mask/node/path arrays, original edge indices and depth displacement field.
- `report.json`: parameters, realized displacements, guide-mask support and distance from the best-fit plane.

## Measured results (2026-10-16)

Seed: `364505`. Both samples completed; finite arrays, nodes within bounds, nonplanarity and rotation consistency checks passed.

| Sample | Nodes / edges | Guide points inside mask: original → warped → rotated | RMS distance from best-fit plane |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| sample_000001 | 8 / 6 | 98.96% → 98.96% → 98.96% | 1.80 voxels |
| sample_000002 | 10 / 7 | 93.08% → 93.08% → 93.08% | 2.23 voxels |

Actual node depth offsets span −2.94 to +3.02 voxels and −4.13 to +3.71 voxels, respectively. These are realized shifts after smoothing and amplitude limiting, not the initial Gaussian draws.

Both PNG renders were inspected: the raw structure and graph bend together and remain aligned after rotation. Existing imperfect guide-mask agreement remains; this augmentation does not repair source annotations. The quantitative check measures sampled guide support in the binary mask, not perfect raw-image correspondence or topology after voxelization.

Conclusion: this shared deformation is feasible on these two examples. It demonstrates consistent nonplanar augmentation, not improved learning or transfer. Before training integration, refit continuous targets to warped paths and check the resulting fit error. Keep a matched planar control when assessing any training benefit.

The small machine-readable result is also tracked at `experiments/source_augmentation/report.json`; large visualizations and arrays remain in the output directory above.

# Mixed plant pretraining recovery — 2026-10-14

## Recovered implementation

Original repository: `/lustre/fswork/projects/rech/vnc/upz25mj/projects/Image-to-Graph-Vessel/3d`.
Exact reference snapshots and SHA256 provenance: `experiments/plant_pretraining/reference/`.
These are archival references, not a new training entrypoint. In particular, the original generator's `__main__` overrides CLI arguments with hardcoded `/data/scavone` paths; do not execute it unchanged.

- `data/dataset_mixed.py`: concatenate source plants and target MRI. With target upsampling, target sample weight is source_count/target_count, giving equal expected source/target draws and twice the source count per epoch, with replacement. Both domains have supervised graph losses.
- `configs/mixed_plants_synth_HNS_3Dsynthmr.yaml`: 25,900 plants + 3,800 SyntheticMRI requested; 50 epochs, batch32, AdamW7e-5, decay1e-4. Image/graph adversarial and consistency options enabled, domain weight0.1. These are configuration facts, not proof of the exact historical run used by the user. A separate `pretrain_plants_synth_supcl.yaml` exists; its SupCL switch is false.
- `data/dataset_plants.py`: PNG image/segmentation plus VTP graph, resize to54², project into five slices, pad to64³; image scales to[-.5,.5]. Graph coordinates transform with projection/rotation. This is planar source anatomy embedded in3D, not a full3D vessel distribution.
- `data/generate_plants_data.py`: original image-level `splits.csv`, default6x downsampling,128² crops, graph clipping/pruning, optional degree2 contraction. Hardcoded example uses overlap.35 and budgets25923/6421/6737 with contraction. Those defaults do not establish the uploaded dataset's actual generation history.
- `data/generate_plants_augmented_data.py`: preserved alternate generator; not selected or run.

## Existing implementation to reuse

Current `data/loaders/plants.py`, `data/loaders/mixed.py`, `data/loaders/discovery.py`, `configs/pretrain_mixed.yaml` already provide compatible data loading and balanced sampling. Current pretrain config differs: batch48,4000MRI, explicit validation caps; domain adaptation disabled by base config. Do not claim it exactly reproduces the legacy approach.

Current plant loader corrects the stored(y,x) coordinates for the image reader, preserves small segmentation branches through occupancy downsampling, and disables random validation augmentation. Preserve these corrections rather than copying the older loader wholesale. Current plant augmentation uses quarter-turns and flips; the legacy loader has additional continuous/elastic options whose parity is not established.

## Uploaded dataset

Use `/lustre/fsn1/projects/rech/vnc/upz25mj/datasets/plants_3d2cut/patches_3d` as loader root, **not** the top-level root or `patches` (those use different graph layouts).
Observed counts:25923train,6421val,6737test, each raw/seg/vtp. Inventory snapshot records missing/empty triplets; upload may still be active, so this is not transfer completion certification.
Eight VTPs per train/val were read successfully. Some contain degree2 nodes (0–2 per sampled graph). Resolve whether they are legitimate retained boundary nodes or intermediate nodes before harmonizing topology; do not blindly contract boundary anchors. There are no confirmed continuous spline targets for these plant patches. Preserve original uploaded data.

## Recommended experiment after compatibility checks

User's50epoch mixed pretraining then100epoch vessel fine-tuning is a reasonable transfer baseline. It changes data diversity and initialization, not merely epoch count. With25k source patches and balanced sampling there are approximately50k draws/epoch; report updates/exposure as well as epochs.

1. Implement and verify rigid augmentation of image, nodes, controls, guides and coordinate metric consistently. Current spline loader explicitly rejects augmentation; all related scratch comparisons were constrained by this. Start with right-angle rotations/flips, not elastic changes to graph geometry.
2. Reuse mixed graph pretraining with a fixed25k plant manifest and only the existing MRI training membership. Keep vessel validation/test unchanged and plant splits separated by original image. Confirm patch-to-parent provenance before claiming independent plant splits.
3. Fine-tune matched straight and detached-residual spline models from the same pretrained graph checkpoint, for up to100epochs, selecting by declared validation reconstruction metrics. Plant graph-only supervision is sufficient for this pretraining hypothesis; continuous plant supervision would require real curve targets and a separate decision.
4. Compare against a matched vessel-only initialization/training control with identical augmentation and fine-tuning conditions. This distinguishes transfer from simply fixing augmentation. Avoid simultaneously restoring legacy domain-adversarial losses, edge sampling, optimizer schedules and other changes without a specific ablation.

Expected benefit: diverse branching patterns and orientation exposure may improve graph feature transfer. This is a hypothesis, not a guarantee; slab-to-volume domain mismatch remains. More epochs or relation-negative reweighting alone did not resolve the gap. Mixed pretraining does not establish that spline training from scratch is impossible.

No plant pretraining or regeneration was launched in this task. Remaining gates: upload completion, topology/provenance harmonization, spline augmentation implementation, and a short mixed-batch forward/loss smoke before training.

Loader check limitation: direct mutable-environment item loading failed because `SimpleITK._version` is missing. VTP reads and all-file triplet inventory passed (no missing or zero-byte counterparts). Use the established fixed runtime archive for the next mixed-batch smoke; do not infer a dataset defect from this environment failure or silently substitute another image reader.

Update: the authorized preparation, augmentation implementation and training submission are recorded in [generalization-training.md](generalization-training.md). Fixed-runtime GPU smoke tests passed; the mutable-environment limitation above no longer blocks these runs.

# Plant/leaf augmentation integration

Implemented 2026-10-16; completed verification and status review 2026-10-17.

## Status

Available as an opt-in training policy in the shared `PlantsDataset`, which also loads the leaf and combined biological datasets. Implementation verification initially involved no training. On 2026-10-18 the matched SyntheticMRI training chains were submitted; see [the launch record](augmented-source-comparison.md). Visual plausibility and geometric consistency have been checked; a learning/generalization improvement has not been demonstrated.

## Policy

1. Load the generator-produced mask-like raw image, preserving its soft foreground profile. Embed and pad using existing conventions.
2. Sample independent node depth shifts (Gaussian sigma 5 voxels), subtract their mean, fit a smooth Gaussian RBF field (length 10 voxels, ridge 0.05). Limit maximum depth shift to 10 voxels, slope to 1, and available volume clearance. One field warps the image, mask, nodes and branch paths. Raw uses linear interpolation; mask uses nearest neighbour. No topology changes or node removal.
3. For continuous supervision, densify the original stored annotation polylines to 257 samples before warping; refit endpoint-constrained cubic B-splines with the configured control count (K8 in these plans). Resample guides along the deformed paths. Do not directly warp old control positions. Distances use the existing virtual voxel spacing; it is not measured plant anatomy.
4. Render correlated background throughout the padded cube. Reuse prototype slow-field sigma8 and correlated-field sigma1.2; background mean varies uniformly 0.18–0.26, foreground mean 0.62–0.82, noise strength 0.75–1.25 times the prototype, boundary smoothing sigma0.5–0.8 voxels. Texture and parameters are drawn afresh per retrieval. These ranges are mild extensions of the preferred visual prototype, not calibrated MRI statistics.
5. Apply existing quarter-turns/flips consistently to images, nodes and targets. Update the geometry metric for the rigid transform. Do not min/max normalize or add empty padding after rendering, because that would undo the intended background/intensity policy.

Intensity remains [-0.5,0.5]. Masks remain binary labels. Foreground softening changes apparent thickness, not labels. Geometry is still a warped sheet rather than arbitrary volumetric anatomy. The policy is applied only when training augmentation and its own enabled flag are true. Validation/test and old configurations follow the previous path. NumPy receives a per-item seed from the existing worker-seeded Python RNG; equal seed and retrieval order reproduce outputs.

## Configuration and files

Plan option (copied by the training configuration builder to `augmentation.plants.source_augmentation`):

```yaml
source_augmentation:
  enabled: true
  nonplanar: true
  textured_soft: true
```

The last two flags can be disabled independently for controlled ablations. Separate configurations preserve the old plans and use distinct output roots/tracking groups:

- `configs/plant_generalization_da_b32_source_aug.yaml`
- `configs/leaf_generalization_da_b32_source_aug.yaml`
- `configs/combined_generalization_da_b32_source_aug.yaml`
- `configs/ixi_transfer_source_aug.yaml`

The source-transfer stage policy is unchanged: the SyntheticMRI plans pretrain graph-only and introduce splines in fine-tuning; the IXI runner supports both-stage or delayed spline variants. Enabling augmentation does not silently change that scientific choice, sampling, losses, batch size or epochs. MRI-only arms are unaffected because they have no biological source loader.

Implementation: `data/source_augmentation.py`, `data/loaders/plants.py`, `data/loaders/mixed.py`, `scripts/train_plant_generalization.py`. The IXI runner reuses that configuration builder.

## Checks

- All four configuration builders validate with augmentation enabled, including IXI K8 pretraining with the recorded virtual spacing 0.5601755961.
- Four focused tests passed: new source-warp/refit test and existing spline projection/rotation tests.
- Actual loader checked on two plant and two leaf training samples, each with K8 targets. Endpoints match nodes; edges unchanged; arrays finite and nodes inside the cube. Equal seed gives identical input. Validation with the option enabled matches old validation output exactly, including geometry.
- Four samples collate through the existing training collator; graph-only source-loading route also passed.
- Mean refit error: 0.00930/0.00698 voxels for plants; 0.02508/0.02259 for leaves. Maximum sampled error: 0.201/0.151/0.491/0.445 voxels. These compare arc-resampled fitted curves with warped guides; they are not learned-model errors.
- Guide-mask support: plants 98.96→98.18% and 93.08→93.08%; leaves 84.31→84.44% and 87.32→87.32%. Existing leaf annotation/mask discrepancies remain. Small differences reflect warp voxelization and guide resampling.
- Observed per-item loader time 0.126–0.360 seconds in the four-sample CPU check; not a full DataLoader throughput or GPU utilization benchmark.
- Plant and leaf preview PNGs visually inspected. Different projected crossings in a MIP do not imply changed 3D connectivity.

Numeric record: `experiments/source_augmentation/training-loader-check.json`.
Previews: `/lustre/fsn1/projects/rech/vnc/upz25mj/experiments/gnbm/source_augmentation_loader_20261016/`.
Reproduction script: `experiments/source_augmentation/check_training_augmentation.py --output /path/to/new/folder` in the fixed project environment.

## Scheduler/results review — 2026-10-17

Scheduler queue empty at review. Previously cancelled/failed job entries are historical and have successful replacement chains (see the disk-recovery and overfit reports); no pending dependency chain found. Source-transfer, IXI full-100-epoch continuations and their held-out evaluations are complete. No new augmentation-training results exist.

The previous SyntheticMRI comparison remains led by MRI-only spline: edge F1 0.7258 and curve F1 0.5097; plants spline 0.6879/0.4581; leaves spline 0.6905/0.4607; combined spline 0.6809/0.4484. IXI spline throughout: IXI-only 0.16395/0.12215; plants+IXI 0.12090/0.09441; SyntheticMRI+IXI 0.11126/0.09214. Single seed, different target datasets: do not compare the numeric scales across tables as a controlled dataset effect.

## Next decision

Run a short model forward/backward smoke with the new resolved configuration before substantial training, then compare augmented versus existing source rendering under identical membership, budgets and stage policy. Existing training comparisons are the baseline, not evidence that the new augmentation improves transfer. No long runs were launched during implementation.

## Follow-up submission — 2026-10-18

[Three source pretrainings, six matched fine-tunings and dependent held-out tests](augmented-source-comparison.md) now queued behind running GPU smoke gates. This supersedes the earlier no-training status; results are still pending.

<!-- BEGIN SOURCE: docs/research/pretraining/textured-source-prototype.md -->

# Simple textured-background plant prototype

Date: 2026-10-16. Appearance prototype only; no dataset or training settings changed.

## Input provenance

Verified `Image-to-Graph-Vessel/3d/data/generate_plants_data.py`, lines 311–325: the saved raw input is generated from the segmentation with four 3×3 all-ones convolutions, saturation at 1 and conversion to 8-bit intensity. It is not the original RGB photograph. `PlantsDataset` subsequently resizes it, embeds it into a five-slice slab, scales to [-0.5,0.5], and pads the volume.

The generated input is mask-like but not strictly binary after resizing/warping: the two planar prototypes have 29 and 30 distinct intensities. Therefore use `alpha=clip(raw+0.5,0,1)` as the existing soft foreground coverage rather than discarding its interpolation profile or replacing it with the narrower segmentation. The segmentation and graph annotations remain unchanged.

Reuse both samples from the nonplanar prototype, each in planar and nonplanar form. This yields four cases with three appearance variants each. No new geometries are sampled. Appearance is shown before rotation to make the original slab orientation easy to inspect; a later training integration must rotate the completed image and annotations together.

## Minimal construction

Seed 364506. In normalized [0,1] intensity units:

- Generate independent Gaussian fields: standardized slow variation (Gaussian smoothing sigma 8 voxels), standardized correlated texture (sigma 1.2 voxels), and unsmoothed unit noise.
- Background B = clip(0.22 + 0.045 slow + 0.035 texture + 0.015 noise, 0, 1).
- Foreground F = clip(0.72 + 0.04 slow + 0.025 texture + 0.015 noise, 0, 1).
- Textured variant: I = (1-alpha) B + alpha F.
- Softened variant: same B and F, but smooth alpha in 3D with Gaussian sigma 0.65 voxels before compositing.

The same texture realization is used for the two textured variants within each case. Textures differ between planar/nonplanar cases; use within-case columns for controlled appearance comparisons. Every zero-alpha voxel in the unsoftened variant receives exactly B, including background pixels within the slab and original padding. There is no slice-sized pasted background rectangle. Texture is also present in foreground intensities rather than leaving saturated flat white branches.

These constants are illustrative, not fitted to MRI or claimed as a physical MRI noise model. No real MRI image is pasted into the background, avoiding accidental unlabeled vessels. Background textures can still create distracting bright regions. The Gaussian texture lacks real anatomical tissue structure.

## Verification and observations

Four cases completed with finite intensities in [0,1]; the exact zero-alpha replacement assertion passed. Nodes, edges, masks and dense guides are copied unchanged into NPZ outputs. The original foreground already extends beyond the segmentation due to generation/resizing; this discrepancy is not repaired. Boundary softening further alters apparent thickness and contrast, without changing annotations.

Inspected PNGs for sample_000001 nonplanar and sample_000002 planar: background is continuous through and outside the embedded structure; foreground remains visible; soft boundaries remove abrupt extrusion edges. The planar geometry still looks like an extruded sheet. This appearance change does not solve that geometric limitation and provides no evidence of improved transfer yet.

Across the four cases, mean intensity inside the mask is 0.68099–0.72669 for the textured variant and 0.64235–0.68360 for the softened version. Outside-mask mean is approximately 0.224 (includes generator foreground halos). Full values: `experiments/source_augmentation/texture-report.json`.

## Artifacts and reproduction

Output: `/lustre/fsn1/projects/rech/vnc/upz25mj/experiments/gnbm/source_texture_20261016/`.

- `textured-plants.html`: standalone, offline slice viewer (~5.4 MB); download just this file. Select sample/geometry, move three orthogonal slice sliders, optionally overlay mask outlines and nearby nodes. Shared [0,1] display limits across columns.
- Four PNGs: orthogonal slices and a maximum intensity projection.
- Four NPZs: three input variants, background, mask, nodes, paths and edges.
- `report.json`: measured intensity summaries.

```bash
source cluster/jean_zay/env.sh
OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 python experiments/source_augmentation/prototype_textured_background.py --output /path/to/new/output
```

The command requires a new output folder, preserving previous prototypes. Python syntax and numerical checks passed; PNGs were visually inspected. The HTML was not exercised in a browser on the cluster.

## Requested SyntheticMRI + IXI pretraining: already completed

Checked the existing completion markers and held-out test summaries rather than submitting duplicate jobs. Configuration: `configs/ixi_transfer.yaml`; results under `/lustre/fsn1/projects/rech/vnc/upz25mj/experiments/gnbm/spline_learning/ixi_transfer_20261015/runs/`.

Mixed pretraining starts from scratch: 25,000 SyntheticMRI source patches + 10,000 IXI target patches, 50 epochs, 50,000 replacement draws/epoch, balanced expected source/target sampling (target weight 2.5), batch 32, domain loss weight 1.0. Fine-tuning: 100 epochs on the same IXI training population, domain adaptation disabled. All arms share IXI validation/test membership; test has 2,178 patches. Best checkpoint is selected on validation, not test. Geometry uses K8 residual splines with detached geometry gradients, not fully coupled geometry optimization. These runs use the original source rendering, not this prototype.

| Pretraining source | Representation | Best fine-tuning epoch | Test node F1 | Test edge F1 | Test curve F1 |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| IXI only | Straight | 100 | 0.47404 | 0.15985 | 0.11644 |
| Plants + IXI | Straight | 80 | 0.44480 | 0.12084 | 0.09022 |
| SyntheticMRI + IXI | Straight | 95 | 0.44676 | 0.11688 | 0.08831 |
| IXI only | Spline throughout | 100 | 0.47369 | 0.16395 | 0.12215 |
| Plants + IXI | Spline throughout | 100 | 0.45038 | 0.12090 | 0.09441 |
| SyntheticMRI + IXI | Spline throughout | 100 | 0.44171 | 0.11126 | 0.09214 |
| SyntheticMRI + IXI | Spline only during fine-tuning | 85 | 0.44243 | 0.11373 | 0.08963 |

All finished the 100-epoch fine-tuning budget; best epoch can be earlier. Test summaries are `<arm>/held-out-test/summary.json`; relevant arms are `synthetic_straight`, `synthetic_spline`, `synthetic_delayed_spline`. In this single-seed setup synthetic vessels did not outperform plants or the IXI-only baseline on edge/curve F1. This does not prove synthetic pretraining cannot help under other settings. The IXI-only control matches update count, not IXI exposure: all its draws are IXI. Existing leaf comparisons target SyntheticMRI, so they cannot be inserted into this IXI table as a matched comparison.

## Report 53

Source: `docs/research/metrics/1-ixi-supervision-audit.md`

<!-- BEGIN SOURCE: docs/research/metrics/1-ixi-supervision-audit.md -->

# 1. IXI supervision and prediction audit — 2026-10-18

## Scope and conclusion

Completed a validation-only, read-only audit of the IXI-only **delayed B-spline** model (`ixi_delayed_spline`, saved validation step 028170). This is the straight pretraining → spline fine-tuning arm, not spline supervision throughout pretraining. No training, decoding thresholds, targets, or benchmark metrics changed.

The selected references are spatially consistent with the segmentation. This **does not certify anatomical topology or completeness**: graphs and masks can share extraction errors. Predictions show substantial foreground preference over random points, but poor localization and connectivity. Both node placement and relation prediction warrant attention.

## Protocol

- 16 validation patches, one per filename-derived subject; deterministic SHA256 ranking independent of predictions/results. Selection is reproducible in `summary.json`.
- Raw volumes and masks loaded in native array axes. Coordinates follow loader convention `index / shape`; physical metric comes from spline cache, not potentially identity patch headers.
- Valid extent is voxel faces `[-0.5, size-0.5]`, including boundary nodes. Within that extent, sample border intensity/mask by nearest extension. Truly outside points cannot count as supported.
- Curves resampled at intervals ≤0.25 mm. Mask occupancy uses nearest voxel; proximity uses exact distance to foreground voxel centres, not a smooth surface distance.
- 4,096 seeded uniform points per patch in the voxel-centre bounding box serve as a simple random spatial control. They are not a learned-model baseline.
- Numbers below are macro averages over patches; empty predicted curves are excluded from curve-support averages and recorded with zero count/null support in CSV.
- Foreground completeness flag: a mask voxel is explained if within the radius at its nearest GT guide point plus one largest voxel spacing. Radius is distance to background. This is a permissive thickness-aware **heuristic**, not a recall metric; it can miss annotation defects and flag legitimate geometry.
- Full-validation endpoint/relation counts reuse `relation-diagnostic.json` alongside the saved predictions. Positional maximum-cardinality matching, no degree matching; 1 and 2 mm sensitivity. This differs from the main benchmark's matching, so counts must not be substituted for benchmark TP/F1.

## Foreground support

| Points | Inside mask | Within 1 mm of foreground voxel centres |
|---|---:|---:|
| GT nodes |100.0%|100.0%|
| GT full-path curves |99.52%|100.0%|
| Predicted nodes |34.25%|65.57%|
| Predicted spline curves |28.73%|62.04%|
| Random spatial points |0.94%|3.06%|

Mean thickness-aware unexplained foreground: **2.61%**. This is encouraging for spatial supervision, not proof all true vessels have labels. GT checks use original full paths, not fitted GT spline controls; target-fit error/topological correctness remain separate questions. Model curves are evaluated where present, so good support would not imply complete reconstruction.

## Node versus relation accounting

Counts are over all 51,937 supported GT edges across 2,649 validation patches. No closed/parallel targets were excluded in this saved diagnostic.

| Matching tolerance | Missing ≥1 endpoint | Both endpoints recovered, no direct relation | Correct direct relation |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
|1 mm|48,096 (92.60%)|3,251 (6.26%)|590 (1.14%)|
|2 mm|36,033 (69.38%)|13,738 (26.45%)|2,166 (4.17%)|

At 2 mm, node recall is **50.82%**. Conditional direct relation recall is **13.62%** among the 15,904 recoverable endpoint pairs. For the longest arc-length quartile it is **6.57%**, versus **14.45%** for the shortest. Long relations are harder here, but node errors already prevent most GT edges being recovered. Conditional rates also depend on which nodes are recovered; they do not isolate a causal relation-head defect. Full length bins and nearby-negative pair selection rates are preserved in `full-validation-relations.json`.

## Visual review and limitations

Generated 16 orthogonal slice panels and a standalone slice viewer with independent mask/GT/prediction toggles. Each PNG selects the greatest mask-area slice per axis; it is not a complete volume review. Inspected panels for `sample_000001_0133`, `sample_000012_0032`, `sample_000163_0050`, and `sample_000166_0057` directly. GT generally follows bright vessel structures in these slices; predictions are sparse and sometimes displaced. The 000163 example was also selected for review because the preliminary completeness heuristic flagged it. Slice fragments must not be interpreted as disconnected 3D branches.

Still needed before declaring GT “good enough” anatomically: review suspected omissions/connections through adjacent slices, check difficult small vessels/boundary terminations, and obtain independent annotation review for ambiguous cases. Agreement between a mask and a graph extracted from that mask is not independent validation. No threshold here automatically approves or rejects a dataset.

The foreground check measures graph output support, not a segmentation head or encoder probe. It establishes that output locations are not spatially random, but cannot identify where inside the network foreground information is lost.

## Next decision

Review the viewer's ambiguous cases first. If no material annotation errors emerge, prioritize foreground-supported node localization and conditional connectivity. A small frozen-feature foreground probe can distinguish whether the image features encode foreground from whether graph decoding uses it; an oracle-endpoint relation experiment can further isolate connectivity. These are **proposals, not launched experiments**. Do not introduce new losses or regenerate all GT based on this small audit alone.

## Files and reproduction

Artifacts: `experiments/ixi_supervision_audit/20261018/`:

- `summary.json`, `per-patch.csv`, `full-validation-relations.json`: compact tracked evidence.
- `viewer.html`: download this file alone and open locally; no server or internet required.
- `sample_*.png`: static raw/overlay panels. HTML/PNGs stay local and are reproducible, avoiding binary growth in git.

```bash
source cluster/jean_zay/env.sh
source cluster/jean_zay/stage_spline_runtime.sh
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1
python scripts/audit_ixi_supervision.py \
  --dataset /lustre/fsn1/projects/rech/vnc/upz25mj/datasets/IXI/transfer_splines_k8_20261015 \
  --prediction-dir /lustre/fsn1/projects/rech/vnc/upz25mj/experiments/gnbm/spline_learning/ixi_transfer_20261015/runs/ixi_delayed_spline/best-full-validation/validation-028170 \
  --output experiments/ixi_supervision_audit/20261018 --samples 16
```

Checks: syntax/imports; small physical-coordinate/anisotropic-axis check; voxel-face boundary support, outside exclusion and empty predictions; successful 16-patch run; partition counts add exactly. Initial audit-only bounds and orthogonality checks were corrected for actual voxel-face clipping and affine float precision before recording results. No dataset/model changes. Interactive browser execution was not tested on the cluster; static rendered images were inspected.


## Image inspection: method and observed examples

The raw MRI is displayed in its native voxel axes, with grayscale display limits at the patch's 1st/99.5th intensity percentiles. Static panels show the slice with greatest mask area along each axis; the HTML viewer allows adjacent-slice navigation and independent overlay toggles. Cyan contours mark mask foreground; green sampled paths/crosses show GT curves/nodes; magenta marks predictions. Only points within 0.75 voxel of a displayed slice are overlaid.

Inspected static examples: `sample_000012_0032` shows GT paths running inside bright branching structures and predicted points sometimes displaced from them; `sample_000001_0133` shows GT support on multiple bright vessel sections with predictions concentrated on a smaller portion; `sample_000166_0057` shows strong background texture and sparse predictions despite visible reference vessels. `sample_000163_0050` was additionally reviewed after a completeness flag. These views motivate review of possible omissions but do not resolve all anatomy through a complete slice sequence.

Quantitative checks use nearest-voxel mask occupancy, physical nearest-foreground distance, raw intensity sampled at graph points and thickness-aware mask coverage. They complement the displayed image evidence; they are not pixelwise model segmentation predictions.

## Report 54

Source: `docs/research/metrics/2-ixi-feature-node-diagnostics.md`

<!-- BEGIN SOURCE: docs/research/metrics/2-ixi-feature-node-diagnostics.md -->

# 2. IXI feature and node diagnostics — 2026-10-18

## Research question and status

Follow-up to [the supervision audit](1-ixi-supervision-audit.md). **Completed and inspected.** Smoke 1262339 completed in 1m00s; full diagnostics 1262340 completed in 1m15s (Slurm elapsed, including setup). Both exit 0. The detector remained frozen, including BN buffers.

- Smoke job **1262339**: four train/four validation patches, 20 probe updates; GPU inference, hooks, frozen-state checks, probe fitting, node accounting and rendering.
- Full job **1262340**, `afterok:1262339`: 128 training / 64 validation patches, 1000 fixed probe updates. One H100, six CPUs, two-hour allocation (a limit, not a runtime estimate).
- Same IXI-only delayed-spline best checkpoint as the supervision audit. Straight pretraining followed by spline fine-tuning. No updates to the detector, no BN recalibration, no data augmentation. Strict checkpoint loading.
- Deterministic subject-round-robin patch selection; train and validation filename-derived subject sets asserted disjoint. No test samples. Read exact IDs/checkpoint step from the output summary.

## 1. Frozen-feature foreground probes

Train small linear voxel classifiers on frozen features:

1. early CNN (`encoder.layer0.relu1`),
2. projected CNN features immediately before transformer encoder,
3. transformer encoder memory reshaped back to the same spatial grid,
4. raw input intensity control,
5. encoder features with randomly permuted training labels (negative control).

All probes use the same 512 sampled training voxels per patch, balanced 256 foreground / 256 background. Scarce foreground uses replacement. Feature standardization uses training samples only. Each readout uses Adam, LR 0.01, weight decay 1e-4, batch 2048, fixed 1000 updates. No validation-based selection or architecture search. Save fitting histories: an unconverged readout is not evidence that features lack information.

Evaluate all probes on identical independently sampled 2048 uniform voxels per training/validation patch, at natural foreground prevalence. Primary score: average precision, with prevalence as the random-ranking reference. Also save ROC AUC and descriptive Dice at 0.5. Scores/Dice are uncalibrated because fitting uses balanced samples. Training evaluation can overlap fitting voxels; it is deliberately a within-training-patch diagnostic. Validation subjects remain disjoint.

Early CNN and transformer stages differ in spatial resolution, so that comparison confounds depth and resolution. **Projected CNN versus encoder** has equal channels/spatial grid and is the main controlled comparison. All sampling uses trilinear normalized dense-grid interpolation (`align_corners=False`); this approximates the true CNN receptive-field phase. Poor absolute fine-vessel reconstruction could reflect coarse spatial sampling. Linear readout failure cannot establish that no nonlinear decoder could recover information.

Detector eval mode is retained throughout feature extraction. All parameters have gradients disabled. Assert unchanged BN/other buffers, unchanged parameter version counters, and absent detector gradients before fitting readouts.

## 2. Node localization breakdown

Use the existing node decoding threshold/argmax rule. Do not change object confidence or graph predictions. Categories derive from GT boundary flags and graph degree, with boundary taking priority; interior junction degree ≥3, termination degree 1, other explicitly retained.

At both 1 and 2 mm:

1. Maximum-cardinality positional matching identifies recovered GT nodes.
2. Reserve remaining predictions within the tolerance of an already recovered GT node as **duplicate candidates** (proximity flag, not anatomical proof).
3. Match remaining predictions/GT up to twice the tolerance to identify **displaced** nodes.
4. Remaining GT nodes are **missing**; remaining predictions are **unmatched other**.

Save per-node rows, coordinates, displacement errors and nearest distance from *any* object query (including confidence-rejected queries). A nearby unselected query flags confidence/query-assignment ambiguity, not a recovered object. The displaced radius is an explicit diagnostic convention, not a new benchmark threshold. Train/validation comparisons are stratified by GT node type; different patch difficulty remains a confound.

A CPU crafted example checked recovered/displaced/missing/duplicate accounting and a perfect foreground AP example. It exposed an ambiguity in secondary matching; duplicate reservation now occurs before displacement matching. Syntax and Slurm shell checks passed. GPU checks are gated by the smoke job.

## Reading the results

- Good projected-CNN AP, weak encoder AP: loss of **linear accessibility** across encoder is supported, not proof of complete information collapse.
- Good CNN and encoder probes, poor node recovery: investigate object-token decoding, node objectives/query assignment and confidence filtering.
- Weak probes including early CNN: investigate feature learning, image/reference mismatch and spatial resolution; compare the raw-intensity control before blaming the transformer.
- Good training-node recovery but poor validation: evidence for a generalization gap; inspect subtype and patch difficulty before attributing it entirely to overfitting.
- Boundary-only failures: prioritize cropping/target conventions. Junction-only failures: junction supervision and node context deserve attention.
- High duplicate-candidate count: inspect object matching/confidence. High displaced count: focus on coordinate localization. Missing nodes require examining both confidence-rejected queries and image features.

No new detector loss, architecture change, GT regeneration or full training is authorized by these diagnostic outcomes alone. Results guide the next discussion.

## Outputs and reproduction

Full results: `experiments/ixi_features_nodes/20261018/full-1262340/`:

- `results.md`: generated score/node tables with embedded images.
- `summary.json`: checkpoint, exact IDs, feature shapes, protocol, aggregate scores/counts.
- `probe-per-patch.csv`, `node-errors.csv`: detailed analysis.
- `probe-history.json`: optimization checks.
- `overview.png`, `train-*.png`, `val-*.png`: comparative panels. First two patches per split, selected without looking at performance. Node overlays show points within 1.5 voxels of the displayed slice; absence in a slice is not absence in the whole patch.
- `probes.pt`: tiny fitted readouts and standardization parameters. No feature caches or duplicate detector weights saved.

Logs: `experiments/spline_learning/logs/ixi-features-nodes-{1262339,1262340}.{out,err}`.

Implementation: `scripts/diagnose_ixi_features_nodes.py`, `cluster/jean_zay/ixi_features_nodes.slurm`. Run via `sbatch ... smoke`, then `sbatch --dependency=afterok:SMOKE_JOB ... full`. Each output directory includes its job ID and refuses overwrite. Submission metadata is tracked; generated outputs remain local until compact evidence is reviewed and archived.


## Results and interpretation

Same checkpoint step 28170. 128 training patches, 64 validation patches, natural evaluation prevalence 0.80% / 0.86%. These AP values are **voxel foreground probe AP**, not graph node/edge mAP.

| Probe | Train AP | Validation AP | Feature grid |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Early CNN |0.6318|0.6551|32³, 64 channels|
| Projected CNN |0.0263|0.0271|2³, 552 channels|
| Transformer encoder |0.0287|0.0246|2³, 552 channels|
| Raw intensity |0.6437|0.6802|64³, 1 channel|
| Encoder, shuffled fitting labels |0.0231|0.0157|2³, 552 channels|

The early CNN has useful foreground information that transfers to these validation subjects. Raw intensity alone is also informative against these masks; neither result establishes learned topology or foreground specificity against every bright non-vessel structure. The inspected 000166 slice shows a strong early-probe response at a bright boundary outside the mask.

**No strong encoder-specific collapse is demonstrated for this trained IXI checkpoint:** projected-CNN and encoder readouts are similarly weak. Their 2×2×2 grid limits a linear spatial readout to very smooth fields. Information may still be encoded in channels and require a different decoder. These results cannot resolve collapse in the earlier failed scratch checkpoint, which was not loaded here. Coarse spatial representation/readout is a more immediate hypothesis to test than attributing everything to the transformer.

Probe fitting histories: early-CNN balanced BCE 0.580→0.174; projected CNN 0.739→0.404; encoder 0.767→0.396. They optimized, with some continued slow improvement; this is not a convergence proof. Shuffled-label BCE remained near 0.70. Its AP exceeds prevalence, so do not claim statistical superiority over a randomization distribution from this single control. Correlated patches/voxels and incidental spatial ranking remain relevant.

### Nodes at 2 mm

| GT type | Train recovered | Validation recovered |
|---|---:|---:|
| All |1726/2721 = 63.43%|847/1657 = 51.12%|
| Boundary |785/1127 = 69.65%|412/665 = 61.95%|
| Interior junction |593/877 = 67.62%|275/573 = 47.99%|
| Interior termination |348/717 = 48.54%|159/417 = 38.13%|

Validation also contains 283 displaced GT nodes (17.08%, matched between 2 and 4 mm) and 527 missing (31.80%). Duplicate candidates: 325 train / 209 validation; unmatched other predictions: 765 / 476. Raw counts must not be compared without accounting for population size.

There is a node generalization gap, especially for junctions, **plus substantial training-set error**. This is not explained by pure validation overfitting alone. Interior terminations are hardest in both splits; boundary nodes are the strongest category, so there is no evidence of a boundary-only implementation failure here.

547 of 810 unrecovered validation GT nodes have some object query within 2 mm. This includes low-confidence queries and already-assigned queries; it is not unique matching and does not prove confidence suppression. It motivates a future confidence/query-assignment check, not automatic threshold lowering (which could exacerbate duplicates).

### Inspected artifacts and next decision

Inspected full-run overview and both fixed validation slice panels directly. They confirm smooth projected/encoder readouts and spatially detailed early-CNN responses. Node slice overlays are examples, not an exhaustive node-label audit.

Recommended next intervention to discuss: give node localization access to higher-resolution image features, with a controlled comparison from the same checkpoint, or first test a coordinate-aware readout to separate channel encoding from spatial-resolution limits. Preserve the graph-only control and identical data/updates. A confidence/assignment diagnostic is a cheaper complementary check. Do not claim that increasing feature resolution is already proven to fix graph extraction. Relation isolation remains a separate, unrun experiment.


### Spatial-resolution control (CPU, no additional model training)

Reused the exact evaluation voxel sampling, verifying per-patch foreground counts and the raw-intensity AP check. Mean-pool raw/mask to a coarse grid and trilinearly reconstruct:

| Reference/control | Train foreground AP | Validation foreground AP |
|---|---:|---:|
| Raw intensity pooled to 2³ |0.0112|0.0110|
| GT mask pooled to 2³ |0.0789|0.0665|
| GT mask pooled to 32³ |0.9451|0.9512|

Even a coarse reconstruction built directly from labels loses most fine-vessel localization. This confirms a substantial spatial-resolution confound in the simple pointwise probe. The pooled mask is **not a rigorous upper bound** for learned channel representations or a model prediction. It supports testing access to finer spatial features, but cannot establish that channel-encoded detail has been destroyed.

Direct raw-intensity AP differs from the float fitted scalar readout by 0.000286 on training and <0.000001 on validation (float rank ties/saturation can affect AP). Per-patch labels/counts reproduce exactly; the difference is recorded, not hidden. `scripts/ixi_probe_resolution_control.py` writes `resolution-controls.json`; the Slurm wrapper now includes it for future full runs. This completed run used the same script as a separate CPU follow-up.

### Preserved evidence

Reviewed results, CSVs, fitting histories, small fitted probes and the five PNG panels are copied to [the evidence folder](../evidence/ixi_features_nodes_20261018/results.md). The original job output remains intact. This is about 2.5 MB; no detector weights or feature caches were duplicated. The research interpretation above is authoritative over the automatically generated descriptive tables.


## Image inspection: method and observed examples

The overview plots measured foreground average precision and GT node outcome fractions. For fixed training/validation examples, panels display raw MRI, the binary mask, node crosses, and spatial foreground scores from fitted linear classifiers. These score maps are obtained by applying each readout to frozen features, trilinearly interpolating logits to the input grid, then applying sigmoid. A single greatest-mask-area slice along axis0 is displayed. Node overlays include points within1.5voxels of the slice. The maps visualize what a small supervised readout can recover from each feature stage.

Inspected `val-sample_000040_0078.png`: the early-CNN map follows the bright curved vessel region, whereas projected-CNN/encoder maps vary smoothly over broad areas. In `val-sample_000166_0036.png`, early-CNN scores also light up a bright tissue boundary outside the vessel mask, showing that fine spatial response does not guarantee vessel specificity. The raw-intensity control highlights bright image structures as expected. These observations agree with the coarse2³ versus early32³ feature grids and motivate resolution-aware interpretation of AP.

# 3. IXI higher-resolution node refinement pilot — 2026-10-18

## Question and design

Follow-up to [frozen feature/node diagnostics](2-ixi-feature-node-diagnostics.md): can early 32³ CNN features improve node localization compared with the existing node heads fed by transformer tokens derived from a 2³ image grid?

Three matched arms from **IXI-only delayed B-spline best checkpoint, step 28170**:

| Array task | Arm | Node heads updated | Added refinement |
|---|---|---|---|
|0|baseline|Existing class/coordinate MLPs|None|
|1|local_image|Existing heads + refinement|Early CNN image samples, node token, proposed coordinates|
|2|zero_image|Existing heads + refinement|Same architecture, image samples set to zero|

Backbone, transformer, projection, query embeddings, relation head and spline head remain frozen. All modules stay in eval mode; saved BN statistics and dropout behavior are fixed. This is a **node-head continuation pilot**, not full-network retraining. The zero-image arm controls for adding a token/coordinate-conditioned MLP; image-input weights are inactive when inputs are zero.

Same full IXI training membership, deterministic loader seed, batch size **32**, constant AdamW LR **7e-5**, **1,000 updates**. Weight decay/betas/epsilon inherited from checkpoint configuration. No augmentation for this isolation pilot; this is an explicit choice shared by all arms, not a proposed final training policy. Existing classification/node objectives and Hungarian matcher are preserved. Spline loss weight is zero because its head/inputs were detached and frozen; this avoids computing a constant geometry objective. Other existing losses remain configured; frozen token/relation parameters cannot update.

128 training / 128 disjoint-subject validation patches selected by the diagnostic's deterministic subject-round-robin rule, independent of results. Monitor at updates 0, 500, 1000; training-set evaluation at 0/1000. No test set, early stopping, or best-step cherry-picking. Compare the fixed final step, with intermediate trajectory available.

## Minimal model change

Optional `model.node_refinement` in RelationFormer; disabled by default. Checkpoint-compatible for existing configurations.

- Reuses the early `layer0.relu1` feature map, before max-pooling, 64 channels at 32³.
- Samples 27 positions on a 3×3×3 lattice around each predicted node, offsets −4, 0, +4 **input voxels** per axis. This radius is an exploratory engineering choice, not a physical-mm threshold.
- Sampling follows the actual early convolution grid: feature index `i` is centred at input voxel `2*i` for kernel7/stride2/padding3. Uses W,H,D order for `grid_sample`; node arrays are D,H,W with `index/shape` normalization.
- Detached sampling centres and frozen feature map avoid changing upstream localization through spatial-sampling gradients.
- Concatenates samples, object token and detached proposed coordinates; one 128-wide hidden layer emits three coordinate corrections and two class-logit corrections.
- Coordinate correction bounded by tanh to ±4 voxels **per axis**, then clamped to existing normalized output range [0,1]. Box-size coordinates are unchanged. Total displacement can exceed four voxels in Euclidean norm; existing coordinate heads can also move base proposals further.
- Last layer initialized to zero: exact identity for node positions and logits at initialization, verified on the real model in smoke.

This cannot guarantee recovering missing junctions or endpoints beyond the local sampling region. Good results would support access to local image evidence; bad results would not rule out a higher-resolution or multiscale transformer.

## Correctness and reporting

CPU check passed: identity initialization, trainable-head gradients, per-axis displacement bounds, zero-image invariance. Syntax and Slurm shell checks passed.

GPU smoke runs all three arms sequentially, three updates each, with initial/final graph metrics and plots. Checks finite gradients, new-head gradient presence, absent gradients in frozen parameters, unchanged frozen-state hashes, unchanged transformer tokens, and identity predictions before updates. Full array starts only after all smoke arms succeed.

Full metrics: existing node/edge F1; common curve/branch metrics; same-endpoint chords; 1/2 mm node precision/recall, endpoint-pair recovery and conditional relation recall; boundary/junction/termination localization counts. Changing node confidence affects selected edges even though relation weights stay fixed. This is **not a relation-head-learning experiment**.

Collector verifies identical initial validation metrics and training-batch hashes before emitting comparison tables. Inspect node precision and duplicates alongside recall: accepting more nodes alone is not sufficient. Attribute an image-evidence benefit only if `local_image` improves over both baseline and zero-image on validation, with training/validation behavior and geometry considered.

## Jobs and artifacts

- Smoke **1264051**, 30-minute limit.
- Pilot array **1264054**, tasks 0–2 above, `afterok:1264051`; each requests one H100 independently, 2-hour limit.
- CPU collector **1264058**, `afterok:1264054`.

Configuration: `configs/ixi_node_refinement.yaml`.

Full output: `/lustre/fsn1/projects/rech/vnc/upz25mj/experiments/gnbm/spline_learning/ixi_node_refinement_20261018/{baseline,local_image,zero_image}`. Includes predictions, node subtype summaries, fixed-example PNGs, scalar histories and W&B offline runs. Only updated parameters are saved as `trained-heads.pt`; reconstruct by loading the recorded parent checkpoint then overlaying these named parameters. No duplicate full detector checkpoints are stored.

Comparison: `docs/research/evidence/ixi_node_refinement_20261018/{comparison.md,comparison.csv,summary.json}`, generated after completion. Full validation metrics here use the fixed 128-patch diagnostic subset, not all IXI validation patches.

Logs: `experiments/spline_learning/logs/ixi-node-refine-*` and `ixi-node-table-*`. Submission manifest: `experiments/ixi_node_refinement/submission.json`.

Implementations: `models/node_refinement.py`, opt-in integration in `models/relationformer.py`, `scripts/train_ixi_node_refinement.py`, `scripts/collect_ixi_node_refinement.py` and two Slurm wrappers. Shared node-accounting helper now tolerates empty decoded predictions (no nearest-query distance available).


## Smoke completion

All three arms completed their three GPU updates, metrics and image export successfully. The collector passed on the smoke artifacts: batch-order hashes and initial validation scores agree exactly. Frozen parameters/buffers remained unchanged, active heads had finite gradients, and the new head began as the identity. A local-image smoke validation projection was visually inspected. These checks establish execution correctness only; three-update scores are not evidence of benefit. Compact checks: `experiments/ixi_node_refinement/smoke-checks.json`.


## Completed results — reviewed 2026-10-19

All jobs exited 0: baseline 6m36s, local_image 6m40s, zero_image 6m10s; collector 2s. Same initial scores and training-batch hashes verified; frozen parameters/buffers unchanged. Results below are on the fixed 128 validation patches, one seed, final update 1000 (not the held-out test set).

| Arm | Node recall 2mm | Node precision 2mm | Native node F1 | Native edge F1 | Common curve F1 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Baseline continuation |0.5112|0.4701|0.4857|0.1553|0.1171|
| Local image refinement |**0.5627**|**0.5171**|**0.5196**|**0.1673**|**0.1676**|
| Zero-image control |0.5115|0.4702|0.4829|0.1538|0.1164|

Native F1 uses its original benchmark matching; do not derive it directly from the separate position-only 2mm precision/recall columns.

### Interpretation

Local image evidence helps beyond simply adding an MLP: node precision and recall both improve, while the zero-image control stays near baseline. This is evidence for the proposed direction in this pilot, not multi-seed/test-set proof or proof that the 2³ grid alone caused the original problem. The intervention changes coordinate and confidence prediction jointly; their individual contributions remain unisolated.

Relative to baseline, local refinement adds 0.0339 node F1, 0.0120 edge F1, and 0.0505 curve F1. Validation curve F1 rises from 0.1169 initially to 0.1622 at 500 updates and 0.1676 at 1000. Training curve F1 rises from 0.1366 to 0.1882; improvement is not restricted to training patches.

At 2mm, recoverable endpoint pairs increase from 30.20% (baseline final) to 37.96% (local final), but conditional direct relation recall is essentially unchanged: 12.35% versus 12.48%. This supports improved localization/endpoint recovery, not improved relation-head learning (that head was frozen). Conditional populations differ between arms, so this is not a causal relation comparison.

Junction recall improves from 592/1199 (49.37%) to 698/1199 (58.22%); boundary recall from 884/1400 (63.14%) to 946/1400 (67.57%). Interior termination recall remains low: 321/916 (35.04%) versus 334/916 (36.46%). No claim that all node types are solved.

Same-endpoint straight-chord curve F1 improves from 0.1134 to 0.1641, close to the spline gain (0.1171→0.1676). Most geometric improvement therefore appears attributable to corrected endpoints, not extra learned curvature; the spline head was frozen.

### Visual inspection and evidence

Inspected the fixed sample `sample_000040_0078` baseline/local final projection panels directly. Node positions move toward some visible branches, but misplaced points, missing branches and incorrect connections remain. Projection crossings cannot establish anatomical topology. Panels copied to the evidence folder; no favorable example search was performed.

[Comparison table and CSV](../evidence/ixi_node_refinement_20261018/comparison.md), `comparison.csv`, and all-arm `summary.json` preserve results. Fixed-example images: `baseline-sample_000040_0078.png`, `local_image-sample_000040_0078.png` in the same folder. Original predictions and other fixed examples remain in the run directories.

### Next decision (not launched)

Retain local image refinement as a promising node-localization option. Next isolate relations using recovered/GT endpoint pairs, because connectivity remains poor even when endpoints are available. A controlled longer node-refinement continuation can assess stability, but should preserve both controls and validation-based decisions. Do not claim improved curvature or schedule a full training based only on this pilot.


## Image inspection: method and observed examples

Use the same fixed validation patch and final update for each arm. The six-panel renderer shows maximum-intensity projections along D/H/W: the top row overlays original GT paths and nodes in orange, and the bottom overlays decoded predicted curves/nodes in cyan. This permits direct visual comparison of displacement, omitted structures and spurious connections on the same input. Projections preserve bright structures across depth, so apparent crossings require slice-level confirmation.

For `sample_000040_0078` at update1000, the local-image variant shifts several nodes/segments toward the bright vessel compared with the baseline; isolated nodes and incorrect small connections remain. The annotated images are preserved as `baseline-sample_000040_0078.png` and `local_image-sample_000040_0078.png` beside the comparison table. Aggregate positional matching shows improved node precision/recall, while conditional relation recall stays nearly constant. Thus the image comparison and metrics support better endpoint placement while identifying connectivity as unresolved.
